knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Expectation Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical single-stage DRO objective over a nonempty ambiguity set of probability laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty decision set, let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space, and let \(\mathcal P\) be a nonempty set of probability measures on it. For a measurable loss \(\ell:X\times\Xi\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), assume \(\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\) is well-defined for every \((x,P)\in X\times\mathcal P\). The worst-case expected loss is \(\Phi(x):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\), and the associated distributionally robust optimization problem is \[\inf_{x\in X}\Phi(x)=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DRO chooses a feasible decision minimizing expected loss under the most adverse probability distribution in a specified ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell(x,\cdot)\) is measurable and has a well-defined expectation under every \(P\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\)

notation.meaning: Loss incurred by decision x under outcome xi.

review_flags: Exact DRO source locator not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation is standard, but no inspectable DRO source is cited. The plain statement also says a decision is chosen, although the displayed infimum need not be attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Risk Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DRO model allowing a distribution-dependent risk functional beyond ordinary expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty decision set, \(\mathcal P\) a nonempty ambiguity set on \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\), and \(L_x:=\ell(x,\xi)\) the loss induced by \(x\in X\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P\), let \(\rho_P\) be a risk functional defined on a linear space containing \(L_x\) for all \(x\). Define \(R(x):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\rho_P(L_x)\). The worst-case risk model is \[\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\rho_P\bigl(\ell(x,\xi)\bigr).\] Choosing \(\rho_P(L)=\mathbb E_P[L]\) recovers the worst-case expectation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decision minimizes the largest distribution-specific risk value over all distributions in the ambiguity set; expectation is one special risk functional.
assumptions_latex: Each loss \(L_x\) belongs to the domain of every \(\rho_P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\rho_P(L_x)\)

notation.meaning: Random loss generated by decision x.
Risk functional evaluated under distribution P.

review_flags: A source supporting the distribution-dependent risk formulation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The model fits the leaf, but the distribution-indexed risk-functional formulation and its domain assumptions require an authoritative source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Nature's Distributional Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner adversarial optimization for a fixed decision in the worst-case expectation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\in X\) in a worst-case expectation model with ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\). Nature's distributional subproblem is \[\Phi(x):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\int_{\Xi}\ell(x,\xi)\,P(d\xi).\] Its value is the worst-case expected loss at \(x\). If the supremum is attained, any \(P_x^\star\in\mathcal P\) satisfying \(\mathbb E_{P_x^\star}[\ell(x,\xi)]=\Phi(x)\) is a worst-case distribution. If it is not attained, a sequence \((P_k)\subseteq\mathcal P\) with \(\mathbb E_{P_k}[\ell(x,\xi)]\to\Phi(x)\) is an optimizing sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the decision fixed, nature selects an admissible distribution maximizing expected loss; an optimizer or optimizing sequence describes the adverse law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \Phi(x)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\)

notation.meaning: Worst-case distribution for the fixed decision x.

review_flags: Exact source for the DRO inner problem was not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inner adversarial problem matches the target context and is mathematically plausible, but no source or locator supports the formulation and optimizing-sequence statement.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic–Robust Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested ambiguity sets interpolate between a nominal stochastic model and support-wise robust optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty decision set, let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space, and let \(\widehat P\) be a probability measure on it. Let \((\mathcal P_\theta)_{\theta\in[0,1]}\) be nonempty sets of probability measures on \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) such that \(\mathcal P_0=\{\widehat P\}\), \(\mathcal P_{\theta_1}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\theta_2}\) whenever \(\theta_1\leq\theta_2\), and \(\mathcal P_1=\mathcal M(\Xi,\mathcal F)\), where \(\mathcal M(\Xi,\mathcal F)\) is the set of all probability measures on \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\). Let \(\ell:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\) be measurable in its second argument and bounded above there for each \(x\in X\). Then \(\Phi_\theta(x):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\theta}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\) is nondecreasing in \(\theta\), and \[\Phi_0(x)=\mathbb E_{\widehat P}[\ell(x,\xi)],\qquad \Phi_1(x)=\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}\ell(x,\xi).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each feasible decision, expanding the ambiguity set cannot decrease worst-case expected loss. A singleton nominal distribution yields nominal stochastic optimization, while the set of all probability laws yields support-wise robust optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) is a measurable space.
\(\mathcal P_0=\{\widehat P\}\), the ambiguity sets are nested in \(\theta\), and \(\mathcal P_1=\mathcal M(\Xi,\mathcal F)\).
For every \(x\in X\), \(\ell(x,\cdot)\) is measurable and bounded above on \(\Xi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_0(x)\leq\Phi_\theta(x)\leq\Phi_1(x)=\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}\ell(x,\xi)\)

notation.meaning: All probability measures on the measurable space.
Worst-case expected loss at decision x and ambiguity level theta.

children.title: Ambiguity-Aversion Preferences
children.top_down_role: Preference attitudes toward uncertainty over probability laws.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguity-Aversion Preferences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixture-space uncertainty-aversion axiom for preferences over acts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a convex mixture space of acts and let \(\succeq\) be a preference relation on \(\mathcal A\), with \(f\sim g\) meaning both \(f\succeq g\) and \(g\succeq f\). The preference is ambiguity averse if, for every \(f,g\in\mathcal A\) and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \[f\sim g\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \alpha f+(1-\alpha)g\succeq f.\] Thus, when two acts are indifferent, every mixture of them is weakly preferred to either endpoint; equivalently, every upper contour set \(\{f\in\mathcal A:f\succeq h\}\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ambiguity aversion means that mixing two indifferent acts cannot make the decision maker worse off; equivalently, upper preference sets are convex.
assumptions_latex: \(\succeq\) is a preference relation and \(\sim\) is its symmetric part.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\sim g\Rightarrow \alpha f+(1-\alpha)g\succeq f\)

notation.meaning: Indifference relation induced by weak preference.

review_flags: The supplied sources do not cover the ambiguity-aversion axiom.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ambiguity-aversion axiom fits the leaf, but the asserted equivalence with convex upper contour sets requires additional preference assumptions or a source establishing the exact formulation.

children.title: Maxmin Expected Utility
children.top_down_role: Utility evaluation under the least favorable probability law.

knowledge_statements.title: Maxmin Expected Utility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple-prior utility representation on a measurable state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable state space, let \(C\) be a convex set of probability measures on it, and let \(u\) be a real-valued utility index. For every act \(f\) such that \(u\circ f\) is integrable under each \(P\in C\), define \[V(f):=\inf_{P\in C}\mathbb E_P[u(f)].\] The maxmin expected-utility preference represented by \((u,C)\) is \[f\succeq g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad V(f)\geq V(g).\] The decision maker therefore evaluates each act by its least expected utility across the admissible priors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An act is preferred exactly when its lowest expected utility over the admissible prior set is at least as large as that of another act.
assumptions_latex: \(C\neq\varnothing\) is a convex set of probability measures.
\(u\circ f\) and \(u\circ g\) are integrable under every \(P\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle f\succeq g\Longleftrightarrow \inf_{P\in C}\mathbb E_P[u(f)]\geq\inf_{P\in C}\mathbb E_P[u(g)]\)
review_flags: A source for the multiple-priors representation is required.
This record defines the representation and does not assert its axiomatic characterization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiple-prior representation fits the leaf, but no source is supplied, and the consequence space and domain of the utility index are not introduced precisely.

children.title: Preference–DRO Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Links between ambiguity-sensitive preferences and distributionally robust objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Preference–DRO Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-change equivalence between maxmin utility choice and worst-case-loss DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a feasible decision set, let \(C\) be a nonempty set of probability measures, and let each \(x\in X\) induce an act \(f_x\). Set \(\ell(x,\omega):=-u(f_x(\omega))\), assuming all expectations are finite. Then \[\sup_{x\in X}\inf_{P\in C}\mathbb E_P[u(f_x)]=-\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in C}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\omega)].\] Moreover, \(x^\star\) maximizes maxmin expected utility if and only if it minimizes the corresponding DRO worst-case expected loss. The prior set \(C\) serves as the DRO ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating utility converts maxmin expected-utility choice into worst-case expected-loss minimization, with the multiple-prior set becoming the DRO ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: All displayed expectations and optimization values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\inf_{P\in C}\mathbb E_P[u(f_x)]=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in C}\mathbb E_P[-u(f_x)]\)

notation.meaning: Prior set and corresponding DRO ambiguity set.

review_flags: Exact source for the preference–DRO correspondence was not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sign-change correspondence is algebraically plausible, but it lacks a source. Calling it duality may overstate a direct objective transformation; a sourced record should justify that kind or use property/representation as appropriate.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Envelope Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coherent risk as worst-case expectation over an envelope of probability densities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,P_0)\) be a probability space and let \(L\) be an integrable loss. Suppose a coherent risk functional \(\rho\) admits a nonempty risk envelope \(\mathcal Q\) of densities satisfying \(q\geq0\) and \(\mathbb E_{P_0}[q]=1\). Its envelope representation is \[\rho(L)=\sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb E_{P_0}[qL]=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal Q}}\mathbb E_P[L],\] where \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal Q}:=\{P:q=dP/dP_0\in\mathcal Q\}\). Consequently, minimizing \(\rho(\ell(x,\xi))\) is a worst-case-expectation DRO problem over \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal Q}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coherently risk-averse objective becomes a DRO objective when its dual density envelope is interpreted as an ambiguity set of probability distributions.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is integrable under every measure induced by \(\mathcal Q\).
\(\rho\) is coherent and possesses the stated envelope representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \rho(L)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal Q}}\mathbb E_P[L]\)

notation.meaning: Ambiguity set induced by the risk envelope.

review_flags: A coherent-risk duality source with precise function-space hypotheses is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The risk-envelope interface and duality kind fit the leaf, but coherent-risk envelope representations depend on precise function-space and regularity hypotheses that are not sourced here.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust-Statistics Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributionally robust estimation obtained by minimizing worst-case statistical risk near an empirical law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be observations on \(\mathcal Z\), let \(\widehat P_n:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{Z_i}\), and let \(d\) be a discrepancy between probability measures. For radius \(\varepsilon\geq0\), define \(\mathcal P_{n,\varepsilon}:=\{P:d(P,\widehat P_n)\leq\varepsilon\}\). Given a parameter space \(\Theta\) and measurable loss \(L:\Theta\times\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), a distributionally robust estimator satisfies \[\widehat\theta_{n,\varepsilon}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,\varepsilon}}\mathbb E_P[L(\theta,Z)].\] Thus statistical robustness is encoded by guarding empirical risk against nearby distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust estimator minimizes the largest expected statistical loss over distributions lying within a prescribed discrepancy radius of the empirical distribution.
assumptions_latex: The expectations are well-defined and the displayed argmin is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \widehat\theta_{n,\varepsilon}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_{d(P,\widehat P_n)\leq\varepsilon}\mathbb E_P[L(\theta,Z)]\)
review_flags: The supplied inventory lacks a robust-statistics or data-driven DRO source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation fits the robust-statistics interface, but no data-driven DRO or robust-statistics source is supplied, and the required properties of the discrepancy and ambiguity set are unspecified.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Support Gives Weak Compactness and Dirac Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence regime for support-only worst-case expectations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \Xi is Polish and S\subseteq\Xi is nonempty and compact, then \mathcal P_S is weakly compact. For every upper-semicontinuous h:S\to\mathbb R bounded above, there exists x^\star\in S such that \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_S}\mathbb E_P[h]=h(x^\star)=\mathbb E_{\delta_{x^\star}}[h].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact support makes the ambiguity set weakly compact and lets a Dirac law attain each bounded upper-semicontinuous worst-case payoff.
assumptions_latex: h\text{ is upper semicontinuous and bounded above on }S.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_S\text{ is weakly compact, and the supremum is attained by }\delta_{x^\star}.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Support Gives Weak Compactness and Dirac Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Worst-Case Law Need Not Exist on Noncompact Support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment failure despite a finite support-wise supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S=(0,1) and h(x)=x. Then \sup_{P:P(S)=1}\mathbb E_P[X]=1, but every such law satisfies \mathbb E_P[X]<1; hence no worst-case distribution exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a noncompact support, the support-wise supremum can be finite but unattained by every admissible law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{(0,1)}}\mathbb E_P[X]=1\text{ and the supremum is not attained}.
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Law Need Not Exist on Noncompact Support
Support-Only Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity set containing every probability law concentrated on a prescribed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space and let \(S\in\mathcal F\) be nonempty. The support-only ambiguity set associated with \(S\) is \[\mathcal P_S:=\{P\in\mathcal M(\Xi):P(S)=1\}.\] It imposes no moment, divergence, or shape restrictions beyond concentration on \(S\). For every measurable function \(h:\Xi\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) bounded above on \(S\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_S}\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]=\sup_{\xi\in S}h(\xi),\] because \(\mathcal P_S\) contains every Dirac measure \(\delta_\xi\) with \(\xi\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support-only ambiguity permits every probability distribution concentrated on a given set, so its worst-case expectation equals the pointwise supremum over that support.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is measurable and bounded above on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \mathcal P_S=\{P:P(S)=1\},\qquad \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_S}\mathbb E_P[h]=\sup_{\xi\in S}h(\xi)\)

notation.meaning: Probability measures on the measurable space.

review_flags: No moment-problem or DRO ambiguity-set source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and worst-case-expectation identity fit support-only ambiguity, but the record has no inspectable source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected as proposed because its assumptions do not justify the asserted extreme-point characterization on a general measurable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \operatorname{ext}(\mathcal P_S)=\{\delta_x:x\in S\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity is valid generally, but the claim that all extreme probability laws are Dirac measures can fail on insufficiently separating measurable spaces; the proposed assumption is not precise enough.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chebyshev System on the Nonnegative Half-Line
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of the finite-interval Chebyshev-system definition to an unbounded interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A system $(u_0,\ldots,u_m)$ is a Chebyshev system (respectively, a positive Chebyshev system) on $[0,\infty)$ if it is a Chebyshev system (respectively, a positive Chebyshev system) on every finite closed subinterval of $[0,\infty)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function system is a Chebyshev system, or positive Chebyshev system, on the nonnegative half-line exactly when it has the corresponding property on every finite closed subinterval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (u_0,\ldots,u_m)\text{ has the stated Chebyshev property on }[0,\infty)\iff\forall\,0\leq c<d<\infty,\ (u_0,\ldots,u_m)\text{ has it on }[c,d].

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient endpoint-localizing Hankel conditions for an odd-order power-moment sequence on a bounded interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\) be odd and \(\mu_0=1,\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m\) be real numbers. The sequence is the power-moment sequence of a probability distribution supported on \([a,b]\) if and only if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^{(m+1)/2}\), \[\sum_{i,j=0}^{(m-1)/2}(\mu_{i+j+1}-a\mu_{i+j})x_ix_j\ge0\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_{i,j=0}^{(m-1)/2}(b\mu_{i+j}-\mu_{i+j+1})x_ix_j\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For odd truncation order, a normalized sequence is realizable as the power moments of a probability distribution on [a,b] exactly when both endpoint-localizing Hankel forms are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mu_k)_{k=0}^m\text{ is a power-moment sequence on }[a,b]\iff \sum_{i,j=0}^{(m-1)/2}(\mu_{i+j+1}-a\mu_{i+j})x_ix_j\ge0\text{ and }\sum_{i,j=0}^{(m-1)/2}(b\mu_{i+j}-\mu_{i+j+1})x_ix_j\ge0\quad\forall x\in\mathbb R^{(m+1)/2}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Type I and Type II Chebyshev Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by limiting determinants or dominant-function asymptotics on $[0,\infty)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Chebyshev system $(u_0,\ldots,u_m)$ on $[0,\infty)$ is of Type I if (i) every $u_i(\infty):=\lim_{z\to\infty}u_i(z)$ exists and (ii), for every $0\le z_0<\cdots<z_{m-1}$, $\det\!\begin{pmatrix}u_0(z_0)&\cdots&u_0(z_{m-1})&u_0(\infty)\\ \vdots&&\vdots&\vdots\\ u_m(z_0)&\cdots&u_m(z_{m-1})&u_m(\infty)\end{pmatrix}>0$. A positive Chebyshev system $(u_0,\ldots,u_m)$ on $[0,\infty)$ is of Type II if (i) $u_m(z)>0$ for all $z\ge A$ for some $A$, (ii) $\lim_{z\to\infty}u_i(z)/u_m(z)=0$ for $0\le i<m$, and (iii) $(u_0,\ldots,u_{m-1})$ is also a positive Chebyshev system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type I systems have finite limits at infinity and a strictly positive determinant after adjoining the limiting evaluation column. Type II positive systems have an eventually positive final function that asymptotically dominates every earlier function, and the truncated system remains positive Chebyshev.
assumptions_latex: (u_0,\ldots,u_m)\text{ is a Chebyshev system on }[0,\infty)\text{ for Type I.}
(u_0,\ldots,u_m)\text{ is a positive Chebyshev system on }[0,\infty)\text{ for Type II.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated conditions define Chebyshev systems of Type I and Type II, respectively.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Alternating determinant sign for discrete moment columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign regularity of augmented ordered columns from power- or binomial-moment constraint matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let z_0<\cdots<z_n, let 1\le t\le m+1, and let 1\le i_1<\cdots<i_t<\cdots<i_{m+2}\le n. Suppose either a_i=(1,z_i,z_i^2,\ldots,z_i^m)^\top for every selected index, or a_i=(\binom{z_i}{0},\binom{z_i}{1},\ldots,\binom{z_i}{m})^\top for every selected index. Then
\[
(-1)^t\det\begin{pmatrix}0&\cdots&0&1&\cdots&1\\a_{i_1}&\cdots&a_{i_t}&a_{i_{t+1}}&\cdots&a_{i_{m+2}}\end{pmatrix}>0,
\]
where the first t entries of the appended row are zero and the remaining m+2-t entries are one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an ordered selection of m+2 columns from either a power-moment system or a binomial-moment system, augmenting the columns by a row with t leading zeros and then ones gives a determinant whose sign is (-1)^t.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (-1)^t\det\begin{pmatrix}0&\cdots&0&1&\cdots&1\\a_{i_1}&\cdots&a_{i_t}&a_{i_{t+1}}&\cdots&a_{i_{m+2}}\end{pmatrix}>0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient Hankel-form conditions for a finite power-moment sequence of a probability distribution supported on a bounded interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\) be even and \(\mu_0=1,\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m\) be real numbers. The sequence is the power-moment sequence of a probability distribution supported on \([a,b]\) if and only if the quadratic forms \[\sum_{i,j=0}^{m/2}\mu_{i+j}x_ix_j\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_{i,j=0}^{m/2-1}\bigl((a+b)\mu_{i+j+1}-ab\mu_{i+j}-\mu_{i+j+2}\bigr)x_ix_j\] are nonnegative for all vectors \(x\) of their respective dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For even truncation order, a normalized sequence is realizable as the power moments of a probability distribution on [a,b] exactly when its moment Hankel form and interval-localizing Hankel form are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mu_k)_{k=0}^m\text{ is a power-moment sequence on }[a,b]\iff \sum_{i,j=0}^{m/2}\mu_{i+j}x_ix_j\ge0\text{ and }\sum_{i,j=0}^{m/2-1}\bigl((a+b)\mu_{i+j+1}-ab\mu_{i+j}-\mu_{i+j+2}\bigr)x_ix_j\ge0\text{ for all applicable }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extrema Are Attained by Principal Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extremal integral values under prescribed generalized moments on a compact interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Conditions 1a and 2 hold. For the problems $\min_P\int_a^b f(z)\,dP$ and $\max_P\int_a^b f(z)\,dP$ subject to $\int_a^b u_k(z)\,dP=\mu_k$ for $k=0,\ldots,m$, both extrema are attained. A minimizing $P$ corresponds to a lower principal representation, and a maximizing $P$ corresponds to an upper principal representation. A representation that is not principal does not correspond to an extremal $P$ in either problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Conditions 1a and 2, the minimum and maximum expected values of f over measures having the prescribed generalized moments are attained. Minimizers and maximizers correspond respectively to lower and upper principal representations, while nonprincipal representations are not extremal for either problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_P\int_a^b f\,dP\text{ and }\max_P\int_a^b f\,dP\text{ are attained by lower and upper principal representations, respectively, and no nonprincipal representation is extremal.}

children.title: Mean-Constrained Ambiguity Sets
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity sets specified through mean information.

knowledge_statements.title: Mean-Constrained Ambiguity Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability laws whose mean belongs to a prescribed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable subset of \(\mathbb R^d\), and let \(M\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty. The mean-constrained ambiguity set is \[\mathcal P_M:=\left\{P\in\mathcal M(\Xi):\int_{\Xi}\|\xi\|\,P(d\xi)<\infty,\ \int_{\Xi}\xi\,P(d\xi)\in M\right\}.\] If \(M=\{\mu\}\), this is an exact-mean ambiguity set. If \(M\) is described by componentwise bounds \(\underline\mu\leq m\leq\overline\mu\), the definition permits any distribution whose finite mean lies within those bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mean-constrained ambiguity set contains all distributions with finite first moment whose mean lies in a specified set, including exact and interval-valued means.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \mathcal P_M=\left\{P\in\mathcal M(\Xi):\mathbb E_P[\|\xi\|]<\infty,\ \mathbb E_P[\xi]\in M\right\}\)
review_flags: No classical moment-set source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but no moment-set source is cited. The phrase that a measurable space is a measurable subset of Euclidean space should also be replaced by an explicit measurable subset with its sigma-algebra.

children.title: Support-Constrained Ambiguity Sets
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity sets restricted by known distributional support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Weak Compactness of the Support-Only Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic topological structure of all probability laws concentrated on a compact support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The support-only family \(\mathcal P_S\) is convex. If the ambient space is metric and \(S\) is nonempty and compact, then \(\mathcal P_S\) is weakly compact. Consequently, every bounded upper-semicontinuous loss attains its worst-case expectation over \(\mathcal P_S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support-only ambiguity sets are convex and are weakly compact on compact support, yielding worst-case attainment for bounded upper-semicontinuous losses.
assumptions_latex: For compactness, the ambient space is metric and \(S\) is compact.
For attainment, the loss is bounded and upper semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_S\text{ is convex, and compact }S\implies\mathcal P_S\text{ is weakly compact}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Weak Compactness of the Support-Only Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction to pointwise robust optimization for a bounded-above measurable loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\ne\varnothing\) be measurable and let \(\ell:S\to[-\infty,\infty)\) be measurable and bounded above. Then \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_S}\int\ell(\xi)\,P(d\xi)=\sup_{\xi\in S}\ell(\xi).\] If \(\xi^\star\in S\) attains the pointwise supremum, \(\delta_{\xi^\star}\) is a worst-case law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With no information beyond support, worst-case expected loss equals the pointwise worst loss on that support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_S}\mathbb E_P[\ell]=\sup_{\xi\in S}\ell(\xi).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Only Worst-Case Expectation
Support-Constrained Ambiguity Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability laws required to concentrate on a prescribed measurable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space and let \(S\in\mathcal F\) be nonempty. A support-constrained ambiguity set is any family \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal M(\Xi)\) satisfying \[P(S)=1\qquad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal P.\] Equivalently, \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal P_S\), where \(\mathcal P_S:=\{P\in\mathcal M(\Xi):P(S)=1\}\). Additional moment, distance, or shape restrictions may further reduce \(\mathcal P\); when none are imposed, the family equals the support-only ambiguity set \(\mathcal P_S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support-constrained ambiguity set contains only distributions concentrated on a prescribed measurable set; other information may impose additional restrictions within that family.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a family of probability measures on \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal P_S=\{P\in\mathcal M(\Xi):P(S)=1\}\)

notation.meaning: All probability laws concentrated on S.
Support-constrained ambiguity set, possibly with additional restrictions.

review_flags: No classical support-constrained moment-set source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes a general support-constrained family from the maximal support-only family, but no classical moment-set or DRO source locator is supplied.

children.title: Joint Mean–Support Geometry
children.top_down_role: Structural interaction between mean restrictions and support restrictions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact-Support Mean Feasibility and Carathéodory Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite certificate for joint mean and compact-support feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty and compact, the attainable means of laws supported on \(\Xi\) are exactly \(\operatorname{conv}(\Xi)\). Hence \[\mathcal P_{\Xi,M}\ne\varnothing\iff M\cap\operatorname{conv}(\Xi)\ne\varnothing.\] Whenever feasible, a representing law supported on at most \(d+1\) points of \(\Xi\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compact support, joint feasibility is exactly convex-hull intersection, with a certificate using at most d+1 atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\Xi,M}\ne\varnothing\iff M\cap\operatorname{conv}(\Xi)\ne\varnothing.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Support Mean Feasibility and Carathéodory Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Convex-Hull Membership Need Not Ensure Attainability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for nonclosed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Xi=(0,1)\) and \(M=\{0\}\). Then \(0\in M\cap\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\Xi)\), but every law supported on \((0,1)\) has strictly positive mean. Thus \(\mathcal P_{\Xi,M}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonclosed support, a boundary point of the closed convex hull need not be an attainable mean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\cap\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\Xi)\ne\varnothing\) but \(\mathcal P_{\Xi,M}=\varnothing.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex-Hull Membership Need Not Ensure Attainability
Joint Mean–Support Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barycentric geometry of distributions constrained jointly by support and mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be Borel and let \(M\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). The joint mean–support ambiguity set is
\[\mathcal P_{\Xi,M}:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d):P(\Xi)=1,\ \int_{\Xi}\|\xi\|\,P(d\xi)<\infty,\ \int_{\Xi}\xi\,P(d\xi)\in M\right\}.\]
Thus its feasible means are barycenters of probability measures supported on \(\Xi\). In particular, every feasible mean lies in \(M\cap\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\Xi)\); if \(m\in M\cap\operatorname{conv}(\Xi)\), then a finitely supported member with mean \(m\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family contains distributions supported on the prescribed set whose finite mean belongs to the prescribed mean region; feasible means obey the support’s convex geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\Xi,M}\) couples support feasibility with the barycenter constraint \(\mathbb E_P[\xi]\in M\).

notation.meaning: Borel probability measures on Euclidean space
Convex hull of the support set

children.title: Mean-Constrained Ambiguity Sets
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity sets governed by first-moment information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex Mean Regions Can Produce Nonconvex Ambiguity Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for convexity of an unrestricted-support mean-constrained ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Xi=\mathbb R\) and \(M=\{0,2\}\), \(\delta_0,\delta_2\in\mathcal P_M\), but \(\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12\delta_2\notin\mathcal P_M\) because its mean is \(1\notin M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex mean region can induce a nonconvex ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_M\text{ is not convex}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Mean Regions Can Produce Nonconvex Ambiguity Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Worst-Case Affine Expectation under Mean Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact affine-loss representation for unrestricted support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Xi=\mathbb R^d\), \(\varnothing\ne M\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), and \(\ell(\xi)=a^\top\xi+b\). Then, in the extended-real sense, \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_M}\mathbb E_P[\ell(\xi)]=b+\sup_{m\in M}a^\top m=b+\sigma_M(a).\] If the support function is attained at \(m^\star\in M\), then \(\delta_{m^\star}\) is worst-case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For unrestricted support, the worst-case affine expectation is the intercept plus the support function of the admissible mean region.
assumptions_latex: Admitted laws have finite first moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_M}\mathbb E_P[a^\top\xi+b]=b+\sigma_M(a).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Affine Expectation under Mean Uncertainty
Mean-Constrained Ambiguity Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity sets specified by an admissible region for the first moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a Borel support set \(\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and a nonempty mean region \(M\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), define
\[\mathcal P_M:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\int_{\Xi}\|\xi\|\,P(d\xi)<\infty,\ \mathbb E_P[\xi]\in M\right\}.\]
An equality-constrained mean set is obtained with \(M=\{\mu\}\). If \(M\) is convex, then \(\mathcal P_M\) is convex because the mean map \(P\mapsto\mathbb E_P[\xi]\) is affine under mixtures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mean-constrained ambiguity set contains probability laws with finite first moment whose mean lies in a specified region; convex mean regions yield convex ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_M\) exactly when \(P\) has finite first moment and \(\mathbb E_P[\xi]\in M\).

notation.meaning: Borel probability measures supported on the set

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and mean-constrained formulation fit the leaf, but the record supplies no citation or specific locator supporting the definition and convexity assertion.

children.title: Covariance-Constrained Ambiguity Sets
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity sets governed by covariance information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal tests independent of detailed nonzero support geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every covariance matrix is positive semidefinite, and \(\operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi)=0\) if and only if \(\xi=\mathbb E_P[\xi]\) almost surely. Hence an exact requirement \(\Sigma\notin\mathbb S_+^d\) is infeasible. With support \(\Xi\), zero covariance is feasible exactly when \(\Xi\ne\varnothing\); if the mean is additionally prescribed as \(\mu\), it is feasible exactly when \(\mu\in\Xi\), through \(P=\delta_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covariance must be positive semidefinite, while zero covariance forces a Dirac law and gives an exact elementary support test.
assumptions_latex: \(P(\Xi)=1\) when a support restriction is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi)\succeq0,\qquad\operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi)=0\iff P=\delta_{\mathbb E_P\xi}.
knowledge_statements.title: Basic Covariance Feasibility Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixture Formula and Convexity Boundary for Covariance Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of varying versus fixed means on covariance-set geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For laws \(P,Q\) with means \(\mu_P,\mu_Q\), covariances \(\Sigma_P,\Sigma_Q\), and \(R=\lambda P+(1-\lambda)Q\), \[\operatorname{Cov}_R(\xi)=\lambda\Sigma_P+(1-\lambda)\Sigma_Q+\lambda(1-\lambda)(\mu_P-\mu_Q)(\mu_P-\mu_Q)^\top.\] Exact covariance constraints therefore need not define a convex law family when means vary. If the mean is fixed at \(\mu\), covariance is the affine moment \(\mathbb E[(\xi-\mu)(\xi-\mu)^\top]\); an exact covariance constraint, or membership in a convex matrix region, then defines a convex law family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing different means adds a between-means term and can destroy exact-covariance feasibility; fixing the mean makes the centered second moment affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Cov}_{\lambda P+(1-\lambda)Q}=\lambda\Sigma_P+(1-\lambda)\Sigma_Q+\lambda(1-\lambda)(\mu_P-\mu_Q)(\mu_P-\mu_Q)^\top.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixture Formula and Convexity Boundary for Covariance Constraints
Covariance-Constrained Ambiguity Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity sets restricting the centered second-moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be Borel and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb S_+^d\) be an admissible covariance region. Define
\[\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\mathbb E_P[\|\xi\|^2]<\infty,\ \operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi)\in\mathcal C\right\},\]
where
\[\operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi):=\mathbb E_P\!\left[(\xi-\mathbb E_P[\xi])(\xi-\mathbb E_P[\xi])^\top\right].\]
If a center \(\mu\) is prescribed separately, the corresponding raw constraint is \(\mathbb E_P[(\xi-\mu)(\xi-\mu)^\top]\in\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family contains finite-second-moment distributions whose covariance matrix lies in a prescribed positive-semidefinite matrix region, with a distinct formulation when the center is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}\) exactly when its centered second moment belongs to \(\mathcal C\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covariance-set definition fits the leaf, but it has no source. A source should also confirm the terminology: the matrix centered at a prescribed mean is not ordinarily called a raw moment constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Expectations Determined by Mean and Covariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation requiring both exact first and second moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathbb E_P[\xi]=\mu\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi)=\Sigma\), then \(\mathbb E_P[\xi^\top Q\xi+q^\top\xi+r]=\operatorname{tr}(Q\Sigma)+\mu^\top Q\mu+q^\top\mu+r\) for symmetric \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact mean and covariance determine every expected quadratic loss.
assumptions_latex: Both the mean and covariance are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E_P[\xi^\top Q\xi+q^\top\xi+r]=\operatorname{tr}(Q\Sigma)+\mu^\top Q\mu+q^\top\mu+r.
review_flags: Deferred as canonically dependent on joint exact mean–covariance information; covariance alone does not determine the displayed expectation.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Expectations Determined by Mean and Covariance

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is the covariance-set definition, its distinction from prescribed-center second moments, mixture geometry, and universal feasibility tests. Mean-only sets, joint mean–covariance compatibility, general conic moment duality, and quadratic evaluation requiring both exact moments are excluded; the latter proposed record is deferred.

children.title: Mean–Covariance Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Consistency and geometric interaction of prescribed mean and covariance information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional compatibility test for prescribed mean, covariance, and compact support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty and compact, set \(Q=\Sigma+\mu\mu^\top\), and define \(z(x)=(x,\operatorname{vech}(xx^\top))\). A law supported on \(S\) with mean \(\mu\) and covariance \(\Sigma\) exists if and only if \[(\mu,\operatorname{vech}Q)\in\operatorname{conv}(z(S)).\] When feasible, a representing law exists with at most \(1+d+d(d+1)/2\) atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On compact support, mean–covariance compatibility is exactly membership of the lifted moment vector in the convex hull of lifted support points, with a finite atomic certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists P:\operatorname{supp}P\subseteq S,\ \mathbb E_P[\xi]=\mu,\ \operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi)=\Sigma\iff(\mu,\operatorname{vech}Q)\in\operatorname{conv}(z(S)).\)

notation.meaning: Vectorization of the independent entries of a symmetric matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Support Lifted-Moment Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support geometry forced by covariance degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P\) has mean \(\mu\) and covariance \(\Sigma\succeq0\), then \[v\in\ker\Sigma\implies v^\top(\xi-\mu)=0\quad P\text{-a.s.}\] Hence \(P(\mu+\operatorname{range}\Sigma)=1\). In particular, \(\Sigma=0\) forces \(P=\delta_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular covariance confines every representing law to its associated affine subspace; zero covariance forces a point mass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(\mu+\operatorname{range}\Sigma)=1.\)

notation.meaning: Null space of the covariance matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Support Consequence of Singular Covariance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Mean–Variance Compatibility on an Interval
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar bounded-support compatibility criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a<b\), a probability law supported on \([a,b]\) with mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\sigma^2\) exists if and only if \[a\le\mu\le b,\qquad 0\le\sigma^2\le(b-\mu)(\mu-a).\] Every variance in this interval is realizable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an interval, the mean must lie between the endpoints and the variance must not exceed the sharp endpoint bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists P:\operatorname{supp}P\subseteq[a,b],\ \mathbb E_P[\xi]=\mu,\ \operatorname{Var}_P(\xi)=\sigma^2\iff a\le\mu\le b,\ 0\le\sigma^2\le(b-\mu)(\mu-a).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Mean–Variance Compatibility on an Interval
Mean–Covariance Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compatibility condition when no proper support restriction is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\mu\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^d\). On the unrestricted support \(\mathbb R^d\), there exists a probability measure \(P\) with finite second moment satisfying
\[\mathbb E_P[\xi]=\mu,\qquad \mathbb E_P[(\xi-\mu)(\xi-\mu)^\top]=\Sigma\]
if and only if \(\Sigma\succeq0\). Equivalently, the associated raw second moment \(Q=\Sigma+\mu\mu^\top\) satisfies
\[\begin{pmatrix}1&\mu^\top\\ \mu&Q\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\]
With a proper support set, positive semidefiniteness remains necessary but need not be sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without support restrictions, a mean and covariance are jointly realizable exactly when the covariance is positive semidefinite; restricted supports impose additional compatibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists P:\mathbb E_P[\xi]=\mu,\ \operatorname{Cov}_P(\xi)=\Sigma\iff\Sigma\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: The covariance matrix is positive semidefinite

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unrestricted-support compatibility condition and block-matrix equivalence are plausible and appropriately classified as a condition, but neither is supported by an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributionally robust portfolio VaR with exactly known first and second moments but otherwise unknown return distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be the class of all return distributions with mean \(\widehat r\) and covariance \(\Sigma\), and let \(\varrho(x)=r^\top x\). Define \(\mathbb P_{\rm wc}(-\varrho(x)\geq\zeta)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P(-\varrho(x)\geq\zeta)\). For \(\zeta+\widehat r^\top x>0\), \(\mathbb P_{\rm wc}(-\varrho(x)\geq\zeta)=\frac{\|\Sigma^{1/2}x\|_2^2}{\|\Sigma^{1/2}x\|_2^2+(\zeta+\widehat r^\top x)^2}\). Hence, for \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), \(\operatorname{wc\!\mbox{-}VaR}_\alpha(x)\leq\gamma\) if and only if \(\sqrt{(1-\alpha)/\alpha}\,\|\Sigma^{1/2}x\|_2\leq\widehat r^\top x+\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among all return distributions with a prescribed mean and covariance, the Chebyshev–Cantelli bound gives the exact worst-case upper-tail loss probability. For confidence levels below one half, a worst-case VaR limit is therefore equivalent to a second-order cone constraint whose multiplier is the square root of (1-alpha)/alpha.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{wc\!\mbox{-}VaR}_\alpha(x)\leq\gamma\iff\sqrt{\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}}\|\Sigma^{1/2}x\|_2\leq\widehat r^\top x+\gamma.

children.title: Uncertain Moment Sets
children.top_down_role: Moment ambiguity represented through general uncertainty regions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Compactness under Compact Continuous Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure and attainment regime for general uncertain moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\Xi\) is a compact metric space, \(h:\Xi\to\mathbb R^k\) is continuous, and \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) is closed. Then \(\mathcal P_{h,U}\) is weakly compact. If it is nonempty, every bounded upper-semicontinuous loss attains its worst-case expectation over \(\mathcal P_{h,U}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact support, continuous moment functions, and a closed region make the uncertain-moment set weakly compact and ensure worst-case attainment for bounded upper-semicontinuous losses.
assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set is nonempty for the attainment conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{h,U}\text{ is weakly compact}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Compactness under Compact Continuous Data

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact inverse-image representation and nonemptiness test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D_h\) be a specified class of laws under which every component of \(h\) is integrable, and define \(\mathcal A_h=\{\mathbb E_P[h]:P\in\mathcal D_h\}\). Then \[\mathcal P_{h,U}=\{P\in\mathcal D_h:\mathbb E_P[h]\in U\},\qquad \mathcal P_{h,U}\ne\varnothing\iff\mathcal A_h\cap U\ne\varnothing.\] If \(\mathcal D_h\) and \(U\) are convex, then \(\mathcal P_{h,U}\) is convex; if \(U_1\subseteq U_2\), then \(\mathcal P_{h,U_1}\subseteq\mathcal P_{h,U_2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncertain-moment set is the inverse image of its region under the moment map and is nonempty exactly when that region intersects the attainable moment set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D_h\) independently specifies laws with finite generalized moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{h,U}\ne\varnothing\iff\mathcal A_h\cap U\ne\varnothing.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Attainable-Moment Intersection Characterization
Uncertain Moment Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment ambiguity with the entire moment vector varying over an uncertainty region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Xi\) be a Borel space, let \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_k):\Xi\to\mathbb R^k\) be measurable, and let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) be nonempty. The uncertain-moment ambiguity set is
\[\mathcal P_{h,U}:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\mathbb E_P[|h_i(\xi)|]<\infty\ \text{for every }i,\ (\mathbb E_P[h_1(\xi)],\ldots,\mathbb E_P[h_k(\xi)])\in U\right\}.\]
The region \(U\) may encode uncertainty and dependence among several moments rather than fixing them individually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncertain-moment set contains distributions whose vector of integrable generalized moments lies in a prescribed uncertainty region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_{h,U}\iff\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]\in U\), subject to componentwise integrability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise Attainability Does Not Ensure Joint Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of checking interval restrictions separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Xi=\{-1,1\}\), \(h_1(\xi)=h_2(\xi)=\xi\), and impose \[-1\le\mathbb E_P[h_1]\le-\tfrac12,\qquad \tfrac12\le\mathbb E_P[h_2]\le1.\] Each interval is separately attainable, but no law satisfies both because \(\mathbb E_P[h_1]=\mathbb E_P[h_2]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each moment interval can be separately attainable even though their simultaneous interval-valued moment set is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{[\ell,u]}=\varnothing\) although each coordinate restriction is separately feasible.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties of componentwise moment bands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a convex domain of laws under which \(h_1,\ldots,h_k\) are integrable, \(\mathcal P_{[\ell,u]}\) is convex. If \(\ell'\le\ell\le u\le u'\) componentwise, then \[\mathcal P_{[\ell,u]}\subseteq\mathcal P_{[\ell',u']}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval-valued moment sets are convex, and widening their intervals enlarges the ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: The integrability domain of laws is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{[\ell,u]}\text{ is convex and }\mathcal P_{[\ell,u]}\subseteq\mathcal P_{[\ell',u']}.\)

Interval-Valued Moment Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise lower and upper bounds on generalized moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For measurable functions \(h_i:\Xi\to\mathbb R\) and bounds \(\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\ell_i\le u_i\), the interval-valued moment ambiguity set is
\[\mathcal P_{[\ell,u]}:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\mathbb E_P[|h_i(\xi)|]<\infty,\ \ell_i\le\mathbb E_P[h_i(\xi)]\le u_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,k)\right\}.\]
Equivalently, its moment vector belongs to the axis-aligned box \([\ell,u]=\prod_{i=1}^k[\ell_i,u_i]\). Equality moments arise when \(\ell_i=u_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These sets constrain each integrable generalized moment between specified lower and upper bounds, forming a box-shaped moment-uncertainty region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_{[\ell,u]}\iff\ell\le\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]\le u\) componentwise.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Interval Relaxation Can Destroy Moment Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict failure of replacing a coupled region by coordinate projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Xi=\{0,1\}^2\), \(h(\xi)=\xi\), and \[U=\{(m_1,m_2)\in[0,1]^2:m_1+m_2=1\}.\] Both coordinate projections of \(U\) equal \([0,1]\), so their product is \(B=[0,1]^2\supsetneq U\). The law \(\delta_{(0,0)}\) has moment vector \((0,0)\in B\setminus U\), and is therefore admitted by the interval relaxation but excluded by the coupled specification.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\subsetneq[0,1]^2\), and \(\delta_{(0,0)}\) is feasible only for the box relaxation.

Coupled Moment-Uncertainty Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonseparable uncertainty regions coupling multiple generalized moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\Xi\to\mathbb R^k\) be measurable and integrable under every admitted law, and let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) be a non-product uncertainty region. The coupled moment ambiguity set is
\[\mathcal P_U:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]\in U\right\}.\]
For example, a conic-affine region has the form
\[U=\{m\in\mathbb R^k:b-Am\in K\},\]
where \(K\) is a closed convex cone. Such a region expresses joint tradeoffs among moments that cannot generally be replaced by independent componentwise intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled moment set requires the entire moment vector to satisfy a joint, generally non-product region such as an affine conic constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\Xi\to\mathbb R^k\) is measurable and integrable under admitted laws.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_U\iff\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]\in U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized linear programming procedure for a generalized moment problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The pricing maximization must be solved globally; the source notes that it is generally nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with \(L\leq M+1\) feasible support points having linearly independent augmented moment vectors. At iteration \(j\), solve the restricted master problem over probabilities on the current support, then globally maximize \[\gamma(\xi,\sigma^j,\pi^j)=g(\xi)-\sigma^j-\sum_{i=1}^M\pi_i^jv_i(\xi).\] If its maximum is positive, add a maximizing support point and repeat. If its maximum is nonpositive, stop; the current support points and probabilities solve (5.27).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a restricted probability master problem, use its dual multipliers to price a new support point, and add that point when its reduced cost is positive. A globally nonpositive pricing maximum certifies optimality for the generalized moment problem.
assumptions_latex: \(L\leq M+1\) feasible initial support points have linearly independent augmented moment vectors
The restricted master problem is solved optimally at each iteration
The pricing problem \(\max_\xi\gamma(\xi,\sigma^j,\pi^j)\) is solved globally
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{\xi}\gamma(\xi,\sigma^j,\pi^j)\leq0\implies\text{the current discrete measure is optimal for (5.27)}\)

Expectation-Constraint Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized moment ambiguity expressed through expectation equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_i:\Xi\to\mathbb R\) be measurable and let \(I_=\) and \(I_\le\) be disjoint finite index sets. Given constants \(c_i\), define
\[\mathcal P_g:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\mathbb E_P[|g_i(\xi)|]<\infty,\ \mathbb E_P[g_i(\xi)]=c_i\ (i\in I_=),\ \mathbb E_P[g_i(\xi)]\le c_i\ (i\in I_\le)\right\}.\]
Because integration is affine in \(P\), this ambiguity set is convex whenever the integrability domain is closed under probability mixtures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expectation-constraint sets impose prescribed equalities or inequalities on expectations of measurable statistics; these constraints are affine in the probability law.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i:\Xi\to\mathbb R\) is measurable for every indexed constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_g\) is the family of laws satisfying all specified expectation equalities and inequalities.

Region-Probability Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity sets imposing probability bounds on measurable regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\Xi,\mathcal B)\) be a measurable space, let \(A_1,\ldots,A_k\in\mathcal B\), and choose bounds \(0\le\ell_i\le u_i\le1\). The region-probability ambiguity set is
\[\mathcal P_{A,\ell,u}:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\ell_i\le P(A_i)\le u_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,k)\right\}.\]
Equivalently, these are expectation constraints on indicator functions because \(P(A_i)=\mathbb E_P[\mathbf1_{A_i}(\xi)]\). Nonemptiness additionally requires the bounds to be compatible with normalization and all set relations among the regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region-probability set bounds the probability assigned to each specified measurable region and is equivalently an indicator-based expectation-constraint set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_{A,\ell,u}\iff\ell_i\le P(A_i)\le u_i\) for every \(i\).

Conic-Representable Statistical Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite statistical information encoded by affine membership in a convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\Xi\to\mathbb R^k\) be measurable, let \(A:\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb R^q\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a closed convex cone. Conic-representable statistical information defines
\[\mathcal P_{A,b,K}:=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\mathbb E_P[\|h(\xi)\|]<\infty,\ b-A\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]\in K\right\}.\]
Equivalently, introducing \(m=\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)]\), feasibility is represented by the linear moment equation and the finite-dimensional conic constraint \(b-Am\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Statistical information is conic-representable when the expected statistic vector satisfies an affine constraint in a closed convex cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_{A,b,K}\iff\exists m:\ m=\mathbb E_P[h(\xi)],\ b-Am\in K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fréchet–Hoeffding Bounds and the Higher-Dimensional Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp bivariate pointwise bounds for fixed marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every bivariate joint distribution function \(H\) with marginals \(F_1,F_2\) satisfies \[\max\{F_1(x)+F_2(y)-1,0\}\le H(x,y)\le\min\{F_1(x),F_2(y)\}.\] Both envelopes are joint distribution functions and are attainable in dimension two. For \(d\ge3\), \(\max\{\sum_iF_i(x_i)-d+1,0\}\) remains a pointwise lower bound but generally is not itself a joint distribution function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bivariate couplings have sharp upper and lower Fréchet envelopes; the analogous lower envelope generally fails to be a distribution in higher dimensions.

Fréchet Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint distributions with prescribed one-dimensional marginal laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_1,\ldots,F_d\) be probability distributions on \(\mathbb R\). Their Fréchet class is
\[\mathfrak F(F_1,\ldots,F_d):=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d):P\circ\pi_i^{-1}=F_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,d)\right\},\]
where \(\pi_i(x)=x_i\). Membership fixes every marginal distribution but leaves the dependence structure unrestricted. The class is nonempty because the product measure \(F_1\otimes\cdots\otimes F_d\) belongs to it, and it is convex under mixtures of joint laws sharing the same marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Fréchet class consists of all joint distributions having specified marginals while leaving their dependence structure unrestricted.
assumptions_latex: \(F_i\) is a probability distribution on \(\mathbb R\) for each \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathfrak F(F_1,\ldots,F_d)\iff P\circ\pi_i^{-1}=F_i\) for all \(i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Copula Families Induce Convex Fixed-Marginal Law Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity with fixed marginals and a convex copula class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix marginal distribution functions \(F_1,\ldots,F_d\). If \(\mathcal C\) is convex, then the induced family \(\{P_C:F_{P_C}(x)=C(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d)),\ C\in\mathcal C\}\) is convex, since \(\lambda P_C+(1-\lambda)P_D=P_{\lambda C+(1-\lambda)D}\). If marginal families also vary, separate convexity of the marginal families and \(\mathcal C\) does not by itself imply convexity of the induced joint-law family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex copula class gives a convex ambiguity set when marginals are fixed; this conclusion is not automatic when marginals vary.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Copula Families Induce Convex Fixed-Marginal Law Families
Copula Ambiguity Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-law ambiguity induced by admissible marginals and copulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(i=1,\ldots,d\), let \(\mathcal F_i\) be a family of univariate distribution functions, and let \(\mathcal C\) be a family of \(d\)-copulas. The induced copula ambiguity set is
\[\mathcal P_{\mathcal F,\mathcal C}:=\left\{P:\exists F_i\in\mathcal F_i,\ \exists C\in\mathcal C\ \text{such that }F_P(x_1,\ldots,x_d)=C(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d))\right\}.\]
If all marginals are continuous, the copula associated with each admitted joint distribution is unique. Singleton marginal families isolate dependence uncertainty, whereas singleton \(\mathcal C\) isolates marginal uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A copula ambiguity set contains joint distributions assembled from admissible marginal distributions and an admissible family of copulas.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal F_i\) is a nonempty family of univariate distribution functions.
\(\mathcal C\) is a nonempty family of \(d\)-copulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal F,\mathcal C}\) exactly when its joint distribution admits the displayed marginal–copula representation.

children.title: Dependence-Uncertainty Sets
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity sets based on non-copula restrictions on dependence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Independence Does Not Determine Higher-Order Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for low-order dependence restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U,V\) be independent Bernoulli\((1/2)\) variables and let \(W=U\oplus V\). Every pair among \(U,V,W\) is independent, but \(U\oplus V\oplus W=0\) almost surely; hence the three variables are not mutually independent. Pairwise dependence restrictions therefore do not determine higher-order dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three fair bits can be pairwise independent while satisfying a deterministic joint relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\perp V,\ U\perp W,\ V\perp W,\quad\text{but }(U,V,W)\text{ are not mutually independent}.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Independence Does Not Determine Higher-Order Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-copula restrictions expressed through dependence summaries or predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given marginal classes \(\mathcal F_i\), a specified dependence functional or predicate \(T:\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d)\to\mathcal T\), and an admissible region \(D\subseteq\mathcal T\), define \[\mathcal P_T=\{P:P\circ\pi_i^{-1}\in\mathcal F_i\ (i=1,\ldots,d),\ T(P)\in D\}.\] Examples of \(T\) include cross-moments, covariance or correlation entries, rank correlations, orthant probabilities, and conditional-independence predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependence uncertainty can be modeled by restricting non-copula summaries or predicates while separately controlling the marginals.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a specified dependence functional or predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\in\mathcal P_T\iff P\circ\pi_i^{-1}\in\mathcal F_i\ \forall i\text{ and }T(P)\in D.

notation.meaning: Selected dependence summary or predicate for P

knowledge_statements.title: Dependence-Functional Ambiguity Sets
Dependence-Uncertainty Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Copula-restricted ambiguity set with prescribed marginal distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_1,\ldots,F_d\) be univariate distribution functions and let \(\mathfrak C\) be a specified nonempty class of \(d\)-copulas. The associated dependence-uncertainty set is
\[
\mathcal P(F_1,\ldots,F_d;\mathfrak C)=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d):P(( -\infty,x])=C(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d))\text{ for every }x\in\mathbb R^d\text{ and some }C\in\mathfrak C\right\}.
\]
Thus the marginals are fixed while every dependence structure represented by an admissible copula is allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The set fixes all marginal distributions but permits any joint dependence structure represented by a copula in the prescribed class.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak C\) is a nonempty class of \(d\)-copulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P(F_1,\ldots,F_d;\mathfrak C)\) contains exactly the joint laws with marginals \(F_i\) and copula in \(\mathfrak C\).

notation.meaning: Borel probability measures on Euclidean space

children.title: Marginal–Copula Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Consistency boundaries linking marginal information to admissible copulas.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility in the absence of extra coupled joint-law constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any univariate distribution functions \(F_1,\ldots,F_d\) and any \(d\)-copula \(C\), \(H(x)=C(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d))\) is a joint distribution function with marginals \(F_i\). Thus nonempty marginal classes \(\mathfrak F_i\) and a nonempty copula class \(\mathfrak C\) are automatically compatible when no additional coupled joint constraint is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any copula can be combined with any collection of univariate marginals; incompatibility requires additional coupled restrictions.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathfrak F_i\) contains a univariate distribution function.
No additional coupled joint-law constraint is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathfrak F_i\ne\varnothing\ \forall i,\ \mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow\exists(F_1,\ldots,F_d,C)\text{ inducing a joint law}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unconditional Marginal–Copula Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility versus full-copula identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(H(x)=C(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d))\), then \(H\) determines \(C\) on \(R=\prod_i\operatorname{Ran}(F_i)\). Copulas agreeing on \(R\) induce the same \(H\) for these marginals. When all marginals are continuous, \(R=[0,1]^d\) and the copula is unique; with discontinuous marginals, distinct full-copula extensions may be observationally equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete or mixed marginals may leave parts of the copula unidentified even though the marginal-copula specification is compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C|_R=D|_R\Rightarrow C(F_1,\ldots,F_d)=D(F_1,\ldots,F_d).

notation.meaning: Product of the marginal distribution-function ranges

knowledge_statements.title: Identification Domain for Discontinuous Marginals
Marginal–Copula Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence condition for combining marginal constraints with a copula class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given marginal ambiguity classes \(\mathfrak F_1,\ldots,\mathfrak F_d\) and a copula class \(\mathfrak C\), the specifications are compatible precisely when
\[
\left\{(F_1,\ldots,F_d,C):F_i\in\mathfrak F_i,
C\in\mathfrak C,
C(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d))\text{ is admissible for every imposed joint constraint}
\right\}\ne\varnothing.
\]
For any feasible tuple, \(H(x)=C(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d))\) is a joint distribution function with marginals \(F_i\). Conversely, every compatible joint distribution admits such a copula representation; the copula is unique when all marginals are continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginal and copula restrictions are compatible exactly when some admissible copula–marginal tuple satisfies every joint constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak F_i\) are nonempty classes of univariate distribution functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility is equivalent to existence of a feasible tuple \((F_1,\ldots,F_d,C)\).
review_flags: A source explicitly covering constrained marginal–copula compatibility is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited-evidence requirement is unmet, and “admissible for every imposed joint constraint” leaves the joint constraints and admissibility predicate undefined, making the claimed equivalence insufficiently precise.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixture boundary for independence-structured sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each marginal class contain \(\delta_0\) and \(\delta_1\). Then \(P^0=\delta_0\otimes\delta_0\) and \(P^1=\delta_1\otimes\delta_1\) are admitted product laws, but \(\tfrac12P^0+�tfrac12P^1\) has Bernoulli\((1/2)\) marginals and perfect dependence, so it is not their product. Thus product-law ambiguity sets need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing admitted product laws can create dependence, so an independence-structured ambiguity set need not be convex.
assumptions_latex: Both coordinate marginal classes contain \(\delta_0\) and \(\delta_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^0,P^1\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ind}}\centernot\Rightarrow\tfrac12(P^0+P^1)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ind}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Law Families Are Generally Nonconvex

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological stability of product-measure ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each \(\mathsf X_i\) is Polish and each marginal class \(\mathcal P_i\) is weakly compact, then \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ind}}=\{\bigotimes_iP_i:P_i\in\mathcal P_i\}\) is weakly compact. In particular, if product laws converge weakly, their limiting law is the product of the limiting marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weakly compact marginal classes generate a weakly compact product-law class, and independence is preserved under weak limits.
assumptions_latex: The number of factors is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ind}}\text{ is weakly compact}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Compactness from Marginal Compactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent membership tests for product laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A joint law \(P\) with marginals \(P_i\) equals \(\bigotimes_iP_i\) if and only if \(P(\prod_iA_i)=\prod_iP_i(A_i)\) for every measurable rectangle. Equivalently, \(\mathbb E_P[\prod_if_i(X_i)]=\prod_i\mathbb E_{P_i}[f_i(X_i)]\) for every collection of bounded measurable \(f_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product-law membership is equivalent to factorization of rectangle probabilities or bounded coordinatewise expectations.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a probability law on the finite product measurable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P=\bigotimes_iP_i\iff P(\prod_iA_i)=\prod_iP_i(A_i)\iff\mathbb E_P\prod_if_i=\prod_i\mathbb E_{P_i}f_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Characterizations of Independence
Independence-Structured Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-measure ambiguity generated by separate marginal classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathsf X_i,\mathcal B_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,d\), be measurable spaces and let \(\mathcal P_i\) be nonempty classes of probability measures on them. The independence-structured ambiguity set is
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ind}}=\left\{P_1\otimes\cdots\otimes P_d:P_i\in\mathcal P_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,d\right\}.
\]
Every law in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ind}}\) makes the coordinate projections mutually independent, and every independent joint law whose \(i\)-th marginal belongs to \(\mathcal P_i\) lies in this set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independence-structured set consists exactly of product laws formed from admissible marginal distributions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_i\) are nonempty marginal probability classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ind}}\) if and only if its coordinates are independent and its marginals belong to the respective \(\mathcal P_i\).
review_flags: Standard definition, but no relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-measure definition is standard, precise, and appropriate for the topic, but no source with a specific locator was supplied.

children.title: Unimodality Ambiguity Sets
children.top_down_role: Distribution families restricted by a unimodality requirement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity for a Common Prescribed Mode
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixture stability under the selected fixed-mode convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) have distribution functions convex on \(( -\infty,m)\) and concave on \((m,\infty)\), then \(\lambda P_1+(1-\lambda)P_2\) has the same property for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). Common-mode closure can fail when the component modes differ: \(\tfrac12\delta_{-1}+\tfrac12\delta_1\) is not unimodal about either \(-1\) or \(1\) under this convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-mode unimodal laws form a convex class, but mixing laws having different prescribed modes need not preserve either mode.
assumptions_latex: The immutable seed's one-dimensional convex-then-concave distribution-function convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_1,P_2\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{uni}}(m)\Rightarrow\lambda P_1+(1-\lambda)P_2\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{uni}}(m).
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity for a Common Prescribed Mode

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixture representation under the selected fixed-mode convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A real random variable \(X\) is unimodal about \(m\) in the convex-then-concave distribution-function sense if and only if \(X\overset d=m+UZ\) for some random variable \(Z\) independent of \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\). Equivalently, its law is a mixture of uniform laws on intervals having \(m\) as an endpoint, including the degenerate interval \(\{m\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-dimensional fixed-mode unimodal law is exactly a mixture of uniform laws on intervals ending at the mode.
assumptions_latex: The immutable seed's one-dimensional unimodality convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is unimodal about }m\iff X\overset d=m+UZ.

notation.meaning: Uniform random variable on [0,1], independent of Z

knowledge_statements.title: Khintchine Representation of One-Dimensional Unimodality
Unimodality Ambiguity Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional unimodality about a specified mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(m\in\mathbb R\) and additional distributional constraints \(\mathcal K\). The unimodality ambiguity set about \(m\) is
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{uni}}(m;\mathcal K)=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R):P\text{ satisfies }\mathcal K,
F_P\text{ is convex on }(-\infty,m)\text{ and concave on }(m,\infty)
\right\}.
\]
This convention allows an atom at \(m\). If \(P\) has a density, the condition is equivalent, up to null-set versions, to a density that is nondecreasing to \(m\) and nonincreasing after \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ambiguity set contains laws satisfying the side constraints whose distribution functions are convex before the mode and concave afterward.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is a specified collection of distributional constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{uni}}(m;\mathcal K)\) is unimodal about \(m\) under the stated one-dimensional convention.
review_flags: Unimodality has multiple multivariate extensions; this record selects the one-dimensional distribution-function convention.
A supporting source locator is needed.
