knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust chance value depends on a constraint representation only through its induced measurable safety set \(S(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of robust probability constraints on induced event sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a decision \(x\), let \(S(x)\subseteq\Xi\) be its measurable safety set and let \(V(x):=\Xi\setminus S(x)\). The distributionally robust chance requirement satisfies \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}P(S(x))\ge1-\varepsilon\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nu(x):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P(V(x))\le\varepsilon.\] Consequently, two algebraic constraint descriptions inducing the same set \(S(x)\) have identical robust chance values. Intersections of safety conditions produce unions of violation regions, while unions of safety alternatives produce intersections of violation regions; hence logical event geometry determines which probability is optimized over \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust chance feasibility depends on the induced safety or violation set, with logical intersections and unions determining the event geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a decision \(x\), the distributionally robust tail-risk constraint at level \(\alpha\) and bound \(\tau\) is
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha}^{P}(L(x,\xi))\le \tau,

\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha}^{P}(Z)=\inf_{t\in\mathbb R}\left\{t+\frac{1}{1-\alpha}\mathbb E_P[(Z-t)_+]\right\}.

Thus feasibility controls the worst-case average loss in the upper \((1-\alpha)\)-tail over all laws in \(\mathcal P\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines deviation as centered \(L^p\)-dispersion of loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Z\in L^p(P)\), define its centered \(p\)-deviation by
\[
D_{p,P}(Z):=\left(\mathbb E_P\left[\lvert Z-\mathbb E_P[Z]\rvert^p\right]\right)^{1/p}.
\]
A distributionally robust deviation constraint on the loss is
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}D_{p,P}(L(x,\xi))\le\delta.
\]
The centering mean and the deviation are evaluated under the same candidate law \(P\), before taking the supremum over the ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst centered Lp-dispersion of the loss across all candidate distributions must remain below a specified bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a loss \(Z\in L^p(P)\), its upper \(p\)-semideviation is
\[
D^+_{p,P}(Z):=\left(\mathbb E_P\left[(Z-\mathbb E_P[Z])_+^p\right]\right)^{1/p}.
\]
The associated distributionally robust semideviation constraint is
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}D^+_{p,P}(L(x,\xi))\le\delta_+.
\]
Only realizations above the law-dependent mean loss contribute to dispersion, and the same law \(P\) determines both the mean and expectation.

children.title: Asymmetric-Dispersion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Constraint behavior under directional or unequal treatment of deviations.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric-Dispersion Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes asymmetry through unequal upper and lower deviation weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Z\in L^p(P)\), define weighted asymmetric dispersion by
\[
D^{a_+,a_-}_{p,P}(Z):=\left(\mathbb E_P\left[a_+(Z-\mathbb E_P[Z])_+^p+a_-(\mathbb E_P[Z]-Z)_+^p\right]\right)^{1/p}.
\]
A distributionally robust asymmetric-dispersion regime imposes
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}D^{a_+,a_-}_{p,P}(L(x,\xi))\le\delta.
\]
It is asymmetric when \(a_+\ne a_-\). The normalization \(a_+=1\) and \(a_-=0\) gives the upper \(p\)-semideviation for losses; more generally, \(a_-=0\) gives a scaled upper semideviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal weights penalize fluctuations above and below the mean differently; weights one and zero recover the upper semideviation exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is asymmetric when \(a_+\ne a_-\), and feasibility is \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}D^{a_+,a_-}_{p,P}(L(x,\xi))\le\delta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weighted two-sided semideviation is a standard asymmetric-dispersion construction; normalization conventions vary

knowledge_statements.title: Shortfall Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a loss-oriented expected shortfall-loss constraint without assuming that the loss function vanishes below the reference level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a reference level \(z\in\mathbb R\), a distributionally robust shortfall constraint requires
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P\left[\ell(L(x,\xi)-z)\right]\le b.
\]
Because \(\ell\) is nondecreasing, increasing the loss cannot reduce the transformed shortfall. The supremum requires the expected transformed loss relative to \(z\) to satisfy the bound under every probability law in the ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every candidate distribution must give an acceptably small expected transformed loss relative to the reference level.
assumptions_latex: \(z\in\mathbb R\), \(b\ge0\), and \(\ell(L(x,\xi)-z)\) is integrable under every \(P\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is feasible exactly when \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(L(x,\xi)-z)]\le b\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the gain-loss sign correspondence without optimized certainty equivalents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(L(x,\xi):=-G(x,\xi)\) and \(\ell(t):=-u(-t)\). Then \(\ell\) is nondecreasing and convex, and for every \(P\in\mathcal P\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[\ell(L(x,\xi))]=-\mathbb E_P[u(G(x,\xi))].
\]
Consequently,
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[u(G(x,\xi))]\ge\gamma
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(L(x,\xi))]\le-\gamma.
\]
Thus worst-case utility and worst-case shortfall-loss constraints describe the same feasible set after sign and threshold conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating gains and utility converts a worst-case expected-utility lower bound into an equivalent worst-case expected-loss upper bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Shortfall–Utility Correspondence

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
F(x):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[f(x,\xi)].
\]
For each fixed \(P\), expectation preserves convexity of \(x\mapsto f(x,\xi)\); the pointwise supremum over \(P\in\mathcal P\) also preserves convexity. Hence, for every \(x_0,x_1\in X\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\),
\[
F(\lambda x_0+(1-\lambda)x_1)\le\lambda F(x_0)+(1-\lambda)F(x_1).
\]
Thus \(\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\) is a convex optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario-wise convex losses yield a convex worst-case expected objective because both expectation and pointwise supremum preserve convexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial DRO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributionally robust optimization over a finite or discrete combinatorial family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) encode a nonempty family of combinatorial objects, let \(\mathcal P\) be a nonempty ambiguity set on a measurable uncertainty space, and let \(L(x,\xi)\) be integrable under every \(P\in\mathcal P\). A combinatorial DRO problem has the form
\[
\min_{x\in\mathcal F}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[L(x,\xi)].

More generally, \(\mathcal F\) may be any finite or countable family with an explicit combinatorial encoding; its defining feature is selection among discrete structures rather than merely the presence of auxiliary integer variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality–Ambiguity Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction between discrete feasibility and the worst-case distribution selected by nature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[L(x,\xi)]\), an integrality–ambiguity coupling is present when nature's optimizer depends on the discrete decision: there exist \(x^1,x^2\in X\cap\mathbb Z^n\) such that
\[
\operatorname*{argmax}_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[L(x^1,\xi)]\ne
\operatorname*{argmax}_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[L(x^2,\xi)].
\]
Consequently, replacing \(X\cap\mathbb Z^n\) by \(\operatorname{conv}(X\cap\mathbb Z^n)\) changes both decision geometry and potentially the active worst-case distribution; the resulting relaxation gap cannot generally be attributed to integrality alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupling occurs when different integral decisions induce different worst-case distributions, so convexification may alter both feasible decisions and nature’s active response.
assumptions_latex: \(X\cap\mathbb Z^n\) contains at least two feasible decisions.
The displayed worst-case expectations attain their suprema.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decision-dependent worst-case argmax sets imply integrality–ambiguity coupling.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formalizes coupling through decision-dependent worst-case distributions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Decision-dependent worst-case argmax sets are a plausible coupling phenomenon, but the proposed definition is nonstandard and the claim about attribution of the relaxation gap requires dedicated support.

knowledge_statements.title: Measure Linear-Program Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized moment problem with finitely many equality moments on compact support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be compact Hausdorff and let \(h,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in C(K)\). If at least one probability measure on \(K\) satisfies \(\int_K g_i\,dP=b_i\), then
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(K)}\left\{\int_K h\,dP:\int_K g_i\,dP=b_i\ \forall i\right\}
=
\inf_{\lambda_0\in\mathbb R,\,\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}
\left\{\lambda_0+\lambda^\top b:\lambda_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(\xi)\ge h(\xi)\ \forall\xi\in K\right\}.
\]
The primal supremum is attained; the equality is interpreted in the extended-real sense when the value is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst-case expectation under finitely many exact moments equals the least cost of a linear combination of moment functions that majorizes the loss.
assumptions_latex: The prescribed moment vector \(b\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The measure linear program and its pointwise-majorant dual have equal values.

notation.meaning: Borel probability measures supported on K

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Moment Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment ambiguity described by a finite-dimensional conic inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be compact, let \(h:S\to\mathbb R\) and \(g:S\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuous, let \(A:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^r\) be linear, and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) be a closed convex cone with dual cone \(C^*=\{y\in\mathbb R^r:\langle y,c\rangle\ge0\ \forall c\in C\}\). If a probability measure \(P\) satisfies \(A\int_S g\,dP-b\in\operatorname{int}C\), then
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(S)}\left\{\int_S h\,dP:A\int_Sg\,dP-b\in C\right\}
=
\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R,\,y\in C^*}\left\{\eta-\langle y,b\rangle:\eta-\langle A^*y,g(\xi)\rangle\ge h(\xi)\ \forall\xi\in S\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conically constrained moment problem equals a dual search for the cheapest dual-cone-multiplier majorant when strict feasibility holds.
assumptions_latex: A strictly feasible probability measure exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conic moment primal and the corrected pointwise-majorant dual have equal optimal values.

notation.meaning: dual cone of C under the nonnegative-pairing convention

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Moment Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial majorant dual for prescribed moments on compact support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact, let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), and prescribe feasible moments \(y_\alpha=\int_K x^\alpha\,dP\) for every \(\alpha\) in a finite index set \(I\) containing \(0\), with \(y_0=1\). Then
\[
\sup_P\left\{\int_K f(x)\,dP(x):\int_Kx^\alpha\,dP=y_\alpha\ \forall\alpha\in I\right\}
=
\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^I}\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha y_\alpha:\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha x^\alpha-f(x)\ge0\ \forall x\in K\right\}.
\]
Thus the dual variable is a polynomial majorant assembled from the constrained monomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case expectation of a polynomial under prescribed moments equals the least expected polynomial majorant formed from those constrained moments.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is polynomial and \(I\) is finite with \(0\in I\).
The prescribed moment vector is realizable by a probability measure on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The polynomial moment problem equals its polynomial-majorant dual.

notation.meaning: prescribed moment of monomial x to alpha
coefficients of the dual polynomial majorant

knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic Moment Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order moment and sum-of-squares duality for basic semialgebraic support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\), and fix order \(d\). The truncated moment relaxation
\[
\inf_y\left\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_d(y)\succeq0,\ M_{d-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\ \forall j\right\}
\]
has dual
\[
\sup_{\gamma}\left\{\gamma:f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^s\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_j\text{ sum of squares},\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d\right\},
\]
where \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). If either finite-dimensional conic program is strictly feasible and has finite value, their optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each relaxation order, semidefinite moment constraints are dual to a bounded-degree sum-of-squares certificate on the semialgebraic support.
assumptions_latex: All displayed polynomial degrees do not exceed \(2d\).
The primal or dual semidefinite program is strictly feasible.
The common conic-program value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(d\) moment relaxation and its sum-of-squares dual have equal values.

notation.meaning: linear functional defined by truncated moments y
localizing matrix for support polynomial g_j

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial–Support Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree and Archimedean conditions supporting semialgebraic moment hierarchies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For polynomials \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_s\) and support \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\), order \(d\) is polynomial–support compatible when
\[
2d\ge\deg(f),\qquad d\ge d_j:=\left\lceil\frac{\deg(g_j)}2\right\rceil\quad(j=1,\ldots,s),
\]
so every required moment and localizing matrix is defined, and the quadratic module
\[
Q(g)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^s\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\text{ is sum of squares}\right\}
\]
is Archimedean, meaning \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in Q(g)\) for some \(R>0\). The latter condition implies compactness of \(K\) and supports asymptotic completeness of the hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility requires sufficient truncation degree and an Archimedean support description, ensuring defined localizing matrices, compact support, and asymptotically complete SOS certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The degree inequalities and \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in Q(g)\) constitute polynomial–support compatibility.

notation.meaning: quadratic module generated by the support polynomials

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Reference Divergence Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phi-divergence ambiguity around a positive discrete reference distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q_i>0\), \(\sum_iq_i=1\), let \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(\phi(1)=0\), and let \(\rho>0\). For losses \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\sup_{p\ge0}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N p_i\ell_i:\sum_ip_i=1,\ \sum_iq_i\phi(p_i/q_i)\le\rho\right\}
=
\inf_{\eta\ge0,\,\lambda\in\mathbb R}\left\{\lambda+\eta\rho+\eta\sum_{i=1}^Nq_i\phi^*((\ell_i-\lambda)/\eta)\right\}.
\]
At \(\eta=0\), each perspective term uses its lower-semicontinuous closure. The equality follows under feasibility and a finite primal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-support phi-divergence worst-case expectation equals a two-variable convex minimization involving the convex conjugate of the divergence generator.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and satisfies \(\phi(1)=0\).
\(\rho>0\) and the primal value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The discrete divergence-constrained expectation equals the displayed conjugate dual.

notation.meaning: convex conjugate of the divergence generator

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Reference Divergence Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phi-divergence ambiguity relative to a general reference probability measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\) be a probability measure, let \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(\phi(1)=0\), and define \(D_\phi(P\|Q)=\int\phi(dP/dQ)\,dQ\) for \(P\ll Q\). If \(\rho>0\) and the worst-case expectation of measurable \(\ell\) is finite, then
\[
\sup_{P\ll Q}\left\{\mathbb E_P[\ell]:D_\phi(P\|Q)\le\rho\right\}
=
\inf_{\eta\ge0,\,\lambda\in\mathbb R}\left\{\lambda+\eta\rho+\eta\int\phi^*((\ell(\xi)-\lambda)/\eta)\,Q(d\xi)\right\},
\]
provided the divergence constraint admits a strict feasible density. The perspective is closed at \(\eta=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous-reference phi-divergence worst-case expectation equals a convex conjugate integral minimization under strict feasibility and finiteness.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a probability measure and admissible \(P\) satisfy \(P\ll Q\).
A strictly feasible density exists and the primal value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The divergence-ball worst-case expectation equals the displayed integral conjugate dual.

knowledge_statements.title: Divergence-Specific Conic Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone representation of the relative-entropy conjugate perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the Kullback–Leibler generator \(\phi(t)=t\log t-t+1\), its conjugate is \(\phi^*(u)=e^u-1\). Define the closed exponential cone by
\[
K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(a,b,c):b>0,\ b e^{a/b}\le c\}.
\]
For \(\eta\ge0\), the epigraph of the closed perspective satisfies
\[
t\ge\eta\phi^*(s/\eta)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(s,\eta,t+\eta)\in K_{\exp}.
\]
Thus every KL conjugate term in a discrete or continuous divergence dual can be represented by an exponential-cone constraint, with integration or summation applied to the epigraph variables as appropriate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KL conjugate perspective is exactly representable by one exponential-cone constraint, yielding conic formulations of KL-divergence duals.
assumptions_latex: The perspective and exponential cone are interpreted with their closed extensions at \(\eta=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\eta\phi^*(s/\eta)\) if and only if \((s,\eta,t+\eta)\in K_{\exp}\).

notation.meaning: perspective argument, scale, and epigraph variable

knowledge_statements.title: Transport-Cost Dual Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case expectation over a transport-cost ball around a reference law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be Polish, let \(Q\in\mathcal P(S)\), and let \(c:S\times S\to[0,\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous with \(c(z,z)=0\). Define
\[
W_c(P,Q)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}\int c(x,z)\,\pi(dx,dz).
\]
For an upper semicontinuous loss \(\ell\) satisfying suitable integrable growth relative to \(c\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\),
\[
\sup_{P:W_c(P,Q)\le\varepsilon}\int\ell(x)\,P(dx)
=
\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\lambda\varepsilon+\int\sup_{x\in S}[\ell(x)-\lambda c(x,z)]\,Q(dz)\right\}.
\]
Both sides are understood as extended-real values, and finiteness excludes indeterminate expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case expectation over a transport-cost ball equals a scalar minimization of transport penalty plus the reference expectation of a pointwise transform.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is nonnegative and lower semicontinuous with \(c(z,z)=0\).
\(\ell\) is upper semicontinuous and has integrable growth ensuring a finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transport-ball worst-case expectation equals the displayed scalar dual representation.

notation.meaning: optimal transport cost between P and Q
dual multiplier for the transport budget

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical Kantorovich transport-ball dual under semicontinuity and growth conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The canonical transport dual is plausible, but “suitable integrable growth” is not an explicit theorem hypothesis. An exact strong-duality source and its precise growth or coercivity conditions are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Kantorovich–Rubinstein Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual characterization of the first Wasserstein distance on a Polish metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,d)\) be a Polish metric space, let \(P,Q\in\mathcal P_1(\Xi)\), and let \(\Pi(P,Q)\) denote their couplings. Then \[W_1(P,Q)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}\int_{\Xi\times\Xi}d(\xi,\zeta)\,\pi(d\xi,d\zeta)=\sup_{f:\,\operatorname{Lip}(f)\le 1}\left(\int_\Xi f\,dP-\int_\Xi f\,dQ\right).\] For any fixed \(\xi_0\in\Xi\), the supremum is unchanged when restricted to functions satisfying \(f(\xi_0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first Wasserstein distance equals both the minimum expected transportation cost over couplings and the largest expectation difference over real-valued 1-Lipschitz functions; the functions may be normalized to vanish at any fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_1(P,Q)=\sup_{f:\,\operatorname{Lip}(f)\le1}(E_P[f]-E_Q[f])\).

notation.meaning: Set of couplings of P and Q.
Borel probability measures on Xi having finite first moment.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Constrained Transport Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case expectation over a transport ball whose candidate distributions obey a fixed support constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,d)\) be Polish, let \(P\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\), and let \(S\subseteq\Xi\) be closed. For an upper-semicontinuous payoff \(\ell:S\to\mathbb R\) satisfying the stated integrability conditions, \[\sup_{Q:\,Q(S)=1,\;W_c(P,Q)\le\varepsilon}E_Q[\ell(\zeta)]=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\lambda\varepsilon+E_P\left[\sup_{\zeta\in S}\bigl(\ell(\zeta)-\lambda c(\xi,\zeta)\bigr)\right]\right\},\] provided the transport ambiguity set is nonempty and the usual transport strong-duality conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support-constrained worst-case expectation equals a scalar transport penalty plus a pointwise supremum restricted to the prescribed support.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell\) is upper semicontinuous and has sufficient growth control for finite dual values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_QE_Q[\ell]=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\{\lambda\varepsilon+E_P[\sup_{\zeta\in S}(\ell(\zeta)-\lambda c(\xi,\zeta))]\}\).

notation.meaning: Optimal transport cost induced by c.

knowledge_statements.title: Coherent Risk-Envelope Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual envelope representation of a finite coherent loss-risk functional on an integrable random-variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\), let \(1\le p<\infty\), and let \(q\) be conjugate to \(p\). If \(\rho:L^p(P)\to\mathbb R\) is a finite, lower-semicontinuous coherent risk functional for losses, then there is a nonempty convex \(\sigma(L^q,L^p)\)-compact set \(\mathcal D\subseteq L^q(P)\) such that \[\mathcal D\subseteq\{r\in L^q(P):r\ge0\ \ P\text{-a.s.},\ E_P[r]=1\},\qquad \rho(Z)=\sup_{r\in\mathcal D}E_P[rZ]\quad\text{for every }Z\in L^p(P).\] Conversely, every nonempty convex \(\sigma(L^q,L^p)\)-compact set of such densities defines a finite, lower-semicontinuous coherent loss-risk functional by this formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite lower-semicontinuous coherent risk functional for losses is the worst expected loss over a compact convex envelope of probability densities, and every such envelope defines a functional of this kind.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho:L^p(P)\to\mathbb R\) is finite, lower semicontinuous, and coherent under the loss convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(Z)=\sup_{r\in\mathcal D}E_P[rZ]\) for every \(Z\in L^p(P)\).

notation.meaning: Convex compact risk envelope of probability densities.
Density of an alternative probability measure relative to P.
Weak topology induced by the dual pairing between L^q and L^p.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Certainty-Equivalent Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel dual representation of an optimized certainty equivalent for losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in L^p(P)\) and let \(\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, convex, nondecreasing, with \(\phi(0)=0\) and \(1\in\partial\phi(0)\). Define \(\rho_\phi(Z)=\inf_{m\in\mathbb R}\{m+E_P[\phi(Z-m)]\}\). Under Fenchel-duality and integrability qualifications, \[\rho_\phi(Z)=\sup_{r\ge0,\ E_P[r]=1}\left\{E_P[rZ]-E_P[\phi^*(r)]\right\},\] where densities producing undefined expectations are excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Law-Invariant Risk Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kusuoka representation for coherent law-invariant risk measures on an atomless probability space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\) be atomless. Every coherent, law-invariant risk functional \(\rho:L^\infty(P)\to\mathbb R\) having the Fatou property possesses a nonempty convex set \(\mathcal M\) of probability measures on \((0,1]\) such that \[\rho(Z)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal M}\int_{(0,1]}\operatorname{AVaR}_\alpha(Z)\,\mu(d\alpha).\] Conversely, a supremum of this form defines a coherent, law-invariant risk functional with the Fatou property, subject to the corresponding closedness condition on \(\mathcal M\).

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact convex minimax regime for a DRO decision–distribution game.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(\mathcal P\) be nonempty compact convex subsets of Hausdorff topological vector spaces. Suppose \(L:X\times\mathcal P\to\mathbb R\) is lower semicontinuous and convex in \(x\) for every \(Q\), and upper semicontinuous and concave in \(Q\) for every \(x\). Then \[\min_{x\in X}\max_{Q\in\mathcal P}L(x,Q)=\max_{Q\in\mathcal P}\min_{x\in X}L(x,Q).\] Both extrema are attained, and some \((x^*,Q^*)\) satisfies \(L(x^*,Q)\le L(x^*,Q^*)\le L(x,Q^*)\) for all \((x,Q)\in X\times\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compactness, convexity, semicontinuity, and convex–concave structure yield minimax equality and an attained saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(\mathcal P\) are nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(L(\cdot,Q)\) is lower semicontinuous and convex for each \(Q\).
\(L(x,\cdot)\) is upper semicontinuous and concave for each \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_x\max_QL(x,Q)=\max_Q\min_xL(x,Q)\), and a saddle point exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Favorable Distributions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-favorable distributions in a DRO decision–distribution game and their saddle-point characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonempty sets \(X\) and \(\mathcal P\) and a loss \(L:X\times\mathcal P\to\mathbb R\), a distribution \(Q^*\in\mathcal P\) is least favorable in the maximin sense if \[Q^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{Q\in\mathcal P}\inf_{x\in X}L(x,Q).\] If minimax equality holds, the relevant extrema are attained, and \(x^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}L(x,Q^*)\) also minimizes \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}L(x,Q)\), then \((x^*,Q^*)\) is a saddle point and \[L(x^*,Q)\le L(x^*,Q^*)\le L(x,Q^*)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X\text{ and }Q\in\mathcal P.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-favorable distribution maximizes the loss achievable against an optimally responding decision. Under minimax equality and compatible attainment, it can be paired with an optimal decision to form a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: The maximin optimum is attained for the definition.
Minimax equality and compatible primal and maximin attainment are required for the saddle-point characterization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{Q\in\mathcal P}\inf_{x\in X}L(x,Q)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Minimax-Interchange Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete strict minimax gap when convex decision and ambiguity domains are absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=Y=\{-1,1\}\) and define \(L(x,y)=xy\). Then \[\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}L(x,y)=1,\qquad \max_{y\in Y}\min_{x\in X}L(x,y)=-1.\] Thus the minimax inequality is strict and no saddle point exists. The example isolates the convexification boundary: replacing both sets by \([-1,1]\) while retaining the bilinear payoff restores minimax equality, with common value \(0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Based Analytical Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nature's subproblem when support is the only restriction on the distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a nonempty Borel subset of a Polish space, let \(\mathcal P(S)\) be the Borel probability measures on \(S\), and let \(\ell:S\to\mathbb R\) be Borel measurable and bounded above. Then \[\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P(S)}E_Q[\ell(\xi)]=\sup_{\xi\in S}\ell(\xi).\] If the pointwise supremum is attained at \(\xi^*\in S\), then \(\delta_{\xi^*}\) is optimal. Otherwise, for any sequence \((\xi_n)\subseteq S\) satisfying \(\ell(\xi_n)\to\sup_{\xi\in S}\ell(\xi)\), the values under \(\delta_{\xi_n}\) converge to the supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When support is the only restriction, the worst expected loss equals the largest pointwise loss on the support; an attaining point gives an optimal Dirac law, while maximizing points give asymptotically optimal Dirac laws.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a nonempty Borel subset of a Polish space.
\(\ell:S\to\mathbb R\) is Borel measurable and bounded above.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P(S)}E_Q[\ell]=\sup_{\xi\in S}\ell(\xi)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Based Analytical Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form quadratic expectation under prescribed first and second moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\in\mathbb R^d\) have mean \(\mu\) and covariance matrix \(\Sigma\succeq0\). For any \(a\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\), every distribution with these moments satisfies \[E\bigl[(a^\top\xi+b)^2\bigr]=(a^\top\mu+b)^2+a^\top\Sigma a.\] Consequently, if the corresponding moment class is nonempty, the supremum and infimum of this quadratic expectation over that class coincide with the displayed value.

knowledge_statements.title: Support–Moment Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar bound for convex losses with bounded support and prescribed mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a<b\), \(\mu\in[a,b]\), and let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) be convex. Over all probability laws supported on \([a,b]\) with mean \(\mu\), \[\sup_QE_Q[f(\xi)]=\frac{b-\mu}{b-a}f(a)+\frac{\mu-a}{b-a}f(b).\] The bound is attained by the endpoint distribution assigning probabilities \((b-\mu)/(b-a)\) and \((\mu-a)/(b-a)\) to \(a\) and \(b\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex loss, bounded support and a fixed mean force the worst-case law to place mass at the two endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_QE_Q[f(\xi)]=\frac{b-\mu}{b-a}f(a)+\frac{\mu-a}{b-a}f(b)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Transport Analytical Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kantorovich dual formula for a Wasserstein ball centered at an empirical distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat P_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\widehat\xi_i}\) on a Polish space \((\Xi,d)\), let \(p\ge 1\), and let \(\ell(x,\cdot)\) be upper semicontinuous with at most \(p\)-order growth. For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), under strong transport duality,
\[
\sup_{P:\,W_p(P,\widehat P_N)\le\varepsilon}E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]
=
\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\lambda\varepsilon^p+\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}\bigl(\ell(x,\xi)-\lambda d(\xi,\widehat\xi_i)^p\bigr)\right\}.
\]
Thus nature's distributional problem decomposes into \(N\) penalized pointwise transport problems and one scalar minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst-case expectation over an empirical Wasserstein ball equals a scalar transport-penalty minimization containing one independent pointwise maximization per observation.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,d)\) is Polish and \(\widehat P_N\) has finite \(p\)-th moment.
\(\ell(x,\cdot)\) is upper semicontinuous and has controlled \(p\)-order growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sup_{P:W_p(P,\widehat P_N)\le\varepsilon}E_P[\ell]=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\left(\lambda\varepsilon^p+N^{-1}\sum_i\sup_{\xi}(\ell-\lambda d^p)\right)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Affine Loss Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex reformulation for one-Wasserstein DRO with an unrestricted Euclidean support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Xi=\mathbb R^m\), let the transport cost be \(\|\xi-\zeta\|\), and suppose
\[
\ell(x,\xi)=\max_{1\le k\le K}\{a_k(x)^\top\xi+b_k(x)\}.
\]
For the empirical one-Wasserstein ball of radius \(\varepsilon\),
\[
\sup_{P:W_1(P,\widehat P_N)\le\varepsilon}E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]
=
\min_{\lambda,s}\left\{\lambda\varepsilon+\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^Ns_i:
 s_i\ge a_k(x)^\top\widehat\xi_i+b_k(x),\ 
 \|a_k(x)\|_*\le\lambda\ \forall i,k\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, the value is the empirical loss plus \(\varepsilon\max_k\|a_k(x)\|_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A piecewise-affine loss over an unrestricted one-Wasserstein ball becomes a finite convex program, or empirical loss plus radius times the largest dual-norm slope.
assumptions_latex: \(\Xi=\mathbb R^m\) and transportation uses a norm \(\|\cdot\|\).
The loss is the maximum of finitely many affine functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sup_PE_P[\ell]=N^{-1}\sum_i\ell(x,\widehat\xi_i)+\varepsilon\max_k\|a_k(x)\|_*\).

notation.meaning: dual norm of the transport norm

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Loss Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-matrix reformulation for quadratic loss under squared Euclidean Wasserstein transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Xi=\mathbb R^m\), \(\ell(\xi)=\xi^\top Q\xi+2q^\top\xi+r\), where \(Q=Q^\top\), and use squared Euclidean transport. Then
\[
\sup_{P:W_2(P,\widehat P_N)\le\varepsilon}E_P[\ell(\xi)]
=
\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\lambda\varepsilon^2+\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N
\left[r+\lambda\|\widehat\xi_i\|_2^2+(q+\lambda\widehat\xi_i)^\top(\lambda I-Q)^{-1}(q+\lambda\widehat\xi_i)\right]:\lambda I-Q\succ0\right\}.
\]
Each inverse-quadratic term admits a Schur-complement epigraph, so the expression has a semidefinite formulation. The infimum convention covers limiting feasible boundary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic-loss Wasserstein DRO reduces to one scalar multiplier and inverse-quadratic sample terms, which can be represented by Schur-complement semidefinite constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric and the support is \(\mathbb R^m\).
The ambiguity set uses squared Euclidean transport and has finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sup_PE_P[\ell]\) equals the displayed infimum over \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda I-Q\succ0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Loss Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-Wasserstein reformulation for fixed-recourse linear programs with a bounded dual polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Q(x,\xi)=\min_y\{q^\top y:Wy\ge h(x)+T\xi\},
\qquad
\Pi=\{\pi\ge0:W^\top\pi=q\}.
\]
Assume complete recourse, strong linear-programming duality, and that \(\Pi\) is a nonempty polytope with vertex set \(V\). Then \(Q(x,\xi)=\max_{\pi\in V}\pi^\top(h(x)+T\xi)\). For norm transportation on \(\mathbb R^m\),
\[
\sup_{P:W_1(P,\widehat P_N)\le\varepsilon}E_P[Q(x,\xi)]
=
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^NQ(x,\widehat\xi_i)+
\varepsilon\max_{\pi\in V}\|T^\top\pi\|_*.
\]
Hence the recourse loss inherits the finite piecewise-affine Wasserstein reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-recourse linear value function is a maximum of affine dual pieces; its Wasserstein robustification adds radius times the largest dual-piece slope.
assumptions_latex: The recourse program is feasible with finite value for every \(\xi\).
Transportation uses a norm on the unrestricted support \(\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sup_PE_P[Q]=N^{-1}\sum_iQ(x,\widehat\xi_i)+\varepsilon\max_{\pi\in V}\|T^\top\pi\|_*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Moment Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-programming dual of a finite-support ambiguity set defined by affine moment constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scenarios \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\), let \(l_i=\ell(x,\xi_i)\) and
\[
\mathcal P=\{p\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ap=b,\ Cp\le d\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal P\) is nonempty and the primal value is finite, linear-programming duality gives
\[
\max_{p\in\mathcal P}l^\top p
=
\min_{y,z}\{b^\top y+d^\top z:A^\top y+C^\top z\ge l,\ z\ge0,\ y\text{ free}\}.
\]
Normalization \(\mathbf1^\top p=1\) and prescribed or bounded linear moments are included as rows of \(A\) or \(C\). Thus a finite-support linear moment DRO problem has an exact finite linear reformulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition for continuous real-valued functions on a closed interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_0,\ldots,u_m\) be continuous on \([a,b]\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Moment Representations and Their Index Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for atomic representations of generalized moments generated by a Chebyshev system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a probability measure \(P\) on \([a,b]\), let \(\mu_k=\int_a^b u_k(z)\,dP\), \(k=0,\ldots,m\). If \(P=\sum_{i=1}^N p_i\delta_{z_i}\), then \(\mu_k=\sum_{i=1}^N u_k(z_i)p_i\); the \(z_i\) are seeds and the \(p_i\) are weights. The representation index counts each interior seed twice and each endpoint seed once. It is canonical when its index is at most \(m+2\), and principal when its index is \(m+1\). If \(m+1\) is even, a principal representation is lower when every seed is interior and upper when both endpoints are seeds. If \(m+1\) is odd, it is lower when \(a\) but not \(b\) is a seed, and upper when \(b\) but not \(a\) is a seed.

Its index counts interior seeds twice and endpoint seeds once. Index at most m+2 is canonical and index m+1 is principal. The lower and upper principal classes are distinguished by endpoint inclusion, with the rule depending on the parity of m+1.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Moment Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOCP reformulation for finite-support distributions whose moment vector lies in a Euclidean ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_i\in\mathbb R^r\) be scenario statistics, let \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_n]\), and define
\[
\mathcal P=\{p\ge0:\mathbf1^\top p=1,\ \|Ap-b\|_2\le\rho\}.
\]
For scenario losses \(l_i\), if \(\mathcal P\ne\varnothing\), then
\[
\max_{p\in\mathcal P}l^\top p
=
\min_{y,t,s}\{b^\top y+\rho t+s:\|y\|_2\le t,\ s\ge l_i-a_i^\top y\ \forall i\}.
\]
The displayed problem is a second-order-cone program. The equality follows from conic duality whenever the usual relative-interior condition holds; otherwise its right-hand side remains a valid upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Euclidean-ball restriction on a finite distribution's moment vector yields an SOCP dual with a norm epigraph and one affine inequality per scenario.

A relative-interior feasible probability exists for exact conic duality.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral–Conic Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when norm-bounded moment ambiguity is linear or requires genuine conic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider finite-support ambiguity
\[
\mathcal P_\rho=\{p\ge0:\mathbf1^\top p=1,\ \|Ap-b\|\le\rho\}.
\]
Its dual contains the support function \(\rho\|y\|_*\). If \(\rho=0\), this term vanishes and the reformulation is linear. If the unit ball of \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is polyhedral, the epigraph of \(\rho\|y\|_*\) has a finite linear description, so the reformulation is again an LP. For \(\rho>0\) and the Euclidean norm in dimension at least two, the norm epigraph is nonpolyhedral and the natural exact formulation is an SOCP rather than an LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment DRO is polyhedral for exact moments or polyhedral norms, but a positive-radius Euclidean moment ball generally produces a genuine second-order-cone formulation.
assumptions_latex: The ambiguity model has finite support and affine moment map \(p\mapsto Ap\).
The dual representation is finite and strong duality applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho=0\) or a polyhedral dual norm yields an LP; \(\rho>0\) with a multidimensional Euclidean norm yields an SOCP epigraph.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Moment Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SDP for maximum-of-quadratics loss under prescribed first and second moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z=(1,\xi)\), prescribe \(E_P[zz^\top]=\Omega\succeq0\), and let
\[
\ell(\xi)=\max_{1\le k\le K}z^\top L_kz,
\]
where every \(L_k\) is symmetric. If the generalized moment problem is feasible and satisfies moment-cone strong duality, then
\[
\sup_{P:\,E_P[zz^\top]=\Omega}E_P[\ell(\xi)]
=
\min_{M\in\mathbb S^{m+1}}\{\langle M,\Omega\rangle:M-L_k\succeq0\ \forall k\}.
\]
The matrix \(M\) defines a quadratic majorant of every loss piece, while the objective evaluates its expectation using the prescribed moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fixed first and second moments, the worst expectation of a maximum of quadratic losses equals an SDP over a common quadratic majorant.
assumptions_latex: The prescribed moment matrix is realizable by a probability distribution.
The generalized moment primal and its quadratic-majorant dual have no duality gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sup_PE_P[\ell]=\min_M\{\langle M,\Omega\rangle:M-L_k\succeq0\ \forall k\}\).

children.title: Moment Relaxation Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical outer approximations expressed through truncated moment information.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment Relaxation Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lasserre-type outer moment hierarchy for polynomial maximization on a compact semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{\xi:g_j(\xi)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\) and maximize a polynomial \(f\) over probability measures supported on \(K\). At order \(d\), replace a measure by truncated moments \(y\) and solve
\[
u_d=\sup_y\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_d(y)\succeq0,\ M_{d-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\ \forall j\},
\]
where \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). Every supported measure generates a feasible \(y\), hence \(u_d\) is an upper bound. If the quadratic module is Archimedean, then \(u_{d+1}\le u_d\) and \(u_d\downarrow\max_{\xi\in K}f(\xi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated positive-semidefinite moment and localizing matrices give decreasing upper bounds for polynomial maximization, converging under an Archimedean compactness condition.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation order contains all moments required by \(f\) and the \(g_j\).
The quadratic module generated by the support polynomials is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle u_d\ge u_{d+1}\ge\max_{\xi\in K}f(\xi)\) and \(\displaystyle u_d\to\max_{\xi\in K}f(\xi)\).

notation.meaning: Riesz functional associated with truncated moments y

children.title: Sum-of-Squares Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical positivity certificates based on sum-of-squares structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum-of-Squares Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-truncated sum-of-squares certificates for polynomial upper bounds on semialgebraic supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K=\{\xi:g_j(\xi)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\), define the order-\(d\) bound
\[
v_d=\inf_{\gamma,\sigma_j}\left\{\gamma:\gamma-f=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^s\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_j\ \text{sum of squares},\ \deg(\sigma_0)\le2d,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d\right\}.
\]
The displayed identity certifies \(\gamma\ge f(\xi)\) for every \(\xi\in K\), so \(v_d\) is a verifiable upper bound. Under the Archimedean condition, \(v_{d+1}\le v_d\) and \(v_d\downarrow\max_{\xi\in K}f(\xi)\). Each sum-of-squares constraint has a semidefinite Gram-matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-degree sum-of-squares decomposition certifies a global polynomial upper bound on the support, with convergent bounds under Archimedean compactness.
assumptions_latex: The support is described by polynomial inequalities \(g_j\ge0\).
The generated quadratic module is Archimedean for convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma-f\in\operatorname{QM}_{2d}(g)\) certifies \(\gamma\ge\max_K f\), and the optimal certificates converge downward to \(\max_K f\).

notation.meaning: degree-truncated quadratic module generated by the support polynomials

children.title: Primal–Dual Hierarchy Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between moment relaxations and sum-of-squares certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Hierarchy Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orderwise SDP duality between truncated moment relaxations and sum-of-squares certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an order \(d\) for which the moment and localizing matrices are defined. The conic dual of
\[
\sup_y\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_d(y)\succeq0,\ M_{d-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\}
\]
is
\[
\inf_{\gamma,\sigma_j}\left\{\gamma:\gamma-f=\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_j\ \text{sum of squares},\ \deg(\sigma_0),\deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d\right\}.
\]
Consequently the moment bound does not exceed the sum-of-squares bound. If either SDP satisfies an appropriate Slater condition and both values are finite, their optimal values coincide and the attained primal and dual solutions provide matching pseudo-moment and polynomial certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every relaxation order, the SOS certificate problem is the conic dual of the moment SDP; Slater regularity makes their bounds equal.
assumptions_latex: Both order-d semidefinite programs are feasible with finite value.
A primal or dual Slater condition holds for equality and attainment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_d\le v_d\), and under SDP strong duality \(u_d=v_d\).

children.title: Linear Divergence Reformulations

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Divergence Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear reformulation of finite-support total-variation distributional ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\in\mathbb R_+^n\) satisfy \(\mathbf1^\top q=1\), and define the total-variation ambiguity set using the convention
\[
\mathcal P_\rho=\{p\ge0:\mathbf1^\top p=1,\ \|p-q\|_1\le\rho\}.
\]
For a scenario-loss vector \(l\), its worst-case expectation is exactly the linear program
\[
\max_{p,u}\left\{l^\top p:\mathbf1^\top p=1,\ p\ge0,\ -u_i\le p_i-q_i\le u_i,\ u_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^nu_i\le\rho\right\}.
\]
The auxiliary variables \(u_i\) linearize the absolute deviations. If total variation is instead defined as one half of the \(\ell_1\) distance, the budget becomes \(2\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-support total-variation DRO is an LP obtained by introducing nonnegative variables that majorize each absolute probability deviation from the nominal distribution.
assumptions_latex: The nominal and adversarial distributions share the same finite support.
The stated convention uses total variation equal to the full \(\ell_1\) distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sup_{p\in\mathcal P_\rho}l^\top p\) equals the displayed finite linear program.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary epigraph linearization of finite-support total variation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LP representation is appropriate and internally consistent with the stated full-l1 convention, but no citation supports the convention and exact reformulation.

children.title: Conic Divergence Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Divergence DRO formulations represented through nonpolyhedral cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Divergence Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support conic representation of a worst-case expectation over a phi-divergence ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_i>0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\), and let \(\phi:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(\phi(1)=0\). Define \(K_\phi=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,t):v>0,\ v\phi(u/v)\le t\}\). For losses \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R\), the robust value has the conic formulation
\[\sup\left\{\sum_i q_i\ell_i:q_i\ge0,\ \sum_iq_i=1,\ (q_i,p_i,t_i)\in K_\phi,\ \sum_it_i\le\rho\right\}.\]
Under strict feasibility, it equals
\[\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R,\,\lambda\ge0}\left\{\eta+\rho\lambda+\sum_i p_i\lambda\phi^*((\ell_i-\eta)/\lambda)\right\},\]
where terms at \(\lambda=0\) use the closed perspective convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite phi-divergence worst-case expectation is a conic program and, under strict feasibility, equals a scalar dual involving the conjugate divergence.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and normalized by \(\phi(1)=0\).
The primal divergence ball is strictly feasible for the asserted equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{q:D_\phi(q,p)\le\rho}q^\top\ell=\inf_{\eta,\lambda\ge0}\{\eta+\rho\lambda+\sum_i p_i\lambda\phi^*((\ell_i-\eta)/\lambda)\}\).

notation.meaning: Closed cone generated by the perspective epigraph of the divergence generator.
Convex conjugate of the divergence generator.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite phi-divergence duality follows from perspective-cone modeling and convex conjugacy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the perspective-cone formulation, strong-duality conditions, or conjugate formula.

children.title: Divergence-Cone Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Matching divergence families to linear, second-order, exponential, or related cone geometries.

knowledge_statements.title: Divergence-Cone Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which a finite phi-divergence ambiguity model is representable in a chosen cone family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a closed convex cone family \(\mathcal K\). A divergence generator \(\phi\) is compatible with \(\mathcal K\) when its closed perspective epigraph
\[K_\phi=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,t)\in\mathbb R^3:v>0,\ v\phi(u/v)\le t\}\]
admits a finite lift \(K_\phi=\{y:\exists w,\ Ay+Bw=b,\ w\in\mathcal K\}\). If, additionally, each loss epigraph and the decision set possess finite \(\mathcal K\)-representations, then the finite-support phi-divergence robust expectation and its optimization model admit a finite \(\mathcal K\)-conic formulation. Without such a lift, the generic conjugate reformulation remains convex but need not belong to the selected cone family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone compatibility means that the divergence perspective epigraph has a finite lift over the selected cones; compatible losses and decisions then yield a finite conic DRO model.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(\mathbb R_+\).
The ambiguity distribution has finite support with positive nominal probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite \(\mathcal K\)-lift of \(K_\phi\), together with compatible loss and decision representations, yields a finite \(\mathcal K\)-conic DRO reformulation.

notation.meaning: Selected product family of closed convex cones.
Closed perspective-epigraph cone of the divergence generator.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conic representability is characterized by a finite lift of the relevant perspective epigraph

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the compatibility leaf and is mathematically plausible, but the finite-lift criterion and resulting conic representability require an authoritative conic-modeling source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Cone Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone formulation for relative-entropy ambiguity on a finite scenario set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q\Vert p)=\sum_i p_i\phi(q_i/p_i)\) with \(\phi(r)=r\log r-r+1\), and define
\[K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(a,b,c):b>0,\ b\exp(a/b)\le c\}.\]
For \(p_i>0\), the worst-case expectation over \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q\Vert p)\le\rho\) equals, under strict feasibility,
\[\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R,\,\lambda\ge0,\,z\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\eta+\rho\lambda+\sum_i p_i(z_i-\lambda):(\ell_i-\eta,\lambda,z_i)\in K_{\exp}\ \forall i\right\}.\]
The closure of \(K_{\exp}\) supplies the limiting interpretation when \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KL-divergence worst-case expectation becomes an exponential-cone program with two scalar dual variables and one exponential-cone constraint per scenario.
assumptions_latex: The relative-entropy ambiguity set is strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KL-robust expectation is represented exactly by the displayed \(K_{\exp}\)-conic minimization problem.

notation.meaning: Kullback–Leibler divergence in normalized phi-divergence form.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the conjugate of normalized relative entropy is the exponential-minus-one function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponential-cone representation is consistent with the conjugate of normalized relative entropy, but no inspectable source supports the exact formulation or its strong-duality assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Dimensional Scalar Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar dual reduction of finite-support phi-divergence worst-case expectations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nominal probabilities \(p_i>0\), losses \(\ell_i(x)\), and a phi-divergence radius \(\rho\), define
\[R(x)=\sup\left\{\sum_iq_i\ell_i(x):q\in\Delta_n,\ \sum_i p_i\phi(q_i/p_i)\le\rho\right\}.\]
If \(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex and the ambiguity set is strictly feasible, then
\[R(x)=\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R,\,\lambda\ge0}\left\{\eta+\rho\lambda+\lambda\sum_i p_i\phi^*((\ell_i(x)-\eta)/\lambda)\right\}.\]
Thus distributional optimization over \(n\) probabilities reduces to optimization over the two scalars \(\eta\) and \(\lambda\), with scenario dependence confined to a separable sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality reduces optimization over all scenario probabilities to a convex minimization over two scalars, regardless of the number of scenarios.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and satisfies \(\phi(1)=0\).
The ambiguity set satisfies strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust expectation \(R(x)\) has a two-scalar conjugate reformulation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Lagrange dualization of normalization and divergence constraints leaves two scalar multipliers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-scalar representation fits the leaf, but it lacks a source and does not state the closed-perspective convention required to interpret terms at lambda equal to zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Reformulation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-support reformulation of a distributionally robust chance constraint under phi-divergence ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(x\), let \(v_i(x)=\mathbf 1\{g(x,\xi_i)>0\}\), and let \(\mathcal Q=\{q\in\Delta_n:\sum_i p_i\phi(q_i/p_i)\le\rho\}\). The distributionally robust chance constraint
\[\inf_{q\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb P_q(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\]
is equivalent to
\[\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R,\,\lambda\ge0}\left\{\eta+\rho\lambda+\sum_i p_i\lambda\phi^*((v_i(x)-\eta)/\lambda)\right\}\le\varepsilon,\]
provided strong duality holds. This reformulation is exact for each fixed violation vector; any remaining nonconvexity arises from the indicator dependence on \(x\), not from the distributional maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finite support, the worst-case violation probability has an exact two-scalar divergence dual; decision-dependent violation indicators may still make the overall constraint nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and normalized at one.
The ambiguity set satisfies a constraint qualification ensuring strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{q\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb P_q(g\le0)\ge1-\varepsilon\) holds exactly when the displayed scalar dual value does not exceed \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Indicator that scenario \(i\) violates the constraint at \(x\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a chance constraint is a robust expectation of a violation indicator, permitting the standard phi-divergence dual

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-violation-vector dual is plausible and appropriately distinguishes residual decision nonconvexity, but the exact equivalence, constraint qualification, and lambda-zero convention require authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Convex Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case CVaR sufficient condition for a distributionally robust chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x,\xi)\) be convex in \(x\) for every \(\xi\), let \(0<\varepsilon<1\), and let \(\mathcal P\) be an ambiguity set. If there exists \(t\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[t+\frac1\varepsilon\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[(G(x,\xi)-t)_+]\le0,\]
then
\[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P(G(x,\xi)>0)\le\varepsilon.\]
Whenever the worst-case hinge expectation has a convex representation, the displayed condition is convex in \((x,t)\). It is generally sufficient rather than necessary because upper-tail average control is stronger than controlling only the violation probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common-threshold worst-case CVaR constraint safely enforces the distributionally robust chance constraint and is convex when the robust hinge expectation is convex-representable.
assumptions_latex: The relevant expectations are finite for every \(P\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust CVaR inequality implies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P(G(x,\xi)>0)\le\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: upper-tail CVaR dominates the corresponding quantile and therefore supplies a safe chance-constraint approximation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The worst-case CVaR condition is a standard safe approximation and the condition content kind fits, but no cited source with a specific locator supports the implication and convexity claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact big-M and divergence-dual formulation for finite-scenario robust chance constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(g_i(x)=g(x,\xi_i)\le M_i\) on the decision set, with finite valid constants \(M_i\ge0\). For binary variables \(z_i\), the finite-support phi-divergence chance constraint is equivalent to the existence of \(z\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(\eta\in\mathbb R\), and \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying
\[g_i(x)\le M_i z_i\quad\forall i,\]
\[\eta+\rho\lambda+\sum_i p_i\lambda\phi^*((z_i-\eta)/\lambda)\le\varepsilon.\]
The first constraints force \(z_i=1\) for every violated scenario, while the second bounds the worst-case probability assigned to marked scenarios. Conic-representable conjugate perspectives produce a mixed-integer conic formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid big-M constraints encode scenario violations, while a scalar divergence dual bounds their worst-case probability, yielding an exact mixed-integer conic model.
assumptions_latex: \(M_i\) is a finite valid upper bound for \(g_i(x)\) on the decision set.
The nominal probabilities are positive and the phi-divergence dual has no gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust chance constraint is equivalent to the displayed mixed-integer divergence-dual system.

notation.meaning: Binary marker for violation of scenario \(i\).
Dual variables for probability normalization and divergence radius.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scenario violations admit exact binary big-M encoding, and their robust probability is a phi-divergence worst-case expectation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary big-M construction is plausible, but exactness depends on valid scenario bounds, dual attainment or closure, and the lambda-zero convention; none is supported by an inspectable citation.

children.title: Bonferroni Approximations
children.top_down_role: Bonferroni-based relaxations for distributionally robust joint chance constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Bonferroni Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk-allocation approximation for distributionally robust joint chance constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_1,\dots,g_m\) be measurable constraint functions, let \(\mathcal P\) be an ambiguity set, let \(0\le\varepsilon\le1\), and choose allocations \(\varepsilon_j\ge0\) with \(\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j\le\varepsilon\). If
\[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P(g_j(x,\xi)>0)\le\varepsilon_j\quad\text{for every }j,\]
then
\[\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}P(g_j(x,\xi)\le0\ \text{for all }j)\ge1-\varepsilon.\]
The implication holds without independence assumptions. It may be conservative because the union bound ignores overlap among violation events and because the same distribution need not maximize every marginal violation probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocating a total violation budget across individual robust chance constraints safely enforces the robust joint chance constraint without requiring independence.
assumptions_latex: All violation events are measurable under every \(P\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Individual worst-case violation bounds imply \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}P(\bigcap_j\{g_j\le0\})\ge1-\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the conclusion is the distributionally robust application of Boole's union bound

children.title: Tail-Risk Approximations

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Risk Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CVaR approximation of a distributionally robust joint chance constraint through maximum violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the maximum violation \(G(x,\xi)=\max_{1\le j\le m}g_j(x,\xi)\). For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), the existence of \(t\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[t+\frac1\varepsilon\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[(G(x,\xi)-t)_+]\le0\]
implies
\[\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}P(g_j(x,\xi)\le0\ \text{for all }j)\ge1-\varepsilon.\]
If every \(g_j(\cdot,\xi)\) is convex, then \(G(\cdot,\xi)\) and its positive-part perspective are convex; hence the approximation is convex whenever the worst-case expectation is convex-representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying worst-case CVaR to the maximum constraint violation safely approximates a robust joint chance constraint and preserves convexity under convex scenario constraints.
assumptions_latex: The displayed worst-case expectation is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximum-violation CVaR condition implies robust joint feasibility with probability at least \(1-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Maximum of the component constraint violations.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the joint violation event equals the positive exceedance event of the maximum constraint function

children.title: Approximation Comparison Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguishing the tightness, tractability, or conservatism of the two families.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation Comparison Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set ordering induced by pointwise ordering of safe violation-probability bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U_B(x)\) and \(U_T(x)\) be valid upper bounds on the worst-case joint violation probability, produced respectively by Bonferroni allocation and a tail-risk surrogate. On any decision region \(X_0\) where
\[U_T(x)\le U_B(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in X_0,\]
the associated feasible sets satisfy
\[\{x\in X_0:U_B(x)\le\varepsilon\}\subseteq\{x\in X_0:U_T(x)\le\varepsilon\}\subseteq\left\{x\in X_0:\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P(\text{joint violation})\le\varepsilon\right\}.\]
The reverse inclusion holds when the pointwise ordering of \(U_B\) and \(U_T\) is reversed. Thus relative conservatism is certified by bound dominance on the specified regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whichever safe upper bound is pointwise smaller yields the larger approximate feasible set, while both feasible sets remain inside the exact robust chance-feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(U_B\) and \(U_T\) upper-bound the same worst-case violation probability on \(X_0\).
The comparison uses the same tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise dominance of safe bounds reverses into feasible-set containment.

notation.meaning: Bonferroni upper bound on worst-case joint violation probability.
Tail-risk upper bound on worst-case joint violation probability.
Decision regime on which pointwise dominance is established.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sublevel-set inclusion follows directly from pointwise ordering of valid upper bounds

children.title: Divergence Regularization
