knowledge_statements.title: Divergence Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual regularization induced by a finite-support phi-divergence ambiguity ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nominal probabilities \(p_i>0\) with \(p\in\Delta_n\), a loss vector \(\ell(x)\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\rho\ge0\), define
\[R_\rho(x)=\sup_{q\in\Delta_n}\left\{q^\top\ell(x):D_\phi(q,p)\le\rho\right\},\qquad D_\phi(q,p)=\sum_i p_i\phi(q_i/p_i).\]
If \(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex, satisfies \(\phi(1)=0\), and strong duality holds, then
\[R_\rho(x)=\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R,\,\lambda\ge0}\left\{\eta+\rho\lambda+\sum_i p_i\lambda\phi^*((\ell_i(x)-\eta)/\lambda)\right\},\]
where each term at \(\lambda=0\) is interpreted as a closed perspective. This is a radius-dependent conjugate-regularized representation of the robust value, and \(R_\rho(x)\ge p^\top\ell(x)\). If additionally \(\phi(r)>0\) for every \(r\ne1\), then \(R_0(x)=p^\top\ell(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phi-divergence robustification has a radius-dependent conjugate-regularized dual representation and dominates the nominal expectation; at radius zero it equals the nominal expectation when the divergence vanishes only at the nominal distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, closed, convex, and satisfies \(\phi(1)=0\).
A constraint qualification ensures strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust value has the displayed conjugate-regularized representation; moreover, \(R_\rho(x)\ge p^\top\ell(x)\), and under strict normalization \(R_0(x)=p^\top\ell(x)\).

notation.meaning: Worst-case expected loss at divergence radius \(\rho\).
Dual centering variable for probability normalization.
Convex conjugate of the divergence generator.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: divergence-ball support functions have conjugate dual representations

children.title: Variance Regularization
children.top_down_role: Variance-sensitive penalties arising from robustification.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact mean-standard-deviation form for an interior chi-square divergence ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_i>0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\), \(\ell\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\mu=p^\top\ell\), and \(\sigma^2=\sum_i p_i(\ell_i-\mu)^2>0\). For the chi-square generator \(\phi(r)=\tfrac12(r-1)^2\), suppose
\[1+\frac{\sqrt{2\rho}}{\sigma}(\ell_i-\mu)>0\quad\text{for every }i.\]
Then the nonnegativity constraints on the worst-case probabilities are inactive and
\[\sup_{q\in\Delta_n}\left\{q^\top\ell:\frac12\sum_i p_i(q_i/p_i-1)^2\le\rho\right\}=\mu+\sqrt{2\rho}\,\sigma.\]
A maximizing distribution is
\[q_i^*=p_i\left[1+\frac{\sqrt{2\rho}}{\sigma}(\ell_i-\mu)\right].\]
When this strict interior condition fails, boundary probabilities may invalidate the simple mean-standard-deviation formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the chi-square optimizer has strictly positive scenario probabilities, the robust expectation equals the nominal mean plus a radius-scaled standard deviation; outside that interior regime, boundary probabilities may invalidate the formula.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell\in\mathbb R^n\) and its nominal variance \(\sigma^2\) is positive.
The displayed strict componentwise interior condition holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chi-square robust expectation is \(\mu+\sqrt{2\rho}\,\sigma\), with the displayed strictly positive optimizer \(q^*\).

notation.meaning: Nominal mean of the scenario loss.
Nominal standard deviation of the scenario loss.
Worst-case probability vector in the strict interior regime.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: ellipsoidal chi-square perturbations yield a support function proportional to nominal standard deviation when probability nonnegativity is inactive

children.title: Divergence–Variance Correspondence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where divergence robustification admits a variance-oriented interpretation.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a probability measure and \(f\in L^2(P)\).
\(\phi\) is twice differentiable near \(1\), with \(\phi(1)=\phi'(1)=0\) and \(\phi''(1)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\phi(\eta;f,P)=\mathbb E_P[f]+\sqrt{2\eta\operatorname{Var}_P(f)/\phi''(1)}+o(\sqrt{\eta})\).

notation.meaning: phi-divergence ball of radius eta around P
worst-case expectation over the divergence ball

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local small-radius regime for smooth \(\phi\)-divergences and square-integrable losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U_{\phi,\eta}(P)=\{Q\ll P:D_\phi(Q\|P)\leq\eta\}\) and \(R_\phi(\eta;f,P)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal U_{\phi,\eta}(P)}\mathbb E_Q[f]\). Under regularity ensuring admissible local density perturbations, as \(\eta\downarrow0\),
\[
R_\phi(\eta;f,P)=\mathbb E_P[f]+\sqrt{\frac{2\eta}{\phi''(1)}\operatorname{Var}_P(f)}+o(\sqrt{\eta}).
\]
Thus smooth divergence robustification induces a leading standard-deviation penalty; nonsmooth divergences or active density constraints can produce different regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For small smooth divergence balls, worst-case expectation equals nominal expectation plus a leading standard-deviation penalty whose coefficient depends on divergence curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Divergence–Variance Correspondence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The small-radius variance expansion fits the regime container, but “regularity ensuring admissible local density perturbations” is not a checkable hypothesis and no authoritative source or locator supports the expansion or its failure regimes.

children.title: Wasserstein Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization effects induced by Wasserstein ambiguity sets.

assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,d)\) is a metric space and \(P\) is a probability measure with finite first moment.
\(f:\Xi\to\mathbb R\) is integrable under every distribution considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_\rho(f;P)=\sup_{Q:W_1(Q,P)\leq\rho}\mathbb E_Q[f]\).

notation.meaning: order-one Wasserstein distance induced by d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-one Wasserstein robustification of an expected loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For radius \(\rho\geq0\), define the Wasserstein ambiguity set and its robust risk by
\[
\mathcal U_\rho(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P_1(\Xi):W_1(Q,P)\leq\rho\},\qquad
\mathcal R_\rho(f;P)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal U_\rho(P)}\mathbb E_Q[f].
\]
The excess \(\mathcal R_\rho(f;P)-\mathbb E_P[f]\) is the Wasserstein regularization term associated with \(f\), \(P\), \(d\), and \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wasserstein regularization is the increase from nominal to worst-case expected loss over a Wasserstein ball around the reference distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Wasserstein Regularization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Wasserstein Regularization and is internally consistent, but it has no cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Lipschitz Regularization
children.top_down_role: Penalty interpretations governed by loss sensitivity to perturbations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\Xi\to\mathbb R\) has finite global Lipschitz modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Reg}_{\mathrm{Lip},\rho}(f)=\rho\operatorname{Lip}_d(f)\).

notation.meaning: global Lipschitz modulus with respect to d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global Lipschitz penalty paired with order-one transport cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The global Lipschitz modulus of \(f\) is
\[
\operatorname{Lip}_d(f)=\sup_{x\neq y}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|}{d(x,y)}.
\]
For \(\rho\geq0\), the associated Lipschitz regularization functional is
\[
\operatorname{Reg}_{\mathrm{Lip},\rho}(f)=\rho\operatorname{Lip}_d(f).
\]
It penalizes sensitivity of the loss to displacement in the same metric that defines the transport ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz regularization multiplies the loss's global metric sensitivity by the transport radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Regularization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The radius-scaled Lipschitz functional fits the leaf and the definition kind, but no cited source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Transport–Lipschitz Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Conditions supporting a correspondence between transport robustness and Lipschitz penalties.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{Q:W_1(Q,P)\leq\rho}\mathbb E_Q[f]\leq\mathbb E_P[f]+\rho L\), with equality for affine losses on normed vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General transport upper bound, with exactness stated only for affine normed-space losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Kantorovich duality implies
\[
\mathbb E_Q[f]-\mathbb E_P[f]\leq L W_1(Q,P),
\qquad
\sup_{Q:W_1(Q,P)\leq\rho}\mathbb E_Q[f]
\leq\mathbb E_P[f]+\rho L.
\]
If \(\Xi\) is a normed vector space, \(d(x,y)=\|x-y\|\), and \(f(x)=a^\top x+b\), then \(L=\|a\|_*\) and the bound is exact whenever the required translated distributions remain admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transport duality bounds Wasserstein worst-case risk by nominal risk plus radius times Lipschitz modulus; affine losses attain the bound under suitable support conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Transport–Lipschitz Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inequality matches the correspondence leaf, but it is a theorem/property rather than merely a representation. The affine exactness clause also requires precise support, moment, and admissibility conditions backed by a source.

children.title: Correspondence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss, metric, or support regimes where the regularization interpretation breaks down.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{Q:W_1(Q,P)\leq\rho}\mathbb E_Q[f]=1<\rho=\mathbb E_P[f]+\rho\operatorname{Lip}(f)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of exact radius-times-Lipschitz regularization for bounded losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Here \(\operatorname{Lip}(f)=1\) and \(0\leq f\leq1\). For \(\rho>1\), the distribution \(Q=\delta_1\) satisfies \(W_1(Q,P)=1\leq\rho\), so
\[
\sup_{Q:W_1(Q,P)\leq\rho}\mathbb E_Q[f]=1.
\]
However,
\[
\mathbb E_P[f]+\rho\operatorname{Lip}(f)=\rho>1.
\]
Therefore the Lipschitz expression is generally an upper bound, not an exact regularization identity, without additional geometry and loss assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded one-Lipschitz loss saturates at one, so for large Wasserstein radii the radius-times-Lipschitz formula strictly overestimates robust risk.
knowledge_statements.title: Correspondence Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically coherent and correctly fits a failure-boundary container, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Transport Robustification
children.top_down_role: Distributional perturbations represented through transport-based ambiguity.

assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,d)\) is a Polish metric space and \(P\) is a probability measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T_\varepsilon(\theta)=\sup_{Q:W_\infty(Q,P)\leq\varepsilon}\mathbb E_Q[\ell_\theta]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise-budget transport robustification represented by an infinity-Wasserstein ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), define
\[
W_\infty(Q,P)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{(x,z)\sim\pi}d(x,z),
\qquad
\mathcal T_\varepsilon(\theta)=\sup_{Q:W_\infty(Q,P)\leq\varepsilon}\mathbb E_Q[\ell_\theta(Z)].
\]
Thus every admissible distribution must admit a coupling with \(P\) whose transported samples move by at most \(\varepsilon\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transport robustification maximizes expected loss over distributions coupled to the data distribution by uniformly bounded sample displacements.
knowledge_statements.title: Transport Robustification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Transport Robustification, but measurability alone for an extended-real loss does not ensure that every displayed expectation is well defined. A source and precise integrability convention are required.

children.title: Adversarial Training
children.top_down_role: Learning formulations based on adversarial perturbation exposure.

assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,d)\) is a metric sample space with reference distribution \(P\).
\(\ell_\theta\) is measurable and the pointwise supremum is integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon(\theta)=\mathbb E_{X\sim P}[\sup_{d(z,X)\leq\varepsilon}\ell_\theta(z)]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population adversarial training with a metric perturbation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_\varepsilon(x)=\{z\in\Xi:d(z,x)\leq\varepsilon\}\). The population adversarial-training objective is
\[
\mathcal A_\varepsilon(\theta)=
\mathbb E_{X\sim P}\left[\sup_{z\in B_\varepsilon(X)}\ell_\theta(z)\right].
\]
An adversarially trained parameter minimizes this quantity over its feasible parameter set; empirical adversarial training replaces \(P\) by the empirical distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adversarial training minimizes the expected worst loss obtained by perturbing each sample within a prescribed metric ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Training

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The population objective fits the Adversarial Training leaf and its definition kind, but it lacks a source with an inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prediction-stability regularization using unlabeled data, including its label-preserving perturbation condition, stopped-target convention, virtual-adversarial variant, and excessive-weight failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For labeled data $\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^M$, unlabeled data $\{x_j\}_{j=1}^N$, and samples $x'_j\sim q(\cdot\mid x_j)$, a common consistency-regularized objective is
\[\mathcal L(\theta)=-\sum_{i=1}^M\log p_\theta(y_i\mid x_i)+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^N\left\|\operatorname{sg}\!\left(p_\theta(\cdot\mid x_j)\right)-p_\theta(\cdot\mid x'_j)\right\|_2^2,\]
where the unperturbed prediction is typically treated as fixed for differentiation. Transformations should generally preserve the true label. In virtual adversarial training, a perturbation direction is approximated by increasing $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_\theta(\cdot\mid x)\|p_\theta(\cdot\mid x+\delta))$, after which $x'=x+\epsilon\delta/\|\delta\|_2$. If $\lambda$ is too large, particularly early in training, the model can reinforce erroneous predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistency regularization penalizes changes in a model's prediction under stochastic input or model perturbations, usually stopping gradients through the unperturbed prediction. Input transformations should generally preserve labels. Virtual adversarial training instead searches approximately for a perturbation that changes the prediction maximally. Excessive consistency weight can amplify early prediction errors.
assumptions_latex: q(\cdot\mid x)\text{ is generally intended to produce label-preserving transformations}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_\theta\left[-\sum_{i=1}^M\log p_\theta(y_i\mid x_i)+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^N\left\|\operatorname{sg}(p_\theta(\cdot\mid x_j))-p_\theta(\cdot\mid x'_j)\right\|_2^2\right].

source_evidence.locator: Learning with Fewer Labeled Examples / 19. Learning with Fewer Labeled Examples / Definition 19-extra-20

source_refs.locator: Learning with Fewer Labeled Examples / 19. Learning with Fewer Labeled Examples / Definition 19-extra-20

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency Regularization for Semi-Supervised Learning

source_witnesses.locator: Learning with Fewer Labeled Examples / 19. Learning with Fewer Labeled Examples / Definition 19-extra-20

directory_assessment.rationale: The general principle belongs under semi-supervised learning, which is absent from the packet. The adversarial-training candidate is relevant only to the VAT specialization and is not a valid primary home.

children.title: Robustification–Training Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Modeling regimes where transport robustness corresponds to adversarial training.

assumptions_latex: \(\Xi\) is Polish, \(P\) is a Borel probability measure, and perturbation balls are measurable.
\(\ell_\theta\) is upper semianalytic, bounded above, or otherwise satisfies valid measurable-selection and integrability conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{Q:W_\infty(Q,P)\leq\varepsilon}\mathbb E_Q[\ell_\theta]=\mathbb E_P[\sup_{d(z,X)\leq\varepsilon}\ell_\theta(z)]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population equivalence under an infinity-transport budget and measurable selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated measurability and selection hypotheses,
\[
\sup_{Q:W_\infty(Q,P)\leq\varepsilon}\mathbb E_Q[\ell_\theta(Z)]
=
\mathbb E_{X\sim P}\left[\sup_{z:d(z,X)\leq\varepsilon}\ell_\theta(z)\right].
\]
Consequently, minimizing the infinity-Wasserstein robust risk over \(\theta\) is equivalent to population adversarial training with the same metric and radius. The identity concerns objective values; attainment requires an admissible measurable maximizing selector or an appropriate limiting argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With matching metrics and uniform transport budgets, infinity-Wasserstein robust risk equals the population pointwise adversarial-loss objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Robustification–Training Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem belongs in the equivalence leaf, but “bounded above, or otherwise satisfies” does not state a determinate sufficient hypothesis. The equality and any nonattainment/selection qualification require an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Perturbation-Mismatch Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where distributional transport and samplewise adversaries encode different uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_1(Q,P)=\varepsilon\) while \(W_\infty(Q,P)=M>\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mismatch between average transport budgets and pointwise adversarial perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The unique transport from \(P\) sends mass \(\varepsilon/M\) from \(0\) to \(M\), giving
\[
W_1(Q,P)=\frac{\varepsilon}{M}M=\varepsilon,
\qquad
W_\infty(Q,P)=M>\varepsilon.
\]
Hence \(Q\) belongs to the order-one Wasserstein ball of radius \(\varepsilon\) but not to the pointwise-budget ambiguity set. Therefore order-one transport robustification is not generally equivalent to adversarial training with radius \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An average transport budget can move a small mass arbitrarily far, whereas pointwise adversarial training forbids every displacement beyond its radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Mismatch Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly distinguishes average and uniform transport budgets and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but it has no supporting citation or locator.

assumptions_latex: The robust risk and proposed regularizer are finite on the parameter domain.
Their ambiguity geometry, loss class, and support restrictions are explicitly fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R(\theta)\leq\mathbb E_P[\ell_\theta]+\Omega(\theta)\) does not imply equality; exact equivalence requires zero duality and relaxation gaps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General boundary separating exact reformulations from upper bounds and asymptotic correspondences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An asserted regularization equivalence requires
\[
\mathcal R(\theta)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal U(P)}\mathbb E_Q[\ell_\theta]
=
\mathbb E_P[\ell_\theta]+\Omega(\theta)
\]
on the stated parameter domain. A one-sided sensitivity bound, a small-radius expansion, or a dual relaxation establishes only an inequality or approximation. Exactness can fail through support restrictions, nonattainment, mismatched transport budgets, nonsmooth divergence geometry, or a loss class that cannot realize the relevant dual extremizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robustification equals regularization only when the dual representation is exact; bounds, asymptotics, support restrictions, and mismatched geometries mark failure boundaries.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization-Equivalence Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content fits the boundary topic, but exact robustification–regularization equality is not characterized solely by zero duality and relaxation gaps; representation and model-matching conditions also matter. The proposed boundary taxonomy needs authoritative support.

children.title: Linear Optimization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: DRO reformulations representable through linear optimization.

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set is \(\mathcal U=\{q\in\mathbb R^m:Aq\leq b,\ q\geq0,\ \mathbf1^\top q=1\}\) and is nonempty.
The scenario-loss vector \(c(x)\in\mathbb R^m\) is affine in the decision \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{q\in\mathcal U}c(x)^\top q\) has an exact linear-programming primal-dual interface under LP strong duality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario DRO with a polyhedral probability ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(x\), the worst-case expectation is the linear program
\[
\sup_{q\geq0}\{c(x)^\top q:Aq\leq b,\ \mathbf1^\top q=1\}.
\]
Its dual is
\[
\inf_{y\geq0,\,\nu\in\mathbb R}\{b^\top y+\nu:A^\top y+\nu\mathbf1\geq c(x)\}.
\]
When the primal is feasible with finite value, linear-programming strong duality makes the dual constraints and objective an exact deterministic linear optimization interface for the DRO term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-scenario DRO problem with polyhedral probability ambiguity has an exact linear-programming reformulation through the dual of its worst-case expectation problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Optimization Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LP primal–dual representation fits the linear-interface leaf and its signs are consistent, but the dimensions of A and b are not introduced and no LP/DRO source locator is supplied.

children.title: Second-Order-Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: DRO reformulations representable through second-order-cone optimization.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty vector has representation \(u=u_0+Bz\) with \(\|z\|_2\leq\rho\).
The uncertain scalar expression is affine: \(a(x)+g(x)^\top u\), with affine \(a\) and \(g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+g(x)^\top u_0+\rho\|B^\top g(x)\|_2\leq0\) is an exact SOC robust counterpart.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ellipsoidal uncertainty in an affine robust constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The robust constraint
\[
a(x)+g(x)^\top(u_0+Bz)\leq0\quad\text{for every }\|z\|_2\leq\rho
\]
is equivalent, by the Euclidean support function, to
\[
a(x)+g(x)^\top u_0+\rho\|B^\top g(x)\|_2\leq0.
\]
Introducing \(t\) yields the second-order-cone interface
\[
\|B^\top g(x)\|_2\leq t,\qquad a(x)+g(x)^\top u_0+\rho t\leq0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine constraint robustified over an ellipsoid becomes an exact second-order-cone constraint through the ellipsoid's support function.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-function reformulation correctly has SOC form and fits the interface leaf, but the spaces and dimensions of u, z, B, and g(x) are not specified, and no authoritative locator supports the claim.

children.title: Linear-to-Conic Escalation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural features that require moving from linear to second-order-cone representations.

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity-set description and loss epigraph are finite-dimensional and admit exact strong conic duality.
All uncertainty-set and moment data are represented without approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The smallest exact interface is linear in the polyhedral regime, second-order-conic when only norm or ellipsoidal epigraphs are added, and genuinely nonpolyhedral conic beyond those regimes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between LP and genuinely conic exact DRO reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an epigraph constraint \(t\geq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\). Its exact reformulation remains a linear program when dualizing \(\mathcal P\) produces finitely many affine inequalities and \(\ell\) has a polyhedral epigraph. It escalates to a second-order-cone program when every additional nonlinear condition is representable by norm epigraphs or Schur complements of arrow matrices. If exact dual feasibility instead requires a general positive-semidefinite matrix, a relative-entropy epigraph, or integrality, an LP or SOCP formulation is unavailable in general; the appropriate interface is respectively semidefinite, exponential-conic, or mixed-integer conic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact DRO models are linear only under polyhedral structure; norms require SOC constraints, while general matrix positivity, entropy, or discrete decisions require stronger interfaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-to-Conic Escalation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary classification fits the leaf, but the asserted exact LP/SOCP limitations and escalation to SDP, exponential-conic, or mixed-integer interfaces require inspectable sources and precise representability qualifications.

children.title: Semidefinite Optimization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: DRO reformulations expressed through positive-semidefinite constraints.

assumptions_latex: The generalized moment problem and its conic dual satisfy strong duality.
Every quadratic nonnegativity condition is certified exactly by the stated semidefinite representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The DRO epigraph is represented by affine equalities and inequalities together with \(F_0+\sum_j z_jF_j\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SDP interfaces arising from moment duality and quadratic nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a moment-based ambiguity set, dualization of \(t\geq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\) yields finitely many scalar dual variables \(z\) and a pointwise majorization condition. When that condition is quadratic in \(\xi\) and admits an exact quadratic nonnegativity certificate, it can be written as \(F_0(x,t)+\sum_j z_jF_j\succeq0\), together with affine restrictions on \((x,t,z)\). Thus the DRO epigraph is the projection of a spectrahedron. General positive-semidefinite constraints of unbounded block size cannot, without additional structure, be replaced exactly by finitely many linear or second-order-cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment duality converts suitable quadratic DRO constraints into affine matrix inequalities, making the robust epigraph a projection of a spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Optimization Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the SDP-interface leaf, but no source supports the exact moment-duality certificate or the claimed impossibility of finite LP/SOCP replacement for general PSD constraints.

children.title: Exponential-Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: DRO reformulations expressed through exponential-cone constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support KL-divergence ambiguity with the closed exponential-cone convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal P=\{p\geq0:\sum_i p_i=1,\ D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)\leq\rho\}\). Then
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_i p_i l_i
=
\inf_{\eta\geq0,\,\lambda\in\mathbb R}
\left\{\eta\rho+\lambda+\eta\sum_i q_i\left[\exp\!\left(\frac{l_i-\lambda}{\eta}\right)-1\right]\right\},
\]
where the objective at \(\eta=0\) is interpreted by closure. Introducing \(s_i\) with \((l_i-\lambda,\eta,s_i)\in K_{\exp}\) and imposing \(t\geq\eta\rho+\lambda+\sum_i q_i s_i-\eta\) gives an exact exponential-cone epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite KL-divergence DRO expectation has a dual formulation whose corrected exponential terms admit an exact exponential-cone epigraph.
assumptions_latex: The nominal probabilities satisfy \(q_i>0\) and \(\sum_i q_i=1\).
The ambiguity radius satisfies \(\rho\geq0\), and every loss \(l_i\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The worst-case expectation over a finite Kullback--Leibler ball has an exact exponential-cone representation.

children.title: Cone-Selection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity and loss structures determining the appropriate conic interface.

assumptions_latex: The reformulation is required to be exact and finite-dimensional.
No special simultaneous diagonalization or finite enumeration structure is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polyhedral, norm, matrix-positivity, and entropy primitives determine LP, SOCP, SDP, and exponential-cone interfaces, respectively.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary for choosing an exact finite-dimensional DRO cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact DRO reformulation uses an LP interface when all primitive epigraphs and dual feasibility sets are polyhedral. It uses an SOCP interface when its nonpolyhedral primitives reduce to finitely many Euclidean-norm inequalities. A general affine constraint in \(\mathbb S_+^m\) requires an SDP interface unless additional structure reduces it to smaller cones. Relative-entropy or log-sum-exp epigraphs require the exponential cone unless they are approximated. Consequently, replacing SDP or exponential-cone primitives by LP or SOCP constraints without such structure changes the feasible set in general; mixed primitive families require a product-cone interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algebraic primitives of the exact reformulation determine the cone; general PSD and entropy constraints do not reduce exactly to LP or SOCP form.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Selection Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but claims that PSD and entropy primitives require particular cones and cannot reduce to LP/SOCP need authoritative nonrepresentability support and explicit treatment of special cases.

assumptions_latex: The continuous conic constraints are closed and convex for each fixed integer vector.
All integer-variable bounds and cone data are explicitly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting DRO reformulation is a mixed-integer conic program over a product of the required closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conic DRO reformulations containing discrete first-stage or logical decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose dualization of a DRO model with discrete decisions produces affine-conic constraints. Its interface has the form
\[
\min_{x,y,z}\ \{c^\top x+d^\top y:\ A x+B y+G z-b\in K,\ y\in\mathbb Z^p,\ \ell\leq y\leq u\},
\]
where \(K\) is a product of nonnegative, second-order, positive-semidefinite, or exponential cones and \(z\) contains dual and lifting variables. Fixing \(y\) leaves a convex conic subproblem. Integrality is essential whenever admissible policies, selections, or logical alternatives are discrete; relaxing \(y\in\mathbb Z^p\) to its continuous bounds generally yields only a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete DRO decisions combined with an exact conic reformulation produce a mixed-integer conic model; fixing the integers leaves a convex conic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Conic Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed-integer conic representation is mathematically plausible and matches the topic, but no inspectable source supports its DRO specialization or the stated relaxation interpretation.

children.title: Exchange Methods
children.top_down_role: Finite-restriction schemes centered on active distributional or constraint elements.

assumptions_latex: The set \(X\) is nonempty, and every finite restricted master problem attains a minimizer.
An exact maximization oracle for \(\max_{u\in U}g(x,u)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the returned point is \(\varepsilon\)-feasible for every semi-infinite constraint.

notation.meaning: active finite index set at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exchange algorithm for a semi-infinite convex constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\) subject to \(g(x,u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in U\), choose a finite \(U_0\subset U\). At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted master with constraints \(g(x,u)\leq0\) for \(u\in U_k\), obtaining \(x_k\). Compute \(u_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in U}g(x_k,u)\). If \(g(x_k,u_k)\leq\varepsilon\), stop and return \(x_k\). Otherwise set \(U_{k+1}=U_k\cup\{u_k\}\) and repeat. Hence the stopping test directly certifies \(g(x_k,u)\leq\varepsilon\) for all \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exchange methods repeatedly solve a finite restriction and add its most violated index until the oracle certifies global approximate feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Exchange Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and stopping certificate fit Exchange Methods, but the exact-oracle exchange scheme has no cited source.

children.title: Cutting-Plane Methods
children.top_down_role: Outer-approximation schemes based on successively generated separating cuts.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(X\) is closed and convex.
The violation function \(\phi(x)=\sup_{u\in U}g(x,u)\) is finite and convex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated affine inequality is valid for \(\{x\in X:\phi(x)\leq0\}\), and the stopping test certifies \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-approximation cutting planes for a convex semi-infinite feasibility function.

source_refs.locator: 1.8.2.1 Cutting-plane methods p. 90

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize a master problem over \(X\). At iteration \(k\), solve it to obtain \(x_k\), evaluate \(\phi(x_k)\), and stop if \(\phi(x_k)\leq\varepsilon\). Otherwise choose \(s_k\in\partial\phi(x_k)\) and add the valid cut
\[
\phi(x_k)+s_k^\top(x-x_k)\leq0.
\]
Convexity implies that every point satisfying \(\phi(x)\leq0\) obeys this cut. The master therefore remains an outer approximation of the feasible region, while the oracle evaluation supplies the stopping certificate. A bounded master or another rule preventing unbounded trial points is required for implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cutting-plane method separates an infeasible trial point using a subgradient of the maximum-violation function and stops when violation is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutting-Plane Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 1.8.2.1 Cutting-plane methods p. 90

children.title: Exchange–Cut Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Representations under which exchanged elements induce cutting planes or vice versa.

assumptions_latex: For every \(u\in U\), the function \(g(\cdot,u)\) is affine.
The violation oracle returns an index attaining \(\phi(x)=\max_{u\in U}g(x,u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding the exchanged constraint indexed by \(u_k\) is identical to adding the corresponding supporting cut of \(\phi\) at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence for affine-in-decision semi-infinite constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x,u)=a(u)^\top x-b(u)\) and \(\phi(x)=\max_{u\in U}g(x,u)\). If \(u_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in U}g(x_k,u)\), then \(a(u_k)\in\partial\phi(x_k)\). The cutting-plane inequality generated at \(x_k\) is
\[
\phi(x_k)+a(u_k)^\top(x-x_k)\leq0,
\]
which simplifies exactly to \(g(x,u_k)\leq0\). Thus an exchange step and a maximum-violation cutting-plane step add the same master constraint. When \(g(\cdot,u)\) is nonlinear, an exchanged constraint and its affine supporting cut need not coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For affine indexed constraints, the most violated exchanged constraint is exactly the subgradient cut of the maximum-violation function; nonlinear constraints break this identity.
knowledge_statements.title: Exchange–Cut Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine exchange–cut identity is precise and fits the correspondence leaf, but no citation supports the stated equivalence or its nonlinear boundary.

children.title: Finite-Termination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem structures supporting finite identification of a sufficient restricted model.

assumptions_latex: There exists a finite set \(U^\star\subset U\) such that \(\max_{u\in U}g(x,u)=\max_{u\in U^\star}g(x,u)\) for every \(x\in X\).
Restricted masters and the maximization oracle are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exchange method adding a previously absent violated maximizer terminates after at most \(|U^\star|\) successful additions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination under a finite determining family and exact oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(U^\star\) is finite and determines every maximum violation. Whenever the current restricted solution is not \(\varepsilon\)-feasible, let the oracle return a violated maximizer in \(U^\star\) that is absent from the master, and add it permanently. Each unsuccessful iteration therefore inserts a distinct element of \(U^\star\). After at most \(|U^\star\setminus U_0|\) additions, the master contains the determining family and its optimizer is globally feasible, so the next oracle call terminates. Without a finite determining family, exact arithmetic alone does not imply finite termination; only asymptotic or tolerance-based convergence may remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exchange terminates finitely when a finite family determines all violations and each failed iteration adds a new member; infinite determining families remove that guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Termination Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-determining-family argument supports the stated addition bound and the complexity-bound kind fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for this termination regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributional Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column generation over adversarial distributions in a DRO epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To minimize \(f(x)+t\) subject to \(t\geq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[L(x,\xi)]\), initialize a finite \(\mathcal P_0\subset\mathcal P\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master with \(t\geq\mathbb E_P[L(x,\xi)]\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_k\), obtaining \((x_k,t_k)\). A pricing oracle computes \(P_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[L(x_k,\xi)]\). Stop if \(\mathbb E_{P_k}[L(x_k,\xi)]\leq t_k+\varepsilon\); otherwise set \(\mathcal P_{k+1}=\mathcal P_k\cup\{P_k\}\). The stopping test certifies the robust epigraph constraint within \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributional column generation adds a worst-case distribution to a restricted DRO master until no omitted distribution violates its epigraph beyond tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) is convex and its relevant extreme distributions can be generated by an exact pricing oracle.
Every restricted master problem attains an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm stops when no distribution violates the robust epigraph by more than \(\varepsilon\).

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) is nonempty.
The loss \(L(x,\cdot)\) is integrable under every \(P\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle output and upper bound certify an additive \(\varepsilon\)-solution of the inner worst-case distribution problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive certificate for a worst-case expectation oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed decision \(x\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), a certified worst-case distribution oracle returns \(\widehat P\in\mathcal P\) and a scalar \(U\) satisfying
\[
\mathbb E_{\widehat P}[L(x,\xi)]\leq
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[L(x,\xi)]
\leq U
\quad\text{and}\quad
U-\mathbb E_{\widehat P}[L(x,\xi)]\leq\varepsilon.
\]
The feasible distribution supplies a verifiable lower bound on the inner supremum, while a valid dual solution may supply \(U\). Their gap certifies additive \(\varepsilon\)-optimality; returning only a candidate distribution without an upper bound does not provide this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified worst-case oracle returns a feasible adversarial distribution and a valid upper bound whose gap is at most the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Distribution Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower/upper-bound gap is a valid additive certificate and the content kind fits, but the proposed worst-case oracle contract lacks an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Worst-case expected-performance objective over a distribution ambiguity set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a distributionally robust maximization objective and records the stated conditions for a confidence-bound method's convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) of probability measures on the environment space, define \(f(x)=\inf_{p\in\mathcal P}\int g(x,\omega)p(\omega)\,\mathrm d\omega\). Maximizing \(f\) seeks the decision with greatest expected performance under its worst admissible environment distribution. A confidence-bound method for this model has convergence guarantees under the stated technical conditions that \(g\) has bounded RKHS norm and every admissible distribution has bounded maximum mean discrepancy from a reference distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributionally robust decision maximizes expected performance evaluated under the least favorable probability distribution in an ambiguity set. The reported confidence-bound method requires bounded RKHS norm for the performance function and a bounded maximum-mean-discrepancy neighborhood of a reference distribution for its convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal P\) is a set of probability measures on the environment space
\(\int g(x,\omega)p(\omega)\,\mathrm d\omega\) is well-defined for \(x\in X\) and \(p\in\mathcal P\)
For the stated confidence-bound convergence guarantee, \(\lVert g\rVert_{\mathcal H}<\infty\) in the relevant RKHS
For the stated confidence-bound convergence guarantee, the maximum mean discrepancy from a reference distribution is bounded over \(\mathcal P\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \max_{x\in X}\inf_{p\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_{\omega\sim p}[g(x,\omega)]\) maximizes worst-case expected performance over \(\mathcal P\).

children.title: Benders DRO Methods
children.top_down_role: DRO decomposition organized around master problems and subproblem information.

assumptions_latex: For every realization, the recourse problem is feasible, bounded, and has strong linear or conic duality.
The ambiguity-set oracle and all master subproblems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each generated inequality is a valid lower cut for the worst-case recourse function, and the master-oracle gap provides the stopping test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multicut or aggregated Benders decomposition for two-stage DRO with dualizable recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in X}c^\top x+\Psi(x)\), where \(\Psi(x)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\). Initialize a master in \((x,\theta)\). At iteration \(k\), solve it for \((x_k,\theta_k)\), call a worst-case distribution oracle at \(x_k\), and solve the associated recourse duals. Their optimal dual solutions yield an affine function \(\alpha_k^\top x+\beta_k\leq\Psi(x)\). If the certified upper estimate of \(\Psi(x_k)\) exceeds \(\theta_k\) by more than \(\varepsilon\), add \(\theta\geq\alpha_k^\top x+\beta_k\); otherwise return \(x_k\). Feasibility cuts are added analogously when recourse is not complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Benders DRO alternates a first-stage master with worst-case distribution and recourse-dual oracles, adding valid affine cuts until the certified gap closes.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders DRO Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Benders DRO Methods, but no source supports the construction of a globally valid affine lower cut from the distribution and recourse duals or the stated master-oracle stopping criterion.

children.title: L-Shaped DRO Methods
children.top_down_role: Scenario-structured DRO decomposition using L-shaped architectures.

knowledge_statements.title: L-Shaped DRO Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support two-stage DRO with linear recourse and a tractable ambiguity set over scenario probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x)\}\), initialize lower recourse models \(\underline Q_s^0\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master problem obtained by replacing each \(Q_s\) with \(\underline Q_s^k\). For its optimizer \(x^k\), solve every scenario recourse problem and its dual. Add \(Q_s(x)\ge \pi_s^\top(h_s-T_sx)\) for each dual optimizer \(\pi_s\), or a feasibility cut from a dual ray when recourse is infeasible. Stop when the incumbent upper bound minus the master lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\), and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteratively solve a distributionally robust master problem, evaluate scenario recourse, and add dual optimality or feasibility cuts until the certified bound gap is within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal P\subseteq\{p\in\mathbb R_+^S:\mathbf1^\top p=1\}\) are tractably representable.
Each \(Q_s(x)\) is a linear-programming recourse value with strong duality.
Master and scenario subproblems attain the values used in the stopping bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the returned incumbent has certified objective gap at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Optimal recourse value in scenario s.
Ambiguity set of scenario probability vectors.
Maximum of scenario cuts accumulated by iteration k.

children.title: Benders–L-Shaped Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between general Benders decompositions and L-shaped variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders–L-Shaped Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence for finite-scenario linear two-stage models after introducing scenario-recourse epigraph variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the deterministic equivalent of a finite-scenario two-stage linear DRO model, introduce epigraph variables \(\theta_s\ge Q_s(x)\). Benders decomposition with \(x\) and \(\theta=(\theta_s)_{s=1}^S\) in the master produces, from each recourse dual optimizer \(\pi_s\), the cut \(\theta_s\ge\pi_s^\top(h_s-T_sx)\). These are exactly the scenario optimality cuts of the multicut L-shaped method; dual extreme rays produce the same feasibility cuts. Aggregating scenario cuts yields the single-cut L-shaped variant when the ambiguity-weighted aggregation is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: L-shaped cuts are Benders cuts applied to the scenario-recourse epigraph of a two-stage model; multicut and valid aggregated forms differ only in cut aggregation.
assumptions_latex: The model has finite scenarios and linear recourse satisfying strong duality.
The ambiguity-weighted recourse epigraph is represented exactly in the master.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Applicability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for exact Benders or L-shaped decomposition of finite-support two-stage DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Benders–L-shaped decomposition is directly applicable when: \(\mathcal P\) has a finite-dimensional tractable representation; for fixed \(x\), the recourse value separates as \((Q_s(x))_{s=1}^S\); every recourse problem is a linear program with an attained dual value or a detectable infeasibility ray; and \(\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_s p_s\theta_s\) can be evaluated or represented in the master. Relatively complete recourse eliminates feasibility cuts but is not required when valid ray cuts are available.

assumptions_latex: The DRO model has finitely many scenarios.
First-stage and ambiguity-set constraints remain in a tractable master problem.

children.title: Column Generation
children.top_down_role: Restricted-master approaches that introduce distributional or decision columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atom generation for a moment-constrained worst-case distribution problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\sup_{\mu\ge0}\{\int_\Xi g(\xi)\,d\mu(\xi):\int_\Xi a(\xi)\,d\mu(\xi)=b\}\). Initialize a finite atom set \(V_0\subset\Xi\). At iteration \(k\), solve the measure problem restricted to \(V_k\) and obtain a dual vector \(y^k\). Compute \(r^k=\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}\{g(\xi)-a(\xi)^\top y^k\}\). If \(r^k\le\varepsilon\), return the restricted distribution and \(y^k\); otherwise choose an atom attaining positive reduced cost and set \(V_{k+1}=V_k\cup\{\xi^k\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a restricted worst-case distribution problem and repeatedly add an atom having positive reduced cost until the pricing violation is within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The initial restricted problem is feasible.
Restricted master problems attain primal and dual optima.
The pricing supremum is attained or an admissible approximate maximizer is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(r^k\le\varepsilon\), \(y^k\) is dual feasible within \(\varepsilon\) in reduced-cost violation.

notation.meaning: Atoms present in the restricted master problem.
Maximum reduced cost returned by pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange method for the semi-infinite dual of a moment-based DRO problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_y\{b^\top y:a(\xi)^\top y\ge g(\xi)\ \text{for all }\xi\in\Xi\}\), initialize a finite set \(V_0\subset\Xi\). At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted problem containing constraints only for \(\xi\in V_k\), obtaining \(y^k\). Compute \(v^k=\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}\{g(\xi)-a(\xi)^\top y^k\}\). If \(v^k\le\varepsilon\), return \(y^k\); otherwise select a violating \(\xi^k\) and set \(V_{k+1}=V_k\cup\{\xi^k\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a finite relaxation of the semi-infinite DRO dual and add its most violated uncertainty constraint.
assumptions_latex: Every restricted master problem is feasible and attains its optimum.
The separation problem can return a maximizer or a certified upper bound.

children.title: Coupled Generation Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Generation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which column and constraint generation must be coordinated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Coupled generation applies when a DRO reformulation contains both a restricted representation \(\mu=\sum_{\xi\in V}w_\xi\delta_\xi\) and constraints indexed by all \(\xi\in\Xi\), and a common oracle evaluates \(g(\xi)-a(\xi)^\top y\). At each major iteration, the restricted primal and dual must be solved consistently; any oracle point with positive reduced cost is added as a column, and any point violating dual feasibility is added as a constraint. Termination is valid only when both residuals are at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled generation is required when restricted distribution atoms and semi-infinite dual constraints coexist; termination requires both pricing and separation residuals to be small.
assumptions_latex: Restricted primal and dual formulations share the same uncertainty index set \(\Xi\).
The pricing and separation oracle supplies certified residual bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If both generation residuals are at most \(\varepsilon\), neither omitted atoms nor omitted indexed constraints improve the relaxation beyond the prescribed tolerance.

notation.meaning: Dirac probability measure at uncertainty point xi.

children.title: Generation Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Pricing, separation, or master-growth limitations affecting generation schemes.

knowledge_statements.title: Generation Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle and degeneracy boundaries for column-constraint generation in DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Generation loses an exact termination certificate if the oracle cannot certify \(\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}\{g(\xi)-a(\xi)^\top y\}\). In particular, if this maximization is nonconvex or NP-hard, polynomial-time restricted-master solves do not imply polynomial-time DRO solution. If an oracle returns only a local maximizer with nonpositive value while some omitted \(\hat\xi\) satisfies \(g(\hat\xi)-a(\hat\xi)^\top y>0\), the method may terminate at a nonoptimal restricted solution. Degeneracy may additionally generate many atoms or constraints without appreciable bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard or uncertified pricing can cause false termination, while degeneracy can force many nearly redundant generated objects and dominate runtime.
assumptions_latex: Termination is based on the sign or magnitude of an oracle residual.
The oracle is not guaranteed to solve the global separation problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonpositive local residual alone does not certify feasibility or optimality for the full indexed DRO problem.

notation.meaning: An omitted point exhibiting positive global violation.

review_flags: complexity and degeneracy claims require a generation-method source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The false-termination example is sound, but the NP-hardness and degeneracy claims require a specific generation-method or complexity source.

children.title: Lagrangian Decomposition
children.top_down_role: DRO decompositions based on relaxing complicating couplings.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex scenario-block decomposition obtained by dualizing finite-dimensional linear coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\in\mathbb N\). For each \(s=1,\ldots,S\), let \(Z_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_s}\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(f_s:\mathbb R^{n_s}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(A_s:\mathbb R^{n_s}\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. Define \(F_s=f_s+\delta_{Z_s}\) and \[p^\star=\inf\left\{\sum_{s=1}^S F_s(z_s):\sum_{s=1}^S A_sz_s=0\right\}.\] If \(p^\star\in\mathbb R\) and \(0\in\operatorname{ri}\!\left(\sum_{s=1}^S A_s(\operatorname{dom}F_s)\right)\), then \[p^\star=d^\star:=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}\sum_{s=1}^S\inf_{z_s\in\mathbb R^{n_s}}\bigl(F_s(z_s)+\lambda^\top A_sz_s\bigr).\] For each fixed \(\lambda\), the inner minimizations are independent across scenario blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the linear cross-scenario constraint separates the convex problem into independent scenario subproblems. Under the stated relative-interior condition, the Lagrangian dual and primal optimal values are equal.
assumptions_latex: \(S\in\mathbb N\), each \(Z_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_s}\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and each \(A_s:\mathbb R^{n_s}\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
Each \(f_s:\mathbb R^{n_s}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian dual satisfies \(d^\star=p^\star\), and its inner minimizations separate across \(s=1,\ldots,S\).

notation.meaning: Extended-real scenario objective f_s plus the indicator of Z_s.
Multiplier for the cross-scenario coupling constraint.

children.title: Scenario Decomposition
children.top_down_role: DRO decompositions organized by scenarios, distributions, or support elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus representation that exposes independent finite-scenario DRO blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a finite-scenario formulation has objective \(\sum_{s=1}^S\phi_s(x)\) and common feasible set \(X\). Introduce copies \(x_s\) and a consensus variable \(z\). Then \[\inf_{x\in X}\sum_{s=1}^S\phi_s(x)=\inf_{z\in X,\,x_s\in X}\left\{\sum_{s=1}^S\phi_s(x_s):x_s=z\ \text{for }s=1,\ldots,S\right\}.\] For fixed multipliers or fixed \(z\), the scenario variables occur in independent blocks; the consensus equations contain all cross-scenario coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replicating the common decision by scenario and imposing consensus yields an equivalent formulation whose scenario objectives and constraints are otherwise independent.
assumptions_latex: The same decision \(x\) enters every scenario term.
All scenario copies use the common feasible set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The consensus formulation has the same feasible decisions and optimal value as the original finite-scenario problem.

notation.meaning: Decision copy assigned to scenario s.

children.title: Dualized Scenario Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: Dualized Scenario Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-separable Lagrangian representation of a consensus formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the consensus model \(\inf\{\sum_s\phi_s(x_s):x_s\in X_s,\ x_s=z\}\), assign multipliers \(\lambda_s\) to \(x_s-z=0\). Its dual function is \[q(\lambda)=\sum_{s=1}^S\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\bigl(\phi_s(x_s)+\lambda_s^\top x_s\bigr)+\inf_z\left(-\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\right)^\top z.\] If \(z\) is unrestricted, finiteness requires \(\sum_s\lambda_s=0\), leaving independent scenario infima. Maximizing \(q\) gives a lower bound, with equality under convex strong-duality conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing consensus moves all scenario interaction into multiplier balance; the remaining minimizations are independent scenario problems.
assumptions_latex: Each scenario block has a well-defined extended-real objective on \(X_s\).
For equality of primal and dual values, the consensus problem is convex and satisfies a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For unrestricted \(z\), dual feasibility imposes \(\sum_s\lambda_s=0\), and the dual objective otherwise separates over scenarios.

children.title: Decomposition Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanisms from incomplete recourse, nonconvex blocks, and unresolved coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Scenario decomposition is not exact merely from syntactic scenario labels. If recourse is \(Q(x)=\inf\{y:y\ge0,\ 0\cdot y=1-x\}\), then \(Q(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\ne1\); an L-shaped scheme using only optimality cuts cannot exclude such points and requires feasibility cuts. Likewise, for nonconvex scenario sets, maximizing the decomposed Lagrangian can have a positive duality gap. Finally, if ambiguity constraints couple scenarios nonseparably and are neither retained in the master nor dualized, independent scenario solutions need not assemble into a feasible DRO solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposition can fail through missing feasibility cuts, nonconvex duality gaps, or ambiguity constraints left outside both the master and the dualization.
assumptions_latex: The candidate method treats scenario subproblems independently.
At least one stated failure mechanism is present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent scenario optimality does not then certify feasibility or global optimality of the original DRO problem.

notation.meaning: Recourse value in the incomplete-recourse example.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a hypothesis class and \(A\) an online algorithm. For every \(T\in\mathbb N\), \(h^\star\in\mathcal H\), and realizable sequence \(S=((x_t,h^\star(x_t)))_{t=1}^T\), let \(M_A(S)\) be the number of mistakes made by \(A\), and define \[M_A(\mathcal H)=\sup_S M_A(S),\] where the supremum ranges over all such finite realizable sequences. An inequality \(M_A(\mathcal H)\le B<\infty\) is a mistake bound; \(\mathcal H\) is online learnable if some algorithm \(A\) has such a finite bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mistake complexity of an online algorithm on a hypothesis class is its worst-case number of mistakes over all finite sequences realizable by a member of the class. A finite upper bound is a mistake bound, and the class is online learnable when some algorithm has a finite mistake bound.

children.title: Subgradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Nonsmooth first-order approaches for DRO objectives or dual formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient minimization of a convex, possibly nonsmooth DRO objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Choose \(x_1\in X\), positive steps \(\alpha_k\), and at iteration \(k\) obtain \(g_k\in\partial F(x_k)\). Update \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kg_k)\). After \(N\) iterations return the weighted average \(\bar x_N=(\sum_{k=1}^N\alpha_kx_k)/(\sum_{k=1}^N\alpha_k)\), or stop earlier when an available valid optimality-gap certificate is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move opposite a selected subgradient, project onto the feasible set, and return a stepsize-weighted average or a point with a certified small gap.
assumptions_latex: A subgradient \(g_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) can be computed at every iterate.
Euclidean projection onto \(X\) is well defined and computationally available.
The chosen stepsizes satisfy the convergence requirements of the intended finite-horizon or asymptotic regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\bar x_N\) is feasible; standard subgradient convergence bounds apply when subgradients and the feasible-set diameter are appropriately bounded.

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of F at x.

children.title: Mirror Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Mirror Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected stochastic mirror descent for a convex DRO objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and let \(h:X\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and \(1\)-strongly convex. Given \(x_1\in X\), positive steps \(\eta_t\), and stochastic subgradients \(g_t\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[g_t\mid x_t]\in\partial F(x_t)\), update \[x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\right\},\qquad D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle.\] After \(T\) iterations, output \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t x_t)/(\sum_{t=1}^T\eta_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror descent linearizes the DRO objective, regularizes the step by a Bregman divergence, and returns a step-size-weighted average of the iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex and admits conditionally unbiased stochastic subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_T\in X\) is the algorithm's averaged candidate solution.

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence generated by the mirror map
stochastic subgradient at the current iterate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits the Mirror Methods leaf, but it has no cited source. An authoritative locator supporting this stochastic mirror-descent update and averaging convention is required.

children.title: Geometry-Matching Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Matching Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm selection for mirror descent on convex DRO reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and every queried subgradient satisfies \(\lVert g_t\rVert_*\le G\). Let \(h\) be \(1\)-strongly convex relative to \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), and assume \(D_h(x^*,x_1)\le R_h^2\) for an optimizer \(x^*\). For the mirror update with constant step \(\eta=\sqrt{2}R_h/(G\sqrt T)\), the averaged iterate satisfies \[F(\bar x_T)-F(x^*)\le \frac{\sqrt{2}R_hG}{\sqrt T}.\] Thus a geometry is well matched when the chosen primal norm and mirror map jointly keep both the dual subgradient bound \(G\) and Bregman radius \(R_h\) small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mirror geometry is effective when it simultaneously controls the feasible Bregman radius and the dual norm of objective subgradients.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex on \(X\) and has an optimizer \(x^*\).
\(\lVert g_t\rVert_*\le G\) for all queried subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\bar x_T)-F(x^*)\le \sqrt{2}R_hG/\sqrt T\).

notation.meaning: dual norm of the selected primal norm
Bregman-radius bound from initialization to an optimizer

children.title: Nonsmoothness Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmoothness Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of smooth first-order rates for kinked worst-case objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex objective \(F(x)=L|x|\) on \(X=[-1,1]\), whose unique minimizer is \(x^*=0\). The gradient is undefined at \(0\), and for every \(x\ne0\) its derivative equals \(L\mathop{\rm sign}(x)\); hence no finite constant \(M\) can make \(F\) differentiable with \(M\)-Lipschitz gradient on \(X\). Therefore convergence guarantees requiring global smoothness, including the usual accelerated \(O(T^{-2})\) objective rate, do not apply. Under only bounded-subgradient access, the generic convex rate reverts to order \(O(T^{-1/2})\), unless additional structure or smoothing is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A kinked worst-case objective violates Lipschitz-gradient assumptions, so smooth accelerated rates are unavailable without smoothing or additional structure.
assumptions_latex: The method relies on a globally Lipschitz gradient of the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)=L|x|\) lies outside the smooth-rate regime; bounded-subgradient guarantees are generally only of order \(O(T^{-1/2})\).

children.title: Primal–Dual Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected stochastic primal–dual subgradient iteration for convex-concave DRO saddles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty closed convex sets and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) be convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\). Initialize \((x_1,y_1)\in X\times Y\). Given positive steps \(\eta_t\) and stochastic directions satisfying \(\mathbb E[g_t^x\mid x_t,y_t]\in\partial_xL(x_t,y_t)\) and \(\mathbb E[g_t^y\mid x_t,y_t]\in\partial_yL(x_t,y_t)\), set \[x_{t+1}=\Pi_X(x_t-\eta_tg_t^x),\qquad y_{t+1}=\Pi_Y(y_t+\eta_tg_t^y).\] Stop after \(T\) iterations and output the weighted averages \(\bar x_T=(\sum_t\eta_tx_t)/(\sum_t\eta_t)\) and \(\bar y_T=(\sum_t\eta_ty_t)/(\sum_t\eta_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method descends in the primal variable, ascends in the ambiguity or dual variable, and returns weighted average iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(L\) is convex-concave and has conditionally unbiased stochastic subgradients.
Euclidean projections onto \(X\) and \(Y\) are computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bar x_T,\bar y_T)\in X\times Y\) is the returned approximate saddle pair.

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic mirror descent-ascent for a compact convex-concave DRO formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be compact convex sets, let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) be convex-concave, and let \(h_X,h_Y\) be strongly convex mirror maps. Starting from \((x_1,y_1)\), choose \(g_t^x\in\partial_xL(x_t,y_t)\) and \(g_t^y\in\partial_yL(x_t,y_t)\), then compute \[x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\{\eta_t\langle g_t^x,x\rangle+D_{h_X}(x,x_t)\},\] \[y_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{y\in Y}\{-\eta_t\langle g_t^y,y\rangle+D_{h_Y}(y,y_t)\}.\] After \(T\) steps, return the step-size-weighted averages \((\bar x_T,\bar y_T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror descent-ascent alternates a primal descent step and adversarial ascent step, then averages the iterates to approximate a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(L\) is convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\).
\(h_X\) and \(h_Y\) are strongly convex mirror maps.

children.title: Primal–Dual Saddle Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Conditions linking primal–dual architectures to explicit saddle formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Saddle Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong minimax correspondence for convex DRO saddle reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty compact convex subsets of finite-dimensional spaces, and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, convex in \(x\), and concave in \(y\). Then \[\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}L(x,y)=\max_{y\in Y}\min_{x\in X}L(x,y)=v.\] A pair \((x^*,y^*)\in X\times Y\) is a saddle point if and only if \(x^*\) solves the primal minimax problem, \(y^*\) solves the dual maximin problem, and both attain the common value \(v\); equivalently, \[L(x^*,y)\le L(x^*,y^*)\le L(x,y^*)\quad\text{for all }x\in X,\ y\in Y.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compact convexity and continuity, primal minimax and dual maximin values agree, and their joint optimizers are exactly the saddle points.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}L(x,y)=\max_{y\in Y}\min_{x\in X}L(x,y)\), with optimal pairs characterized by the saddle inequalities.

notation.meaning: common primal and dual saddle value

children.title: Gap-Certificate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where primal–dual gaps provide meaningful computational certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Certificate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable primal–dual gap certificate for compact DRO saddle problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex-concave saddle function \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), define the gap at \((\hat x,\hat y)\in X\times Y\) by \[G(\hat x,\hat y)=\max_{y\in Y}L(\hat x,y)-\min_{x\in X}L(x,\hat y).\] If both extremal subproblems are solved exactly, then \(G(\hat x,\hat y)\ge0\), and \(G(\hat x,\hat y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies simultaneously \[\max_{y\in Y}L(\hat x,y)-v\le\varepsilon,\qquad v-\min_{x\in X}L(x,\hat y)\le\varepsilon,\] where \(v\) is the common saddle value. In particular, zero gap is equivalent to \((\hat x,\hat y)\) being a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computable primal–dual gap upper-bounds both primal and dual suboptimality; zero gap exactly certifies a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) has a finite common saddle value \(v\).
The maximum over \(Y\) and minimum over \(X\) defining the gap are attained and evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(\hat x,\hat y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies primal and dual errors at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-Approximation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected Robbins–Monro approximation for a convex DRO objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F(x)=\mathbb E[\phi(x,\xi)]\) be convex. Initialize \(x_1\in X\). At iteration \(t\), draw \(\xi_t\), obtain \(G(x_t,\xi_t)\) with \(\mathbb E[G(x_t,\xi_t)\mid x_t]\in\partial F(x_t)\), and update \[x_{t+1}=\Pi_X\bigl(x_t-\eta_tG(x_t,\xi_t)\bigr).\] Use steps satisfying \(\eta_t>0\), \(\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\eta_t=\infty\), and \(\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\eta_t^2<\infty\). Stop at a prescribed horizon or tolerance and return the final iterate or a specified weighted average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic approximation repeatedly projects an unbiased noisy subgradient step, using diminishing step sizes whose sum diverges while squared steps are summable.

The oracle is conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded conditional second moment.
The step sizes satisfy the Robbins–Monro summability conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}=\Pi_X(x_t-\eta_tG(x_t,\xi_t))\) defines the stochastic-approximation sequence and its stated output convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Online Convex Optimization Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online mirror descent for sequential convex DRO losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a closed convex decision set and let \(f_1,\ldots,f_T:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex losses revealed sequentially. Choose a differentiable strongly convex mirror map \(h\), initialize \(x_1\in X\), and at round \(t\) play \(x_t\), observe \(f_t\) and a subgradient \(g_t\in\partial f_t(x_t)\), then update \[x_{t+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\eta_t\langle g_t,x\rangle+D_h(x,x_t)\right\}.\] After \(T\) rounds, output the sequence \((x_t)_{t=1}^T\) and evaluate it by static regret \[R_T=\sum_{t=1}^Tf_t(x_t)-\min_{x\in X}\sum_{t=1}^Tf_t(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Online mirror descent chooses decisions before seeing each convex loss, updates from its subgradient, and is evaluated by regret against the best fixed decision.
assumptions_latex: The mirror map \(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_t)_{t=1}^T\) is the online decision sequence, measured by static regret \(R_T\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boosting algorithm for online convex optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online procedure that combines N gamma-weak online convex learners, projects the resulting prediction, smooths each revealed loss, and feeds linearized losses to the component learners.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(N\) copies \(\mathcal W^1,\ldots,\mathcal W^N\) of a \(\gamma\)-WOCL and parameters \(\eta_i\), \(\delta\), and \(\kappa=G\), at each round \(t\) receive \(\mathbf a_t\), set \(\mathbf x_t^0=\mathbf0\), and compute, for \(i=1,\ldots,N\), \[\mathbf x_t^i=(1-\eta_i)\mathbf x_t^{i-1}+\frac{\eta_i}{\gamma}\mathcal W^i(\mathbf a_t).\] Predict \(\mathbf x_t=\operatorname{proj}_{\mathcal K}(\mathbf x_t^N)\) and incur \(f_t(\mathbf x_t)\). After observing \(f_t\), form \(\widehat f_t=X_{\mathcal K,\kappa,\delta}[f_t]\) and pass to each \(\mathcal W^i\) the linear loss \[f_t^i(\mathbf x)=\nabla\widehat f_t(\mathbf x_t^{i-1})\cdot\mathbf x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, the algorithm sequentially combines the scaled predictions of N gamma-weak online convex learners. It projects the final combination onto the feasible set, incurs the revealed loss, smooths that loss, and trains each component learner using a linearization at the preceding intermediate prediction.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf x_t=\operatorname{proj}_{\mathcal K}(\mathbf x_t^N),\qquad f_t^i(\mathbf x)=\nabla\widehat f_t(\mathbf x_t^{i-1})\cdot\mathbf x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bandit convex optimization protocol and static-comparator regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines bandit convex optimization with convex losses, action-local scalar feedback, and worst-case regret relative to the best fixed decision in hindsight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rounds \(t=1,\ldots,T\), an online algorithm \(\mathcal A\) selects \(\mathbf{x}_t\in\mathcal K\) from the available history. A convex loss \(f_t\in\mathcal F\), with \(f_t:\mathcal K\to\mathbb R\), is then selected, and the algorithm incurs and observes only \(f_t(\mathbf{x}_t)\); it receives neither a gradient oracle nor the losses at alternative points. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On each round of bandit convex optimization, the player chooses a feasible point and observes only the scalar loss incurred there, not gradients or losses at other points. Worst-case regret is the excess cumulative loss over the best single fixed feasible decision chosen in hindsight, maximized over admissible loss sequences.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Online convex optimization protocol, regret, and no-regret criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines adversarial OCO with bounded convex losses, external regret, the sublinear-regret criterion, and per-decision running time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a bounded or otherwise suitably structured convex decision set, and let \(\mathcal F\) be a bounded family of convex functions \(f:\mathcal K\to\mathbb R\). At each round \(t=1,\ldots,T\), a nonanticipating algorithm \(\mathcal A\) chooses \(x_t^{\mathcal A}=\mathcal A(f_1,\ldots,f_{t-1})\in\mathcal K\); then \(f_t\in\mathcal F\) is revealed and loss \(f_t(x_t^{\mathcal A})\) is incurred. Its worst-case external regret is
\[
\operatorname{Regret}_T(\mathcal A)=\sup_{(f_1,\ldots,f_T)\in\mathcal F^T}\left\{\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x_t^{\mathcal A})-\min_{x\in\mathcal K}\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x)\right\}.
\]
The algorithm is no-regret when \(\operatorname{Regret}_T(\mathcal A)=o(T)\), in which case its worst-case average excess loss over the best fixed decision in hindsight tends to zero. Its per-round running time is the worst-case expected time required to produce \(x_t\), potentially depending on \(n,T,\mathcal K\), and parameters of the losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In online convex optimization, a nonanticipating player selects a point from a suitably bounded or structured convex set before the current bounded convex loss is revealed. Worst-case external regret compares the player's cumulative loss with that of the best single fixed decision chosen in hindsight. Sublinear regret means that the average excess loss tends to zero. Per-round running time is the worst-case expected time needed to produce the next decision.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and bounded or otherwise sufficiently structured.
\(\mathcal F\) is a bounded family of convex functions \(f:\mathcal K\to\mathbb R\).
\(x_t^{\mathcal A}=\mathcal A(f_1,\ldots,f_{t-1})\), so the round-\(t\) decision is made before \(f_t\) is revealed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Regret}_T(\mathcal A)=\sup_{(f_1,\ldots,f_T)\in\mathcal F^T}\left[\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x_t^{\mathcal A})-\min_{x\in\mathcal K}\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(x)\right],\qquad \operatorname{Regret}_T(\mathcal A)=o(T)\Rightarrow \operatorname{Regret}_T(\mathcal A)/T\to0.
