knowledge_statements.statement_title: Online Convex Optimization Protocol and Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the sequential convex-loss protocol and comparator-based cumulative regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a convex set S, at each round t the learner selects \mathbf{w}_t\in S, then receives a convex function f_t:S\to\mathbb{R} and incurs f_t(\mathbf{w}_t). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected regret bound for bandit online gradient descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon expected-regret guarantee for the stated one-point bandit online algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_T\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz functions, let \(S\) be convex, and define
\[
B=\max_{\mathbf u\in S}\|\mathbf u\|,
\qquad
F=\max_{\mathbf u\in S,\,t\in[T]}f_t(\mathbf u).
\]
For iterates generated by the bandit online convex-optimization algorithm, every \(\mathbf u\in S\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_t\left(f_t(\mathbf w_t+\delta\mathbf v_t)-f_t(\mathbf u)\right)\right]
\le 3L\delta T+\frac{B^2}{2\eta}+\eta T d^2\left(F/\delta+L\right)^2.
\]
When the displayed choices are positive and well-defined, setting
\[
\eta=\frac{B}{d(F/\delta+L)\sqrt{2T}},
\qquad
\delta=\sqrt{\frac{BdF}{3L}}\,T^{-1/4}
\]
gives expected regret \(O(\sqrt{BdFL}\,T^{3/4})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the one-point bandit online method, expected regret is bounded by the sum of smoothing, initial-geometry, and estimator terms. Subject to the stated parameters being well-defined and positive, the given tuning yields order T^(3/4) expected regret.
assumptions_latex: B=\max_{\mathbf u\in S}\|\mathbf u\|\text{ is finite and defined}
F=\max_{\mathbf u\in S,\,t\in[T]}f_t(\mathbf u)\text{ is finite and defined}
(\mathbf w_t,\mathbf v_t)\text{ are generated by the stated bandit online algorithm}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E\left[\sum_t\left(f_t(\mathbf w_t+\delta\mathbf v_t)-f_t(\mathbf u)\right)\right]\le 3L\delta T+\frac{B^2}{2\eta}+\eta T d^2(F/\delta+L)^2,\quad\text{with the stated valid tuning giving }O(\sqrt{BdFL}\,T^{3/4}).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perceptron Mistake Bound with Comparator Hinge Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds the number of Perceptron errors by comparator loss and norm, including the unit-margin separable case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the Perceptron runs on $(\mathbf x_1,y_1),\ldots,(\mathbf x_T,y_T)$. Let $R=\max_{1\le t\le T}\|\mathbf x_t\|$, let $\mathcal M$ be the set of error rounds, and define $f_t(\mathbf w)=\mathbb 1_{[t\in\mathcal M]}[1-y_t\langle\mathbf w,\mathbf x_t\rangle]_+$. Then, for every $\mathbf w^\star$, $$|\mathcal M|\le\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(\mathbf w^\star)+R\|\mathbf w^\star\|\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(\mathbf w^\star)}+R^2\|\mathbf w^\star\|^2.$$ In particular, if $y_t\langle\mathbf w^\star,\mathbf x_t\rangle\ge1$ for every $t$, then $|\mathcal M|\le R^2\|\mathbf w^\star\|^2$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every comparator, the Perceptron's number of mistakes is at most its comparator hinge loss on mistake rounds, plus a mixed radius-norm term and a squared radius-norm term. If one comparator separates every example with margin at least one, the number of mistakes is at most the squared product of the data radius and comparator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathcal M|\le\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(\mathbf w^\star)+R\|\mathbf w^\star\|\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(\mathbf w^\star)}+R^2\|\mathbf w^\star\|^2;\quad \bigl(\forall t,\ y_t\langle\mathbf w^\star,\mathbf x_t\rangle\ge1\bigr)\Rightarrow |\mathcal M|\le R^2\|\mathbf w^\star\|^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\eta,\delta>0\) and a convex set \(S\subset\mathbb R^d\), initialize \(\boldsymbol\theta_1=\mathbf0\). For \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let
\[
\mathbf w_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf w\in S}\|\mathbf w-\eta\boldsymbol\theta_t\|_2,

Predict \(\mathbf w_t+\delta\mathbf v_t\), observe \(f_t(\mathbf w_t+\delta\mathbf v_t)\), set
\[
\mathbf z_t=\frac d\delta f_t(\mathbf w_t+\delta\mathbf v_t)\mathbf v_t,
\]

\[
\boldsymbol\theta_{t+1}=\boldsymbol\theta_t-\mathbf z_t.
\]

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Tractability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding-based tractability condition for finite-dimensional DRO reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a class of DRO instances encoded by rational data of total bit length \(N\). The class is polynomially tractable to additive accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\) if an algorithm returns a feasible decision \(\hat x\) satisfying \[F(\hat x)-\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\le\varepsilon\] using at most \(p(N,\log(1/\varepsilon))\) bit operations, where \(p\) is one polynomial independent of the instance and \(\varepsilon\). For oracle-based input, tractability additionally requires every oracle call and returned number to have polynomial encoding and processing cost. A finite-dimensional convex reformulation is therefore polynomially tractable only when its separation or optimization oracles are polynomial-time implementable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DRO class is polynomially tractable when additive-accuracy solutions require polynomial bit complexity, including the cost and encoding of all oracle operations.
assumptions_latex: Instances have rational encodings of bit length \(N\).
Accuracy is measured by additive objective error \(\varepsilon\).
Oracle calls, if used, are charged their full bit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\hat x)-\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\le\varepsilon\) is attainable within \(p(N,\log(1/\varepsilon))\) bit operations.
review_flags: dependence on log accuracy excludes generic nonsmooth first-order methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition targets the correct tractability leaf, but polynomial dependence on log(1/epsilon) is a strong bit-complexity requirement and the claim that tractability requires polynomial-time separation or optimization oracles is not valid without a specified oracle-based solution framework. A precise complexity-model source is needed before the mathematical scope can be fixed reliably.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stochastic first-order oracle bound for Lipschitz convex DRO objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be convex with Euclidean diameter at most \(D\), and let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex. Suppose each oracle call at \(x\) returns \(g(x,\xi)\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[g(x,\xi)\mid x]\in\partial F(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert g(x,\xi)\rVert_2^2\mid x]\le G^2\). Projected stochastic subgradient descent with an appropriate constant step and averaged output uses \(T\) oracle calls and satisfies \[\mathbb E[F(\bar x_T)]-\min_{x\in X}F(x)\le\frac{DG}{\sqrt T}.\] Consequently, at most \(\lceil D^2G^2/\varepsilon^2\rceil\) calls suffice for expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For bounded-domain convex DRO with a bounded-variance stochastic subgradient oracle, expected epsilon accuracy requires order epsilon-to-the-minus-two oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) has Euclidean diameter at most \(D\), and \(F\) is convex.
The oracle is conditionally unbiased with conditional second moment at most \(G^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\ge D^2G^2/\varepsilon^2\) suffices for \(\mathbb E[F(\bar x_T)]-\min_XF\le\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration bound for deterministic projected subgradient optimization of DRO reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex, and suppose an optimizer \(x^*\) satisfies \(\lVert x_1-x^*\rVert_2\le R\). If every selected subgradient obeys \(\lVert g_t\rVert_2\le G\), projected subgradient descent with constant step \(\eta=R/(G\sqrt T)\) and average \(\bar x_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Tx_t\) satisfies \[F(\bar x_T)-F(x^*)\le\frac{RG}{\sqrt T}.\] Hence \(T\ge\lceil R^2G^2/\varepsilon^2\rceil\) iterations suffice for objective error at most \(\varepsilon\), with one projection and one subgradient evaluation per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected subgradient descent reaches additive epsilon objective error in order epsilon-to-the-minus-two iterations under bounded distance and bounded subgradients.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(X\).
All selected subgradients satisfy \(\lVert g_t\rVert_2\le G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\ge\lceil R^2G^2/\varepsilon^2\rceil\) guarantees \(F(\bar x_T)-F(x^*)\le\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle–Iteration Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient tradeoff for a convex DRO objective accessed through an inexact first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex on a closed convex set \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) of diameter at most \(R\). Suppose an oracle of accuracy \(\delta\ge0\) returns \(g_t\) with \(\|g_t\|_2\le L\) and \(F(y)\ge F(x_t)+g_t^{\mathsf T}(y-x_t)-\delta\) for every \(y\in X\). Projected subgradient iterations with step \(R/(L\sqrt T)\) and averaged output \(\bar x_T\) satisfy \[F(\bar x_T)-\min_{x\in X}F(x)\le \frac{LR}{\sqrt T}+\delta.\] Thus accuracy \(\varepsilon>\delta\) requires at most \(\lceil(LR/(\varepsilon-\delta))^2\rceil\) oracle calls; if one call costs \(C(\delta)\), total oracle work is \(T C(\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cheaper, less accurate DRO oracles introduce additive error; achieving tolerance ε balances oracle accuracy against a quadratic iteration requirement.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is convex and \(X\) is closed, convex, and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\bar x_T)-F^*\le LR/\sqrt T+\delta\), with total oracle work \(T C(\delta)\).

notation.meaning: cost of one oracle call at accuracy δ

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic scaling of an empirical Wasserstein certificate when sample count is fixed and observations are dense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat P_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\xi_i}\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), and let \(\ell(x,\cdot)\) be \(L_x\)-Lipschitz under a norm \(\|\cdot\|\). For the radius-\(\rho\) order-one Wasserstein ball, the certificate \[\sup_{P:W_1(P,\widehat P_N)\le\rho}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\le \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\ell(x,\xi_i)+\rho L_x\] requires storing \(N\) dense vectors and evaluating \(N\) losses. If each loss and norm evaluation costs \(\Theta(d)\), then, for fixed \(N\), certificate evaluation uses \(\Theta(Nd)\) arithmetic operations and \(\Theta(Nd)\) input storage, hence scales linearly in \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed sample count, evaluating a dense empirical Wasserstein upper certificate scales linearly with uncertainty dimension when each loss evaluation is linear-time.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty space is \(\mathbb R^d\) with the transport cost induced by \(\|\cdot\|\).
The loss is finite and \(L_x\)-Lipschitz in uncertainty.
Dense loss and norm evaluations cost \(\Theta(d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(N\), certificate evaluation time and input storage are \(\Theta(Nd)\).

children.title: Scenario Scaling

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-count scaling of an empirical Wasserstein certificate with fixed uncertainty dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat P_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\xi_i}\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), and suppose \(\ell(x,\cdot)\) is \(L_x\)-Lipschitz. Computing the upper certificate \[U_N(x)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\ell(x,\xi_i)+\rho L_x\] requires one loss evaluation per scenario. If one evaluation costs \(C_d\) operations and the observations are streamed, then computing \(U_N(x)\) costs \(\Theta(NC_d)\) time and \(O(d)\) working memory beyond the input stream. Consequently, for fixed \(d\) and fixed evaluation architecture, the certificate time is linear in \(N\), while streaming avoids working-memory growth with \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fixed dimension, an empirical Wasserstein certificate requires one loss evaluation per scenario, giving linear time and constant streaming workspace.
assumptions_latex: The loss is finite and Lipschitz in uncertainty.
Each scenario loss evaluation has fixed cost \(C_d\).

children.title: Dimension–Scenario Interaction

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension–Scenario Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint dense-data scaling for empirical DRO certificate evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dense observations \(\xi_i\in\mathbb R^d\), suppose evaluating \(\ell(x,\xi_i)\) and its transport norm requires \(a d+O(1)\) arithmetic operations. Evaluating an empirical certificate of the separable form \[U_{N,d}(x)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N h_d(x,\xi_i)+r_d(x)\] therefore costs \(aNd+O(N)+C_r(d)\), where \(C_r(d)\) is the cost of \(r_d\). If \(C_r(d)=O(Nd)\), the total cost is \(\Theta(Nd)\). Thus dimension and scenario count interact multiplicatively rather than additively for dense per-scenario processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense per-scenario processing couples dimension and sample count multiplicatively, producing Θ(Nd) certificate-evaluation time.
assumptions_latex: Each of the \(N\) scenarios is a dense vector in \(\mathbb R^d\).

children.title: Scalability Breakdown Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem sizes or structures that defeat otherwise tractable DRO representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalability Breakdown Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic scenario growth caused by an explicitly represented discrete transport plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let both a nominal distribution and an adversarial distribution have \(N\) support points. An explicit discrete optimal-transport formulation introduces couplings \(\pi_{ij}\ge0\) for every ordered pair \((i,j)\in\{1,\ldots,N\}^2\), together with row and column marginal equations. Any implementation that materializes the dense transport plan must store or process \(N^2\) coupling coefficients. Hence its representation requires \(\Omega(N^2)\) memory and at least \(\Omega(N^2)\) arithmetic merely to inspect all coefficients. Linear scenario scaling fails in this dense pairwise-coupling regime, independently of the optimization algorithm subsequently applied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit dense transport between two N-point distributions creates N² coupling variables, forcing quadratic memory and inspection time.
assumptions_latex: Both distributions have \(N\) explicitly listed support points.
All support-point pairs are admissible transport arcs.
The coupling matrix is materialized densely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dense explicit transport representation has \(\Omega(N^2)\) memory and coefficient-processing cost.

notation.meaning: mass transported from nominal point i to adversarial point j
support size of each discrete distribution

DRO transport-complexity source locator is missing

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case hardness inherited from deterministic binary optimization embedded in DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the DRO problem \[\min_{x\in X\cap(\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^{d-p})}\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[f(x,\xi)].\] If \(\mathcal P=\{\delta_{\bar\xi}\}\), then its objective reduces to \(f(x,\bar\xi)\). Given a binary-knapsack instance with rational weights \(w\in\mathbb Q_+^d\), profits \(v\in\mathbb Q_+^d\), and capacity \(B\in\mathbb Q_+\), choose \(p=d\), \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^d:w^{\mathsf T}x\le B\}\), and \(f(x,\bar\xi)=-v^{\mathsf T}x\). Solving the resulting DRO problem is equivalent to maximizing \(v^{\mathsf T}x\) over the binary-knapsack feasible set. Consequently, the general mixed-integer DRO class is NP-hard, even for a singleton ambiguity set, unless additional structural restrictions are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General mixed-integer DRO is NP-hard because a singleton ambiguity set can reproduce binary knapsack exactly.
assumptions_latex: The model permits binary decision variables and rational linear objectives and constraints.
Complexity is measured in the binary encoding length of the rational input data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The general mixed-integer DRO optimization class is NP-hard, even when \(\mathcal P\) is a singleton.

notation.meaning: Dirac distribution at the fixed uncertainty realization

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Discrete Optimization p. 46; 1.5.1 Branch and Bound search p. 46

knowledge_statements.title: Extremal Moment-Distribution Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-atomic attainment certificate for a moment-constrained worst-case expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P=\{P\in\mathcal M_+(\Xi):\int dP=1,\ \int g_j(\xi)dP=b_j,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). A finite atomic measure \(P^*=\sum_{k=1}^r p_k\delta_{\xi_k}\) is a worst-case certificate for \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\int\ell(\xi)dP\) when \(p_k\ge0\), \(\sum_kp_k=1\), \(\sum_kp_kg_j(\xi_k)=b_j\), and \(\sum_kp_k\ell(\xi_k)=\eta\), while a valid dual moment bound also equals \(\eta\). Under standard compactness and continuity conditions, an optimal extreme measure may be chosen with \(r\le m+1\). The atoms, weights, and matching dual bound jointly certify attainment and optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small atomic distribution satisfying all moments and matching a dual bound certifies the worst-case moment value.
assumptions_latex: \(\Xi\) is compact and the moment functions and loss are continuous.
The moment ambiguity set is nonempty.
Strong duality holds for the generalized moment problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A matching primal atomic measure and dual moment bound certify the worst-case value \(\eta\), with an extreme optimizer supported on at most \(m+1\) points.
review_flags: support bound depends on the precise independence and extreme-point hypotheses
authoritative generalized-moment theorem locator is required

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Transport Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual majorization certificate for empirical optimal-transport ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat P_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\xi_i}\), and define \(\mathcal P_\rho=\{P:W_c(P,\widehat P_N)\le\rho\}\) for a nonnegative lower-semicontinuous transport cost \(c\). If \(\lambda\ge0\) and scalars \(s_i\) satisfy \[\ell(z)\le s_i+\lambda c(z,\xi_i)\quad\text{for every }z\in\Xi\text{ and }i=1,\ldots,N,\] then every \(P\in\mathcal P_\rho\) obeys \[\mathbb E_P[\ell(\xi)]\le \lambda\rho+\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^Ns_i.\] Thus \((\lambda,s_1,\ldots,s_N)\) is a verifiable adversarial-transport upper-bound certificate; equality with a feasible adversarial distribution certifies worst-case optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transport multiplier and pointwise loss majorants certify an upper bound; a matching feasible adversarial distribution certifies exactness.
assumptions_latex: The nominal distribution is empirical with equal weights.
The transport cost is nonnegative and lower semicontinuous.
All displayed expectations and suprema are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\rho}\mathbb E_P[\ell]\le\lambda\rho+N^{-1}\sum_i s_i\), with equality certified by a matching feasible distribution.

notation.meaning: optimal-transport discrepancy induced by cost c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weak transport duality yields the displayed upper certificate
authoritative Wasserstein-DRO duality locator is missing

knowledge_statements.title: Divergence-Reweighting Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual certificate for a finite-support phi-divergence ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let nominal weights \(p_i>0\) sum to one and let \(\phi\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(\phi(1)=0\). For losses \(l_i\), consider weights \(q_i\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_iq_i=1\) and \(\sum_ip_i\phi(q_i/p_i)\le\rho\). If \(\lambda\ge0\), \(\eta\in\mathbb R\), and feasible \(q\) satisfy \[\sum_iq_il_i=\eta+\lambda\rho+\lambda\sum_ip_i\phi^*\!\left(\frac{l_i-\eta}{\lambda}\right),\] with the closed perspective convention at \(\lambda=0\), then weak duality makes this common value the worst-case expectation. The feasible reweighting and matching dual pair form an exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible adversarial reweighting and a matching phi-divergence dual value certify the exact worst-case expectation.
assumptions_latex: Nominal weights are strictly positive and normalized.
The divergence generator is proper, closed, convex, and normalized by \(\phi(1)=0\).
Finite-dimensional strong duality holds for the ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matching feasible primal and dual values certify \(\sup_q\sum_iq_il_i\).

notation.meaning: convex conjugate of the divergence generator

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Dual-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for a conic reformulation of a DRO inner maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the conic maximization problem \[v_P=\sup\{c^{\mathsf T}y:Ay=b,\ y\in K\},\] where \(K\) is a closed convex cone. Any \(z\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}z-c\in K^*\) is dual feasible and gives \(c^{\mathsf T}y\le b^{\mathsf T}z\) for every primal-feasible \(y\). Therefore \(b^{\mathsf T}z\) is a verifiable upper-bound certificate for the DRO inner value. If a primal-feasible \(y^*\) also satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}y^*=b^{\mathsf T}z\), then \(y^*\) and \(z\) certify optimality of both conic programs without requiring an independent strong-duality argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic-dual feasible point certifies an upper bound; equality with a primal feasible point certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual expressions are finite at the displayed feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_P\le b^{\mathsf T}z\); equality with a primal feasible value certifies optimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weak-duality calculation and certificate classification are correct, but no conic-duality or DRO reformulation source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Semi-Infinite Separation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation-or-feasibility certificate for semi-infinite DRO constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\in\mathbb R^p\) be subject to \(g(u,\xi)\le0\) for every \(\xi\in\Xi\), and define \[v(u)=\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}g(u,\xi).\] If a global oracle certifies an upper bound \(\widehat v(u)\) satisfying \(v(u)\le\widehat v(u)\le0\), then \(u\) is feasible for every semi-infinite constraint. If the supremum is attained at \(\xi^*\in\Xi\) and \(g(u,\xi^*)=v(u)>0\), then \(\xi^*\) certifies infeasibility. The constraint \(g(\cdot,\xi^*)\le0\) is a valid scenario cut; when \(g(\cdot,\xi^*)\) is convex, a subgradient at \(u\) yields a separating affine cut. More generally, \(v(u)\le\widehat v(u)\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility in the sense that \(g(u,\xi)\le\varepsilon\) for every \(\xi\in\Xi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified upper bound on the worst violation proves feasibility or approximate feasibility, while an attained positive violation supplies an infeasibility witness and a valid scenario cut.
assumptions_latex: The oracle globally solves the separation problem or returns a certified upper bound \(\widehat v(u)\ge v(u)\).
The supremum is attained when a violating scenario is required.
For an affine separating cut, \(g(\cdot,\xi^*)\) is convex and subdifferentiable at \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(v(u)\le\widehat v(u)\le0\) certifies feasibility; an attained value \(g(u,\xi^*)=v(u)>0\) certifies violation.

notation.meaning: certified upper bound on the maximum violation

review_flags: The upper-bound direction and cut type have been made explicit.
An authoritative semi-infinite optimization locator is still required.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori optimality certificate from feasible and relaxation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization DRO problem with optimal value \(v^*\), let \(x^{\mathrm{feas}}\) be feasible with objective \(U=F(x^{\mathrm{feas}})\), and let \(L\) be the optimal value or any certified lower bound from a relaxation, dual problem, or restricted certificate system. Weak bounding gives \[L\le v^*\le U.\] Hence \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies that \(x^{\mathrm{feas}}\) is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal. If \(L>0\), the relative-gap condition \((U-L)/L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\) certifies the corresponding relative accuracy. The certificate must include independently checkable primal feasibility and validity of the lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible objective and valid relaxation lower bound bracket the optimum; a small gap certifies approximate optimality.
assumptions_latex: The DRO problem is a minimization problem with finite optimal value.
The relaxation or dual construction validly supplies \(L\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) implies \(F(x^{\mathrm{feas}})-v^*\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: objective value of a certified feasible solution

review_flags: DRO-specific certificate-system source locator is missing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The a posteriori gap certificate is mathematically correct and fits the leaf, but it has no inspectable source for the primal-relaxation bounding framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment Confidence-Region Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calibration by a simultaneous confidence region for finitely many population moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Xi\) be measurable, let \(g:\Xi\to\mathbb R^k\), and let \(\widehat C_{n,1-\alpha}\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) be a data-dependent confidence region satisfying \(\mathbb P^n\{\mathbb E_P[g(\xi)]\in\widehat C_{n,1-\alpha}\}\ge 1-\alpha\). The moment-calibrated ambiguity set is
\[\mathcal P_n=\left\{Q:\mathbb E_Q[\|g(\xi)\|]<\infty,\ \mathbb E_Q[g(\xi)]\in\widehat C_{n,1-\alpha}\right\}.\]
Consequently, \(\mathbb P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n\}\ge1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributions whose selected moments lie in a simultaneous confidence region form an ambiguity set containing the data-generating distribution with the region's confidence level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n\}\ge1-\alpha\).
review_flags: Exact DRO-specific source locator is absent from the supplied inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction and coverage implication are mathematically coherent and the definition kind fits the leaf, but no cited source supports the simultaneous moment-confidence calibration claim.

children.title: Divergence Calibration
children.top_down_role: Selection of divergence ambiguity radii from statistical evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Divergence Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample calibration of a divergence ball around an empirical or fitted reference law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D(Q,R)\ge0\) be a divergence between probability measures, let \(\widehat P_n\) be a data-dependent reference distribution, and define \(T_n(P)=D(P,\widehat P_n)\). A level-\((1-\alpha)\) divergence radius is any measurable \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\) satisfying
\[\mathbb P^n\{T_n(P)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.\]
The corresponding calibrated ambiguity set is \(\mathcal P_n(\rho_{n,\alpha})=\{Q:D(Q,\widehat P_n)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the divergence radius as an upper confidence threshold for the divergence between the true and fitted distributions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n(\rho_{n,\alpha})\}\ge1-\alpha\).
review_flags: Divergence-specific calibration source and convention are not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent, but calibration depends on the chosen divergence, its orientation, and the reference-law construction; no inspectable citation supports these conventions.

children.title: Goodness-of-Fit Calibration
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity-set calibration based on goodness-of-fit procedures.

knowledge_statements.title: Goodness-of-Fit Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inversion of a level-\(\alpha\) goodness-of-fit test into a distributional confidence set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every candidate distribution \(Q\), let \(\varphi_{n,\alpha}(Q)\in\{0,1\}\) denote a goodness-of-fit test of \(H_0:P=Q\), where one means rejection. If
\[\sup_Q Q^n\{\varphi_{n,\alpha}(Q)=1\}\le\alpha,\]
then the inverted acceptance set \(\mathcal P_n=\{Q:\varphi_{n,\alpha}(Q)=0\}\) satisfies \(P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every distribution \(P\) in the tested model class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invert all distributions not rejected by a size-controlled goodness-of-fit test; the resulting ambiguity set has the corresponding coverage.
assumptions_latex: The candidate and true distributions belong to the test's model class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n\}\ge1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: test of the candidate distribution Q

review_flags: No supplied locator supports test inversion for DRO ambiguity sets.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The size condition correctly yields coverage by test inversion and the condition kind is appropriate, but no source or locator supports its use as DRO ambiguity-set calibration.

children.title: Test–Radius Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Links between test acceptance regions and divergence-radius choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Test–Radius Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence between threshold-test acceptance and membership in a divergence ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_n(Q)=D(Q,\widehat P_n)\), and define the threshold test \(\varphi_{n,\alpha}(Q)=\mathbf 1\{T_n(Q)>\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\). Then, pointwise for every candidate distribution \(Q\),
\[\varphi_{n,\alpha}(Q)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad D(Q,\widehat P_n)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Q\in\mathcal P_n(\rho_{n,\alpha}).\]
Thus inversion of this test produces exactly the closed divergence ball of radius \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A threshold divergence test accepts exactly those candidate distributions lying in the divergence ball with the same threshold as radius.
assumptions_latex: \(D(Q,\widehat P_n)\) is defined and measurable for every candidate \(Q\).
Rejection uses the strict inequality \(D(Q,\widehat P_n)>\rho_{n,\alpha}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{Q:\varphi_{n,\alpha}(Q)=0\}=\{Q:D(Q,\widehat P_n)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\).
review_flags: The algebraic equivalence is direct, but an external DRO source is required by the evidence contract.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise threshold–ball equivalence is correct and the duality/correspondence kind fits the leaf, but the record contains no evidence or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Calibration-Mismatch Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sampling or model conditions that invalidate the intended statistical coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Calibration-Mismatch Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage failure when a radius is calibrated under a law different from the statistic's actual sampling law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_n(P)=D(P,\widehat P_n)\), and suppose a radius \(\widetilde\rho_{n,\alpha}\) is calibrated under an approximation \(G_n\) rather than the true distribution function \(F_{n,P}(t)=P^n\{T_n(P)\le t\}\). The ambiguity set undercovers whenever
\[F_{n,P}(\widetilde\rho_{n,\alpha})<1-\alpha.\]
In particular, nominal coverage is not implied if the reference model, divergence orientation, parameter fitting rule, support, or sampling regime used for calibration differs from that defining \(T_n(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nominal radius can undercover when its calibration distribution does not match the actual statistic, fitted model, support, or sampling regime.
assumptions_latex: \(T_n(P)\) is measurable under the true sampling law.
\(\widetilde\rho_{n,\alpha}\) is computed from a calibration law not assumed equal to \(F_{n,P}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{n,P}(\widetilde\rho_{n,\alpha})<1-\alpha\Rightarrow P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n(\widetilde\rho_{n,\alpha})\}<1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: true distribution function of the calibration statistic
radius obtained from the approximating law

review_flags: A source classifying concrete divergence-calibration mismatch regimes is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The undercoverage implication is correct, but the listed mismatch regimes and their relevance to divergence calibration require a specific authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Wasserstein Concentration Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radius selection from a finite-sample concentration inequality for empirical Wasserstein distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W_p\) be the order-\(p\) Wasserstein distance, and suppose a known nonincreasing bound \(b_n:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]\) satisfies
\[P^n\{W_p(P,\widehat P_n)>r\}\le b_n(r)\quad\text{for every }r\ge0.\]
For \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), choose \(\rho_{n,\alpha}=\inf\{r\ge0:b_n(r)\le\alpha\}\), with right-continuity or any larger admissible radius. Then the Wasserstein ambiguity set \(\{Q:W_p(Q,\widehat P_n)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\) covers \(P\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invert a concentration bound for empirical Wasserstein distance to obtain a radius with finite-sample distributional coverage.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) has the moment or tail regularity required by the stated bound \(b_n\).
\(\widehat P_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{\xi_i}\) is based on independent observations from \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^n\{W_p(P,\widehat P_n)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\).
review_flags: The exact concentration rate depends on dimension and tail assumptions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inversion principle is sound, but the applicable Wasserstein concentration bound, dimension and tail assumptions, and existence of an admissible radius are not fixed by an inspectable source.

children.title: Bootstrap Calibration
children.top_down_role: Bootstrap-based selection of ambiguity-set parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Bootstrap Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bootstrap quantile calibration of a data-dependent ambiguity-set radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given observations \(\xi_{1:n}\), compute \(\widehat P_n\). For \(b=1,\ldots,B\), draw \(\xi_{1:n}^{*(b)}\) independently with replacement from \(\widehat P_n\), form \(\widehat P_n^{*(b)}\), and calculate \(T_n^{*(b)}=d(\widehat P_n^{*(b)},\widehat P_n)\). Set \(\widehatho_{n,\alpha}^{*}\) to the empirical \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(T_n^{*(1)},\ldots,T_n^{*(B)}\), and output
\[\mathcal P_n^{*}=\{Q:d(Q,\widehat P_n)\le\widehatho_{n,\alpha}^{*}\}.\]
Bootstrap validity requires separate regularity establishing the desired coverage approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resample from the empirical distribution, compute bootstrap discrepancies, and use their upper empirical quantile as the ambiguity radius.
assumptions_latex: The discrepancy \(d\) is measurable on the candidate distributions.
Conditional bootstrap replicates are independent given the observed sample.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_n^{*}=\{Q:d(Q,\widehat P_n)\le\widehatho_{n,\alpha}^{*}\}\) is the algorithm's output.
review_flags: Bootstrap consistency conditions depend on the discrepancy and statistical model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content is appropriately an algorithm and clearly withholds a coverage claim, but a source is needed to establish when this bootstrap discrepancy consistently calibrates a DRO radius.

children.title: Resampling Calibration
children.top_down_role: Repeated-sample procedures for assessing DRO calibration choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Resampling Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic Monte Carlo calibration using a specified resampling law and calibration statistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(Z\), a fitted resampling law \(\widehat R_n\), a statistic \(T(Z,Q)\), and replication count \(B\), generate \(Z^{*(b)}\sim\widehat R_n\) conditionally independently and compute \(S_b=T(Z^{*(b)},\widehat P_n)\) for \(b=1,\ldots,B\). Let \(\widehatho_{n,\alpha}\) be the empirical \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(S_1,\ldots,S_B\). Output the ambiguity set whose defining discrepancy does not exceed \(\widehatho_{n,\alpha}\); stop after \(B\) replications or when a prescribed quantile-error tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simulate the calibration statistic under a fitted resampling law and use its upper quantile as the ambiguity-set radius.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat R_n\) specifies a conditionally simulable resampling distribution.
The resampled statistic uses the same discrepancy and fitting convention as the ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output radius is the empirical \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the resampled calibration statistics.
review_flags: The node does not specify permutation, subsampling, parametric, or bootstrap resampling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic algorithm does not formally identify the ambiguity-set discrepancy or relate the fitted distribution to the statistic, and its adaptive stopping option lacks a quantile-error specification. A source is needed to select a reliable mathematical version.

children.title: Validation Calibration
children.top_down_role: Held-out-data procedures for selecting robustness levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Validation Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Held-out selection of an ambiguity radius from a finite candidate grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Split independent data into training and validation samples. From training data construct centers \(\widehat P_{\mathrm{tr}}\), candidate radii \(\mathcal R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_m\}\), and decisions \(x_r\in\arg\min_x\sup_{Q:d(Q,\widehat P_{\mathrm{tr}})\le r}\mathbb E_Q[\ell(x,\xi)]\). Compute validation losses \(\widehat L_{\mathrm{val}}(x_r)\), select
\[\widehat r\in\arg\min_{r\in\mathcal R}\widehat L_{\mathrm{val}}(x_r),\]
using a fixed tie rule, and output \(x_{\widehat r}\) and \(\widehat r\). Any confidence guarantee must account for selection over \(\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit candidate DRO decisions on training data and select the radius minimizing held-out validation loss, with selection-adjusted guarantees handled separately.
assumptions_latex: Training and validation samples are independent.
Each candidate DRO problem and validation loss is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_{\widehat r},\widehat r)\) is selected solely by the prescribed validation criterion and tie rule.

notation.meaning: training-sample DRO decision at radius r

review_flags: Validation-based DRO radius selection needs a dedicated source and selection guarantee.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits validation-based radius selection, but the decision domain is not introduced and no source supports the stated DRO validation protocol or required selection adjustment.

children.title: Resampling–Validation Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Data regimes governing the choice among bootstrap, resampling, or validation approaches.

knowledge_statements.title: Resampling–Validation Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule distinguishing distributional calibration from decision-performance tuning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_{\mathrm{cov}}\) estimate a \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of a distributional discrepancy by valid resampling, and let \(r_{\mathrm{val}}\) minimize held-out decision loss over a candidate grid. Use \(r_{\mathrm{cov}}\) when the target is ambiguity-set coverage; use \(r_{\mathrm{val}}\) when the target is predictive decision performance. If both properties are required, select only among radii satisfying a simultaneous coverage constraint, for example
\[\widehat r\in\arg\min_{r\in\mathcal R:\,r\ge r_{\mathrm{cov}}}\widehat L_{\mathrm{val}}(x_r),\]
with all calibration and validation multiplicities included in the guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resampling targets distributional coverage; validation targets decision loss. Requiring both calls for validation constrained by a coverage-calibrated radius.
assumptions_latex: The resampling method consistently estimates the required discrepancy quantile.
Validation observations are independent of training and calibration data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coverage and validation objectives are interchangeable only under an additional theorem linking their target criteria.
review_flags: This selection taxonomy and constrained rule require authoritative support.
Coverage multiplicity details depend on the calibration protocol.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle distinguishes coverage calibration from predictive tuning, but the constrained selection prescription and multiplicity requirement need authoritative support and a precisely specified calibration protocol.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguity-Set Coverage Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample inclusion probability for a data-dependent ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z_n\sim P^n\) and let \(\mathcal P_n(Z_n)\) be a measurable random set of probability distributions. It has pointwise \((1-\alpha)\) coverage over a model class \(\mathfrak P\) if
\[P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n(Z_n)\}\ge1-\alpha\qquad\text{for every }P\in\mathfrak P.\]
It has uniform coverage if the stronger condition \(\inf_{P\in\mathfrak P}P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n(Z_n)\}\ge1-\alpha\) holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ambiguity set has pointwise coverage when it contains each true distribution with the nominal probability, and uniform coverage when this holds uniformly over the model class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{P\in\mathfrak P}P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n(Z_n)\}\ge1-\alpha\) characterizes uniform \((1-\alpha)\) coverage.
review_flags: A DRO-specific source for pointwise and uniform ambiguity-set coverage is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise and uniform coverage formulas are coherent and the property kind fits the leaf, but no DRO-specific citation or standard-field rationale is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Out-of-Sample Certificate Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper certificate for the true expected loss of a data-dependent DRO decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat x_n\) be any measurable data-dependent decision, let \(\mathcal P_n\) satisfy \(P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), and define
\[\widehat J_n=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_Q[\ell(\widehat x_n,\xi)].\]
Whenever \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the true risk obeys \(\mathbb E_P[\ell(\widehat x_n,\xi)]\le\widehat J_n\). Therefore
\[P^n\left\{\mathbb E_P[\ell(\widehat x_n,\xi)]\le\widehat J_n\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\]
The implication remains valid despite data dependence of \(\widehat x_n\), provided the ambiguity-set coverage event itself is distributional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the ambiguity set contains the true distribution, its worst-case loss upper-bounds the true loss of the chosen decision with the same confidence.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell(\widehat x_n,\cdot)\) is measurable and has defined expectation for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_n\cup\{P\}\).
\(\widehat x_n\) and \(\widehat J_n\) are measurable functions of the data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^n\{\mathbb E_P[\ell(\widehat x_n,\xi)]\le\widehat J_n\}\ge1-\alpha\).
review_flags: The certificate follows directly from coverage, but an authoritative DRO source is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate follows pointwise from ambiguity-set coverage and remains valid for a measurable data-dependent decision, but the nontrivial DRO certificate claim has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Decision-Class Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform out-of-sample control for a bounded loss class using empirical Rademacher complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a decision class, let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be i.i.d. with law \(P\), and let \(0\leq \ell(x,z)\leq M\). Define \(R(x)=\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,Z)]\), \(\widehat R_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(x,Z_i)\), and \(\mathcal L=\{z\mapsto\ell(x,z):x\in X\}\). If \(\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal L)\) is the empirical Rademacher complexity, then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[\sup_{x\in X}|R(x)-\widehat R_n(x)|\leq 2\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal L)+3M\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With high probability, every decision’s population loss is close to its empirical loss, at a rate controlled by empirical Rademacher complexity and sampling noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in X}|R(x)-\widehat R_n(x)|\leq 2\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal L)+3M\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/(2n)}\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Loss functions induced by the decision class.
Empirical Rademacher complexity on the observed sample.

review_flags: Exact authoritative locator for the stated empirical-Rademacher constants is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound is mathematically plausible and the complexity-bound kind fits, but no citation supports the empirical-Rademacher convention or exact constants. Its connection to DRO generalization is also not made explicit.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Dependent Generalization Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sample-computable upper certificate for the population risk of a data-selected DRO decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the setting of the uniform decision-class bound, let \(\widehat x=\widehat x(Z_1,ldots,Z_n)\in X\) be any measurable data-dependent decision. Define
\[U_n(\widehat x,\delta)=\widehat R_n(\widehat x)+2\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal L)+3M\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}.\]
Because the underlying deviation event holds simultaneously for every \(x\in X\), it also holds at the random choice \(\widehat x\). Consequently,
\[\mathbb P\{R(\widehat x)\leq U_n(\widehat x,\delta)\}\geq1-\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform deviation bound remains valid after data-dependent decision selection, yielding a computable high-confidence upper bound on the selected decision’s population risk.
assumptions_latex: The uniform guarantee of node \(A16.C03.N28A413A93278\) holds for \(X\).
\(\widehat x\) is an \(X\)-valued measurable function of the sample.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_n(\widehat x,\delta)\) is a \((1-\delta)\)-confidence upper certificate for \(R(\widehat x)\).

notation.meaning: Decision selected from the observed data.

review_flags: A source explicitly supporting post-selection use of the stated uniform bound is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The post-selection implication is valid only after establishing the cited uniform event, which is itself unsourced. The expression \(Z_1,ldots,Z_n\) is malformed and must be corrected to \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\). The certificate kind otherwise fits the leaf.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency of DRO optimal values obtained from uniform convergence of robust objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be compact, let \(F_n:X\to\mathbb R\) be random robust objectives, and let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Define \(v_n=\inf_{x\in X}F_n(x)\) and \(v=\min_{x\in X}F(x)\). If
\[\sup_{x\in X}|F_n(x)-F(x)|\longrightarrow0\]
almost surely, then
\[|v_n-v|\leq\sup_{x\in X}|F_n(x)-F(x)|\longrightarrow0\]
almost surely. Thus the optimal values of the data-driven DRO problems converge to the population optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform almost-sure convergence of robust objectives on a compact decision set implies almost-sure convergence of their optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_n\to v\) almost surely.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this uniform-convergence consistency theorem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimal-value consistency statement is standard and mathematically coherent, and theorem is the appropriate kind, but no inspectable citation or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Set Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer consistency of exact DRO minimizers under uniform objective convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a compact metric space, let \(F_n,F:X\to\mathbb R\), and suppose \(F\) is continuous and \(F_n\to F\) uniformly almost surely. Set \(S_n=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F_n(x)\) and \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F(x)\), assuming \(S_n\neq\varnothing\). Then every accumulation point of every sequence \(x_n\in S_n\) belongs to \(S\) almost surely. Equivalently,
\[\sup_{x\in S_n}d(x,S)\longrightarrow0\]
almost surely. If \(S=\{x^\star\}\), every selection \(x_n\in S_n\) converges to \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness and uniform objective convergence, robust minimizers approach the population solution set; a unique population minimizer attracts every selected minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuous and \(F_n\to F\) uniformly almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in S_n}d(x,S)\to0\) almost surely; uniqueness of \(S\) implies convergence of every minimizer selection.

notation.meaning: Set of minimizers of the data-driven robust objective.
Distance from a point to the solution set.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the stated argmin-consistency formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated outer argmin consistency is plausible under the compactness, continuity, uniform-convergence, and nonemptiness assumptions, but it has no supporting citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Shrinking-Ambiguity Asymptotics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform convergence induced by Wasserstein ambiguity balls whose centers and radii approach the true distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal Z,d)\) be Polish, let \(P_0\in\mathcal P_1(\mathcal Z)\), and define \(\mathcal U_n=\{Q:W_1(Q,\widehat P_n)\leq\rho_n\}\). Suppose \(W_1(\widehat P_n,P_0)\to0\), \(\rho_n\to0\), and every \(z\mapsto\ell(x,z)\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz uniformly over \(x\in X\). For
\[F_n(x)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal U_n}\mathbb E_Q[\ell(x,Z)],\qquad F(x)=\mathbb E_{P_0}[\ell(x,Z)],\]
one has
\[\sup_{x\in X}|F_n(x)-F(x)|\leq L\bigl(\rho_n+W_1(\widehat P_n,P_0)\bigr)\longrightarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Wasserstein DRO objective converges uniformly to the true expected loss when its empirical center is consistent and its ambiguity radius vanishes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in X}|F_n(x)-F(x)|\to0\).

notation.meaning: Wasserstein ambiguity ball centered at the empirical distribution.

review_flags: An exact source for the stated uniform Lipschitz bound was not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Wasserstein-Lipschitz argument plausibly gives the displayed uniform bound, and property fits the leaf, but no source verifies the formulation or its integrability conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Distributional Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order limit law for a regularized DRO value functional under a shrinking radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_0\) be a real-valued statistical functional that is Hadamard differentiable at \(P_0\), and suppose \(\sqrt n(\widehat P_n-P_0)\Rightarrow G\) in its tangent space. Let \(T_\rho(P)\) be a DRO value satisfying, uniformly for local perturbations \(H_n\to H\),
\[T_{\rho_n}(P_0+n^{-1/2}H_n)=T_0(P_0)+n^{-1/2}\dot T_{P_0}(H)+\rho_n\kappa+o(n^{-1/2}+\rho_n).\]
If \(\sqrt n\rho_n\to c\in[0,\infty)\), then
\[\sqrt n\bigl(T_{\rho_n}(\widehat P_n)-T_0(P_0)\bigr)\Rightarrow \dot T_{P_0}(G)+c\kappa.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under functional differentiability, a radius of order inverse square root sample size adds a deterministic robustness shift to the ordinary asymptotic limit.
assumptions_latex: \(\sqrt n(\widehat P_n-P_0)\Rightarrow G\) in the derivative tangent space.
The displayed local expansion holds uniformly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt n(T_{\rho_n}(\widehat P_n)-T_0(P_0))\Rightarrow\dot T_{P_0}(G)+c\kappa\).

notation.meaning: Hadamard derivative of the unrobust value functional.
Weak limit of the empirical process.
First-order sensitivity to the ambiguity radius.

review_flags: The node admits model-specific limit laws; a source fixing this generic differentiable-functional version is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic limit law is not justified directly by an expansion stated only for deterministic perturbations \(H_n\to H\), because the empirical perturbations converge weakly. A source must specify the stochastic-uniform expansion and functional delta-method conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Wasserstein Concentration Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent empirical order-one Wasserstein rates on bounded Euclidean support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be supported on a subset of \(\mathbb R^d\) having diameter at most \(D\), and let \(\widehat P_n\) be the empirical distribution of \(n\) i.i.d. observations. There exists \(C_d<\infty\), depending only on \(d\), such that
\[\mathbb E W_1(\widehat P_n,P)\leq C_dD\,r_{n,d},\qquad r_{n,d}=\begin{cases}n^{-1/2},&d=1,\\ \sqrt{\log(1+n)/n},&d=2,\\ n^{-1/d},&d\geq3.\end{cases}\]
Moreover, for every \(t>0\),
\[\mathbb P\{W_1(\widehat P_n,P)>\mathbb EW_1(\widehat P_n,P)+t\}\leq e^{-2nt^2/D^2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On bounded Euclidean support, empirical Wasserstein error has dimension-dependent mean rate and a sub-Gaussian deviation above its mean.
assumptions_latex: The support of \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) has diameter at most \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_1(\widehat P_n,P)=O_{\mathbb P}(r_{n,d})\), with the displayed finite-sample tail bound.
review_flags: An authoritative locator for the dimension-dependent expectation rates and constants is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dimension-dependent mean rates and bounded-differences tail are plausible, and complexity_bound is appropriate, but the combined claim lacks an authoritative locator verifying its assumptions and constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Divergence Confidence Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-alphabet relative-entropy confidence radius obtained from the method of types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be a distribution on an alphabet of size \(m<\infty\), with \(P(a)>0\) for every symbol, and let \(\widehat P_n\) be the empirical distribution of \(n\) i.i.d. samples. For every \(r>0\), the method-of-types bound gives
\[\mathbb P\{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat P_n\Vert P)\geq r\}\leq(n+1)^m e^{-nr}.\]
Hence, for \(0<\delta<1\), the radius
\[r_n(\delta)=\frac{m\log(n+1)+\log(1/\delta)}{n}\]
satisfies \(\mathbb P\{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat P_n\Vert P)\leq r_n(\delta)\}\geq1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite alphabet, a KL confidence radius of order dimension times log sample size over sample size contains the empirical-to-true divergence with high probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat P_n\Vert P)\leq[m\log(n+1)+\log(1/\delta)]/n\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Kullback–Leibler divergence from Q to P.

review_flags: The supplied inventory lacks a locator for this method-of-types confidence inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-alphabet method-of-types calculation is plausible and the selected kind fits, but no citation with a theorem, section, or page locator supports the exact polynomial prefactor and radius.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Estimation Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous concentration rate for finitely many bounded moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k):\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R^k\) satisfy \(a_j\leq g_j(z)\leq b_j\) for all \(z\) and \(j\). For i.i.d. observations define \(\widehat\mu_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^ng(Z_i)\) and \(\mu=\mathbb E[g(Z)]\). Writing \(B=\max_j(b_j-a_j)\), Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound yield, for \(0<\delta<1\),
\[\mathbb P\left\{\|\widehat\mu_n-\mu\|_\infty\leq B\sqrt{\frac{\log(2k/\delta)}{2n}}\right\}\geq1-\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector of bounded moments is estimated uniformly over its coordinates at the square-root log-dimension over sample-size rate.
assumptions_latex: \(a_j\leq g_j(Z)\leq b_j\) almost surely for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat\mu_n-\mu\|_\infty\leq B\sqrt{\log(2k/\delta)/(2n)}\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the stated simultaneous Hoeffding rate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simultaneous Hoeffding rate follows plausibly from coordinatewise concentration and a union bound, but the record supplies no inspectable source locator.

children.title: Hypothesis-Class Complexity Rates
children.top_down_role: Finite-sample rates governed by the richness of predictive hypothesis classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Hypothesis-Class Complexity Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform prediction-risk rate controlled by the Rademacher complexity of a hypothesis class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a class of predictors, let \(L(y,u)\in[0,M]\) be \(L_0\)-Lipschitz in \(u\), and let \((X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) be i.i.d. Define \(R(h)=\mathbb E[L(Y,h(X))]\) and \(\widehat R_n(h)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nL(Y_i,h(X_i))\). With probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[\sup_{h\in H}|R(h)-\widehat R_n(h)|\leq2L_0\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(H)+3M\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}.\]
Thus \(\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(H)=O(n^{-1/2})\) implies a uniform \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) prediction-risk rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz loss transfers hypothesis-class Rademacher complexity into a uniform prediction-risk rate, with an additional confidence term of inverse square-root order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The uniform prediction-risk deviation is bounded by the displayed hypothesis-complexity and confidence terms.

notation.meaning: Empirical Rademacher complexity of predictor outputs.

review_flags: Exact constants depend on the contraction convention; an authoritative matching locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rate transfer is standard in form, but the exact coefficient depends on the empirical-Rademacher and contraction conventions. No source fixes those conventions or constants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial growth bound from VC dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth-function consequence of Sauer's lemma, with fixed VC dimension for the asymptotic notation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If $H$ is a hypothesis set with $\operatorname{VCdim}(H)=d\ge 1$, then for every $m\ge d$, $\Pi_H(m)\le\left(\frac{em}{d}\right)^d$. For fixed $d$, this gives $\Pi_H(m)=O(m^d)$ as $m\to\infty$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypothesis class of positive VC dimension d realizes at most (em/d)^d dichotomies when m is at least d. For fixed d, its growth is polynomial in m of degree at most d.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a binary hypothesis set}
d\text{ is fixed for the }O(m^d)\text{ statement}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi_H(m)\le\left(\frac{em}{d}\right)^d,\qquad \Pi_H(m)=O(m^d)\text{ for fixed }d.

source_evidence.locator: Rademacher Complexity and VC-Dimension / 3.3. VC-dimension / Corollary 3.3

source_refs.locator: Rademacher Complexity and VC-Dimension / 3.3. VC-dimension / Corollary 3.3

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial growth bound from VC dimension

source_witnesses.locator: Rademacher Complexity and VC-Dimension / 3.3. VC-dimension / Corollary 3.3

directory_assessment.rationale: The A16 node is a legitimate statistical-complexity specialization, but its DRO calibration path should not become the primary home of the general Sauer growth bound.

children.title: Decision-Class Complexity Rates
children.top_down_role: Finite-sample rates governed by the richness of feasible decision policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Class Complexity Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform objective-estimation rate governed directly by the complexity of the induced decision-loss class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a decision class and \(\mathcal F_X=\{z\mapsto f(x,z):x\in X\}\), where every \(f\in\mathcal F_X\) takes values in \([0,M]\). For i.i.d. observations, define \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,Z)]\) and \(\widehat F_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf(x,Z_i)\). Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[\sup_{x\in X}|F(x)-\widehat F_n(x)|\leq2\widehat{\mathfrak R}_n(\mathcal F_X)+3M\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}.\]
Consequently, if \(\widehat x_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\widehat F_n(x)\), then \(F(\widehat x_n)-\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\) is at most twice the displayed deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision-loss complexity controls uniform objective error and, after empirical minimization, yields an excess decision-risk bound twice as large.
assumptions_latex: An empirical minimizer exists when the excess-risk conclusion is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform objective error has the displayed rate, and empirical minimization incurs at most twice that error in population excess risk.

notation.meaning: Loss-function class induced by feasible decisions.

review_flags: An authoritative locator for the stated Rademacher and excess-risk constants is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform deviation and twice-deviation excess-risk implication are plausible, and complexity_bound fits the leaf, but no authoritative locator supports the exact empirical-Rademacher constants.

children.title: Prediction-to-Decision Rate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Regimes connecting predictive class control to downstream DRO decision guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Prediction-to-Decision Rate Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of prediction error into downstream decision regret under stability and curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h_0\) be the true predictive object and let \(x(h)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}J(x,h)\). Suppose that for all relevant \(h\),
\[J(x(h),h_0)-J(x(h_0),h_0)\leq C\,d(h,h_0)^\alpha\]
for constants \(C<\infty\) and \(\alpha>0\). If an estimator \(\widehat h_n\) satisfies \(d(\widehat h_n,h_0)=O_{\mathbb P}(r_n)\), then its induced decision \(\widehat x_n=x(\widehat h_n)\) satisfies
\[J(\widehat x_n,h_0)-J(x(h_0),h_0)=O_{\mathbb P}(r_n^\alpha).\]
The same implication holds deterministically whenever the prediction-error bound is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stability inequality converts prediction error of order r into downstream decision regret of order r raised to the stability exponent.
assumptions_latex: The displayed prediction-to-regret stability inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J(x(\widehat h_n),h_0)-J(x(h_0),h_0)=O_{\mathbb P}(r_n^\alpha)\).

notation.meaning: Decision optimized using predictive object h.

review_flags: The stability exponent is problem-dependent; a source specifying conditions that imply the inequality is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rate implication follows from the assumed stability inequality, and property fits the transfer leaf. A source is still required to establish meaningful conditions under which that problem-dependent inequality holds.

children.title: Class-Mismatch Rate Degradation
children.top_down_role: Rate deterioration caused by mismatched hypothesis or decision classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Class-Mismatch Rate Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample prediction-to-decision rate transfer with an explicitly indexed class-mismatch term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(n\), let \(\mathcal H_n\) be a hypothesis class, let \(\mathcal D\) be a decision class, and let \(A_n:\mathcal H_n\to\mathcal D\). Let \(R_{\rm pred}\) and \(R_{\rm dec}\) be prediction and decision risks. Suppose \[R_{\rm pred}(\widehat h_n)-\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_n}R_{\rm pred}(h)\le r_n\] and, for every \(h\in\mathcal H_n\), \[R_{\rm dec}(A_n(h))-\inf_{d\in\mathcal D}R_{\rm dec}(d)\le \psi\!\left(R_{\rm pred}(h)-\inf_{g\in\mathcal H_n}R_{\rm pred}(g)\right)+\delta_n,\] where \(\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is nondecreasing and \(\delta_n\ge0\). Then \[R_{\rm dec}(A_n(\widehat h_n))-\inf_{d\in\mathcal D}R_{\rm dec}(d)\le\psi(r_n)+\delta_n.\] This bound certifies decision consistency when \(\psi(r_n)+\delta_n\to0\). A mismatch term bounded away from zero prevents this bound from certifying consistency, while a more slowly vanishing \(\delta_n\) dominates the displayed upper-bound rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision regret is at most the calibrated prediction-rate term plus class mismatch. The bound certifies consistency only when their sum vanishes, and its rate is dominated by the more slowly vanishing term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\rm dec}(A_n(\widehat h_n))-\inf_{d\in\mathcal D}R_{\rm dec}(d)\le\psi(r_n)+\delta_n\).

notation.meaning: Class-mismatch contribution at sample size n.

knowledge_statements.title: Price of Distributional Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value premium paid when enlarging a nominal distribution into a nested ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty decision set, let \(\ell:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\) be integrable under every relevant distribution, and let \(\{\mathcal P_\rho\}_{\rho\ge0}\) satisfy \(\mathcal P_0=\{\widehat P\}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\rho_1}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\rho_2}\) whenever \(\rho_1\le\rho_2\). Define \[V(\rho)=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\rho}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)].\] The price of distributional robustness at radius \(\rho\) is \(\Pi(\rho)=V(\rho)-V(0)\). Nestedness implies that \(V\) and \(\Pi\) are nondecreasing and that \(\Pi(\rho)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The price of robustness is the increase in optimal worst-case value over the nominal problem; nested ambiguity sets make this premium nonnegative and nondecreasing.
assumptions_latex: \(V(\rho)\) is finite for the radii under consideration.
\(\mathcal P_0=\{\widehat P\}\) and the ambiguity sets are nested in \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi(\rho)=V(\rho)-V(0)\ge0\), and \(\rho_1\le\rho_2\) implies \(\Pi(\rho_1)\le\Pi(\rho_2)\).

children.title: Radius Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Local variation of DRO values or solutions with the ambiguity radius.

knowledge_statements.title: Radius Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and optimizer sensitivity for a penalized representation of a radius-indexed DRO problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty convex subset of a normed vector space, and suppose \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho L(x)\) with \(0\le L(x)\le M<\infty\) for all \(x\in X\). Define \(V(\rho)=\inf_{x\in X}\Phi_\rho(x)\). For every \(0\le\rho_1\le\rho_2\), \[0\le V(\rho_2)-V(\rho_1)\le M(\rho_2-ho_1).\] If each \(\Phi_\rho\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(X\), with respect to the displayed norm, and attains its minimum at \(x_\rho\), then \[\lVert x_{\rho_2}-x_{\rho_1}\rVert\le\sqrt{M(\rho_2-ho_1)/\mu}.\] Thus bounded nonnegative radius penalties give Lipschitz value sensitivity, while uniform strong convexity gives one-half Hölder optimizer sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded nonnegative ambiguity penalty makes the robust value Lipschitz in radius. On a convex domain, uniform strong convexity additionally gives a square-root stability bound for the unique optimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty convex subset of a normed vector space.
For optimizer sensitivity, each \(\Phi_\rho\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(X\) in the stated norm and attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le V(\rho_2)-V(\rho_1)\le M(\rho_2-ho_1)\) and \(\lVert x_{\rho_2}-x_{\rho_1}\rVert\le\sqrt{M(\rho_2-ho_1)/\mu}\).

notation.meaning: Unique robust optimizer at radius rho.

children.title: Solution Paths
children.top_down_role: Global evolution of DRO solutions across robustness levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued trajectory of optimal DRO decisions as the ambiguity radius varies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a radius-indexed ambiguity family \(\{\mathcal P_\rho\}_{\rho\in I}\), define \[S(\rho)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\rho}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)].\] The DRO solution path is the graph \(\operatorname{gph}S=\{(\rho,x):\rho\in I,\ x\in S(\rho)\}\). If \(I\) and \(X\) are compact, the robust objective is finite and jointly continuous in \((\rho,x)\), and every \(S(\rho)\) is nonempty, then \(S\) is compact-valued and upper hemicontinuous. When each minimizer is unique, the path is the ordinary function \(\rho\mapsto x_\rho\), which is continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution path is the graph of robust minimizers over ambiguity radii; standard compactness and continuity conditions yield upper hemicontinuity, or continuity under uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: The robust objective is finite and jointly continuous in \((\rho,x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is compact-valued and upper hemicontinuous; if \(S(\rho)=\{x_\rho\}\), then \(\rho\mapsto x_\rho\) is continuous.

notation.meaning: Set of robust minimizers at radius rho.

children.title: Path Breakpoints
children.top_down_role: Robustness levels where active structures or solution identities change.

knowledge_statements.title: Path Breakpoints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radii at which a specified structural signature changes locally or a selected DRO solution path is nondifferentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_\rho\) be a uniquely selected solution path on an interval \(I\), and let \(\sigma:I\to\Sigma\) be a specified finite-valued structural signature, such as an active-constraint set, worst-case support, or optimal basis. A radius \(\bar\rho\in\operatorname{int}I\) is a path breakpoint if either no neighborhood \(U\subseteq I\) of \(\bar\rho\) makes \(\sigma\) constant on \(U\), or the map \(\rho\mapsto x_\rho\) is not differentiable at \(\bar\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path breakpoint is an interior radius where the chosen finite structural signature is not locally constant or the selected robust optimizer is not differentiable.
assumptions_latex: A unique solution selection \(x_\rho\) is defined on the interval \(I\).
\(\sigma:I\to\Sigma\) is a specified finite-valued structural signature.
Differentiability is interpreted relative to the ambient space containing the solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar\rho\) is a breakpoint exactly when \(\sigma\) is not locally constant at \(\bar\rho\) or \(\rho\mapsto x_\rho\) is not differentiable there.

notation.meaning: Selected robust optimizer at radius rho.

children.title: Radius-Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes featuring discontinuity, instability, or nonunique path behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Radius-Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoints of maximal radius intervals on which a prescribed solution property remains invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S(\rho)\) be the DRO solution correspondence on an interval \(I\), fix \(\rho_0\in I\), and let \(\mathsf P(S(\rho))\) be a specified stability predicate, such as equality of active sets, uniqueness, or \(d_H(S(\rho),S(\rho_0))\le\varepsilon\). Let \(C_{\rho_0}\) be the connected component containing \(\rho_0\) of \[\{\rho\in I:\mathsf P(S(\rho))\text{ holds}\}.\] The lower and upper radius-stability boundaries are \(\rho_- =\inf C_{\rho_0}\) and \(\rho_+=\sup C_{\rho_0}\). They delimit the maximal connected radius regime around \(\rho_0\) satisfying the chosen predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radius-stability boundaries are the endpoints of the largest connected radius interval around a reference radius where a specified solution property remains valid.
assumptions_latex: The stability predicate \(\mathsf P\) and reference radius \(\rho_0\) are fixed.
The predicate holds at \(\rho_0\), so the containing component is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\rho_0}\subseteq[\rho_-,\rho_+]\) is the maximal connected stability regime containing \(\rho_0\).

notation.meaning: Connected stability component containing the reference radius.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicate-dependent construction is internally coherent and fits the terminal, but no source establishes this terminology or its use as a DRO stability-boundary definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias–Variance–Robustness Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates estimator error from the objective premium introduced by distributional robustness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat\theta_\rho\in\mathbb R^d\) be a square-integrable estimator or data-dependent decision at radius \(\rho\), and let \(\theta_0\in\mathbb R^d\) be its target. Then \[\mathbb E\lVert\widehat\theta_\rho-\theta_0\rVert^2=\lVert\mathbb E\widehat\theta_\rho-\theta_0\rVert^2+\mathbb E\lVert\widehat\theta_\rho-\mathbb E\widehat\theta_\rho\rVert^2.\] If the ambiguity sets are nested, the robustness premium \(\Pi(\rho)=V(\rho)-V(0)\) is nonnegative and nondecreasing. Hence radius selection jointly compares squared bias, sampling variance, and robustness premium; neither bias nor variance is universally monotone in \(\rho\) without additional model assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radius selection balances the estimator's exact bias–variance decomposition against a nondecreasing robustness premium; bias and variance need not individually vary monotonically.
assumptions_latex: The ambiguity sets defining \(V(\rho)\) are nested and \(V(\rho)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MSE}(\widehat\theta_\rho)=\operatorname{Bias}(\widehat\theta_\rho)^2+\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\theta_\rho)\) while \(\Pi(\rho)\) is nondecreasing.

notation.meaning: Data-dependent estimator or decision at radius rho.
Robustness premium relative to radius zero.
