knowledge_statements.title: Path-Distribution Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity imposed directly on probability laws over complete multistage uncertainty trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Xi=\Xi_1\times\cdots\times\Xi_T\) be a measurable path space and let \(\widehat P\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\) be a nominal joint law. Given a discrepancy \(D\), radius \(\rho\ge0\), and measurable moment functions \(g_j\), a path-distribution ambiguity set is \[\mathfrak P_\rho=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):D(P,\widehat P)\le\rho,\ \underline m_j\le\mathbb E_P[g_j(\xi_{1:T})]\le\overline m_j\ \text{for all }j\right\}.\] Its elements specify joint trajectory laws and may couple conditional distributions across stages; consequently, the set need not be rectangular or dynamically decomposable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path-distribution ambiguity constrains entire joint trajectory laws by distance and moment conditions, potentially coupling uncertainty choices across time.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a specified discrepancy on probability laws over \(\Xi\).
All displayed expectations exist for every feasible path law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak P_\rho\subseteq\mathcal P(\Xi_1\times\cdots\times\Xi_T)\) is an ambiguity set of complete path distributions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction plausibly represents ambiguity over complete path laws, but no dynamic-DRO source is supplied. The index set for the moment functions and bounds is also not introduced.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Kernel Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity specified through admissible conditional laws at successive histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t=\Xi_1\times\cdots\times\Xi_t\), let \(P_1\) be an admissible initial law, and for each \(t<T\) let \(\mathcal K_{t+1}(h_t)\) be a nonempty set of probability kernels on \(\Xi_{t+1}\). The conditional-kernel ambiguity family consists of all path laws admitting the factorization \[P(d\xi_{1:T})=P_1(d\xi_1)\prod_{t=1}^{T-1}K_{t+1}(d\xi_{t+1}\mid h_t),\qquad K_{t+1}(\cdot\mid h_t)\in\mathcal K_{t+1}(h_t)\] for applicable histories \(h_t\). Measurable kernel selections are required so that the product defines a probability law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional-kernel ambiguity constructs path laws from stagewise conditional distributions selected from history-dependent admissible kernel sets.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal K_{t+1}\) admits measurable kernel selections.
The selected kernels and initial law define a path measure on the product sigma-algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible path law factors into an initial law and admissible history-conditioned transition kernels.

notation.meaning: Conditional kernel for the next uncertainty.
Admissible conditional-kernel set at a history.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The factorized-kernel representation fits the terminal, but a source is needed for the ambiguity convention and for whether kernel membership is required at every history or only almost surely under the induced law.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Distance Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-law ambiguity measured by transport couplings that respect both filtrations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P,Q\) be probability laws on \(\Xi_1\times\cdots\times\Xi_T\), and let \(c_t:\Xi_t\times\Xi_t\to[0,\infty)\) be measurable stage costs. Write \(\Pi_{\rm bc}(P,Q)\) for couplings whose conditional transport kernels are causal in both directions. For \(p\ge1\), define the nested distance \[d_{\rm nest,p}(P,Q)=\left(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\rm bc}(P,Q)}\mathbb E_\pi\left[\sum_{t=1}^T c_t(\xi_t,\zeta_t)^p\right]\right)^{1/p}.\] Given a nominal law \(\widehat P\), the corresponding ambiguity ball is \(\mathfrak P_\rho^{\rm nest}=\{Q:d_{\rm nest,p}(Q,\widehat P)\le\rho\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested-distance ambiguity contains path laws close to a nominal law under transport couplings that preserve the information structure in both directions.
assumptions_latex: The bicausal coupling set \(\Pi_{\rm bc}(P,Q)\) is nonempty.
The stage costs have finite aggregate moment under at least one bicausal coupling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak P_\rho^{\rm nest}=\{Q:d_{\rm nest,p}(Q,\widehat P)\le\rho\}\).

notation.meaning: Set of bicausal couplings of P and Q.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed bicausal-transport formula is a plausible nested-distance convention, but exact conventions vary regarding stage costs, filtrations, and null histories. An authoritative nested-distance source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: State–Action Transition Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity sets for controlled transition laws indexed by state–action pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathsf S\) and \(\mathsf A\) be measurable state and action spaces. For each feasible pair \((s,a)\), let \(\mathcal Q(s,a)\subseteq\mathcal P(\mathsf S)\) be a nonempty set of next-state distributions. A state–action transition ambiguity model permits nature, after observing \((s_t,a_t)\), to choose \[Q_t(\cdot\mid s_t,a_t)\in\mathcal Q(s_t,a_t).\] If these choices can be made independently across pairs and stages, the induced transition family is rectangular. Coupling constraints among different \((s,a)\) pairs or stages instead produce a nonrectangular transition ambiguity model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State–action transition ambiguity assigns each feasible state–action pair a set of possible next-state laws; independent selections yield a rectangular model.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal Q(s,a)\) is nonempty and admits measurable selections.
Actions are selected from the feasible action set at each state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_t(\cdot\mid s_t,a_t)\in\mathcal Q(s_t,a_t)\) characterizes admissible ambiguous transitions.

notation.meaning: Set of admissible next-state laws at a state–action pair.
Selected transition kernel at stage t.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bellman optimality equations for a finite-state Markov decision process
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon and stationary finite-state recursions, together with their lookup-table dimensionality boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For discrete states \(s\in\mathcal S\), admissible actions \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), rewards \(r(s,a)\), and transition probabilities \(P(s'\mid s,a)\), the finite-horizon optimal value satisfies \[V_t(s)=\max_{a\in\mathcal A_s}\left\{r(s,a)+\sum_{s'\in\mathcal S}P(s'\mid s,a)V_{t+1}(s')\right\}.\] Given \(V_T\), this recursion can be evaluated backward. If \(V_t(s)\to V(s)\) as \(t\to\infty\), then \[V(s)=\max_{a\in\mathcal A_s}\left\{r(s,a)+\sum_{s'\in\mathcal S}P(s'\mid s,a)V(s')\right\}.\] Exact lookup-table computation scales exponentially when state, random-information, or action dimensions generate exponentially large discrete spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-state Markov decision process obeys Bellman's backward optimality recursion; under an assumed stationary-value limit it obeys the corresponding fixed-point equation. Exact tabular computation avoids enumerating decision trees but can suffer exponential growth in the state, uncertainty, and action spaces.
assumptions_latex: V_T\text{ is given for the finite-horizon recursion}
V_t(s)\to V(s)\text{ for the stationary equation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_t(s)=\max_{a\in\mathcal A_s}\left\{r(s,a)+\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)V_{t+1}(s')\right\},\quad V(s)=\max_{a\in\mathcal A_s}\left\{r(s,a)+\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)V(s')\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Worst-Case Transition Formulation of Robust MPC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Open-loop robust planning over state-transition support sets, with its conservatism and tractability boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(s,a)\) be the set of possible successor states, for example the support of a conditional transition distribution. A worst-case finite-horizon open-loop plan solves \[\max_{a_{1:d}}\min_{s_{2:d}}\sum_{t=1}^{d}\gamma^tR(s_t,a_t)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad s_{t+1}\in T(s_t,a_t),\ t=1,\ldots,d-1.\] Using full support can cause uncertainty to accumulate and yield highly conservative behavior; restricting each transition set to a high-probability region reduces conservatism but no longer protects against all supported outcomes. The resulting minimax problem need not be convex and may be difficult to solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust MPC chooses an action sequence against the worst admissible sequence of state transitions. Full-support uncertainty can be very conservative, while truncating the transition set trades robustness for reduced conservatism; the minimax problem is often nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: T(s,a)\subseteq S\text{ is the admissible successor-state set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{a_{1:d}}\min_{s_{2:d}}\sum_{t=1}^{d}\gamma^tR(s_t,a_t)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad s_{t+1}\in T(s_t,a_t)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Likelihood-Regularized Adversarial Reformulation of a Fixed Policy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a deterministic adversarial decision problem for robustness analysis of a fixed policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an MDP with state space \(\mathcal S\), reward \(R\), transition model \(T\), a fixed policy \(\pi\), and \(\lambda\ge 0\), define an adversarial problem with state space \(\mathcal S'=\mathcal S\), action space \(\mathcal A'=\mathcal S\), deterministic transition \(T'(s,a,a)=1\), and reward \[R'(s,a)=-R(s,\pi(s))+\lambda\log T(a\mid s,\pi(s)).\] Maximizing cumulative adversarial reward maximizes the negative cumulative policy reward plus \(\lambda\) times the log probability of the selected trajectory under \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed policy, let an adversary choose each next state. Its one-step reward is the negative reward earned by the policy plus lambda times the log probability of the chosen transition. The resulting dynamics move deterministically to the chosen state, and maximizing total adversarial reward balances finding low-return trajectories against keeping those trajectories likely under the original transition model.
assumptions_latex: T(a\mid s,\pi(s))\text{ is the original probability of transitioning to }a
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_t R'(s_t,s_{t+1})=-\sum_t R(s_t,\pi(s_t))+\lambda\log\!\left(\prod_t T(s_{t+1}\mid s_t,\pi(s_t))\right).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality growth for finite componentwise state, outcome, and action spaces; continuous action spaces are identified separately and are not covered by the finite cardinality count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a state vector S_t=(S_{t1},\ldots,S_{tI}) with at most L values per component, the state space can contain up to L^I states. For an outcome vector W_t=(W_{t1},\ldots,W_{tJ}) with at most M outcomes per component, the outcome space can contain up to M^J outcomes. For a finite action vector x_t=(x_{t1},\ldots,x_{tK}) with at most N choices per component, the action space can contain up to N^K actions. Thus state, outcome, and action spaces may each grow exponentially in their respective dimensions. In mathematical programming, the action space is the feasible region and may instead be continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each of I state components has at most L values, there can be up to L^I states; if each of J random-outcome components has at most M outcomes, there can be up to M^J joint outcomes; and if each of K finite action components has at most N choices, there can be up to N^K actions. These are the state-space, outcome-space, and action-space curses of dimensionality. The action space is the feasible region and may be discrete or continuous, with the finite N^K count applying only to the discrete case.
assumptions_latex: x_t=(x_{t1},\ldots,x_{tK}),\quad |\mathcal X_{tk}|\le N\text{ for the finite-action count}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathcal S_t|\le L^I,\qquad |\mathcal W_t|\le M^J,\qquad |\mathcal X_t|\le N^K,\text{ so these spaces may grow exponentially with dimension.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Construction of the Adversarial Policy-Validation MDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state construction; subsequent solution may use dynamic programming or deterministic search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite MDP \(P=(\mathcal S,\mathcal A,T,R,\gamma)\), fixed policy \(\pi\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), construct \(P'=(\mathcal S',\mathcal A',T',R',\gamma)\) by setting \(\mathcal S'=\mathcal A'=\mathcal S\) and, for every \(s,a\in\mathcal S\), \[R'(s,a)=-R(s,\pi(s))+\lambda\log T(a\mid s,\pi(s)),\qquad T'(a\mid s,a)=1.\] Solving \(P'\) yields an adversarial policy \(\pi':\mathcal S\to\mathcal S\) whose induced deterministic trajectory trades off low original reward against likelihood under \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every current state and candidate next state, assign the negative policy reward plus a likelihood penalty as the adversarial reward, and make the candidate next state the deterministic successor. Solving this finite adversarial MDP produces a state-to-next-state policy that searches for plausible trajectories with low original reward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P'\text{ is deterministic and an optimal adversarial policy has type }\pi':\mathcal S\to\mathcal S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationary deterministic policy and average-reward representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representation for a finite MDP under the source's stationary deterministic policy convention. The average-reward formula requires limiting state probabilities under the policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal S\) and each \(\mathcal A(i)\) be finite, and let \(\mu\) be a stationary deterministic policy with \(\mu(i)\in\mathcal A(i)\). The induced transition and transition-reward matrices are
\[
P_\mu(i,j)=p(i,\mu(i),j),\qquad R_\mu(i,j)=r(i,\mu(i),j).
\]
The expected immediate reward is
\[
\bar r(i,a)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal S}p(i,a,j)r(i,a,j).
\]
If the limiting probabilities \(\Pi_\mu(i)\) exist, the policy's average reward is
\[
\rho_\mu=\sum_{i\in\mathcal S}\Pi_\mu(i)\bar r(i,\mu(i)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary deterministic policy fixes one action for each state. It induces transition and reward matrices by selecting the corresponding state-action rows. Expected immediate rewards average over next states, and when limiting state probabilities exist, their weighted sum gives the policy's average reward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_\mu(i,j)=p(i,\mu(i),j),\quad R_\mu(i,j)=r(i,\mu(i),j),\quad \bar r(i,a)=\sum_jp(i,a,j)r(i,a,j),\quad \rho_\mu=\sum_i\Pi_\mu(i)\bar r(i,\mu(i))

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Rectangularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent recombination of admissible one-step conditional laws across stages and histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K_{t+1}(h_t)\) be nonempty sets of conditional probability kernels and let \(\mathcal P_1\) be a set of initial laws. A multistage ambiguity family \(\mathfrak P\) is stagewise rectangular when \[\mathfrak P=\left\{P_1(d\xi_1)\prod_{t=1}^{T-1}K_{t+1}(d\xi_{t+1}\mid h_t):P_1\in\mathcal P_1,\ K_{t+1}(\cdot\mid h_t)\in\mathcal K_{t+1}(h_t)\right\},\] with every admissible measurable recombination included. Thus selecting a permissible kernel at one stage or history imposes no additional coupling restriction on selections at other stages or histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise rectangularity means every measurable recombination of locally admissible conditional kernels is itself an admissible path law.
assumptions_latex: The displayed products define probability laws on the path space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak P\) is closed under independent measurable recombination of its admissible stagewise conditional kernels.

notation.meaning: Admissible next-stage conditional laws at a history.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recombination condition captures a standard intuition for stagewise rectangularity, but precise rectangularity definitions depend on historywise null sets and measurable kernel-selection conventions. No supporting source is supplied.

children.title: State Rectangularity
children.top_down_role: Rectangular ambiguity organized conditionally by state.

assumptions_latex: The state space \(S\) and action space \(A\) are finite.
For each \(s\in S\), \(\mathcal P_s\) is a nonempty subset of \(\prod_{a\in A}\Delta(S)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The admissible transition laws are exactly those obtained by independently selecting one action-indexed kernel vector from each \(\mathcal P_s\).

notation.meaning: Probability simplex on the finite state space
Ambiguity set of action-indexed transition distributions at state s
Global ambiguity set of transition kernels

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state robust-MDP definition allowing dependence among action kernels at a fixed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A transition-kernel ambiguity set is state rectangular if there exist nonempty sets \(\mathcal P_s\subseteq\prod_{a\in A}\Delta(S)\) such that
\[
\mathcal P^{s}=\left\{P:\bigl(P(\cdot\mid s,a)\bigr)_{a\in A}\in\mathcal P_s\ \text{for every }s\in S\right\}=\prod_{s\in S}\mathcal P_s.
\]
Thus nature may choose a different vector of action-conditioned transition distributions at each state, independently across states, while the components \(P(\cdot\mid s,a)\) for different actions at the same state may remain coupled through \(\mathcal P_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State rectangularity permits independent ambiguity choices across states while retaining arbitrary dependence among the transition distributions associated with different actions at the same state.
knowledge_statements.title: State Rectangularity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source verifies the precise state-rectangular convention or locator.

children.title: State–Action Rectangularity
children.top_down_role: Rectangular ambiguity organized conditionally by state–action pairs.

assumptions_latex: The state space \(S\) and action space \(A\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nature can select every state-action transition distribution independently of all other state-action pairs.

notation.meaning: Ambiguity set for the transition distribution at state-action pair (s,a)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state robust-MDP definition with independent ambiguity at every state-action pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A transition-kernel ambiguity set is state-action rectangular if there exist nonempty sets \(\mathcal P_{s,a}\subseteq\Delta(S)\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal P^{sa}=\prod_{(s,a)\in S\times A}\mathcal P_{s,a}
=\left\{P:P(\cdot\mid s,a)\in\mathcal P_{s,a}\ \text{for every }(s,a)\in S\times A\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, any collection formed by choosing one distribution \(p_{s,a}\in\mathcal P_{s,a}\) separately for each state-action pair defines an admissible kernel. This excludes ambiguity-set constraints coupling transition distributions across distinct actions or states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State-action rectangularity makes the admissible transition distribution at each state-action pair independently selectable from its own ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.title: State–Action Rectangularity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the exact state–action rectangular convention has no supporting citation.

children.title: Rectangularity Comparison Regimes
children.top_down_role: Differences in admissible dependence and policy evaluation under the two variants.

assumptions_latex: For each \(s\in S\), \(\mathcal P_s\subseteq\prod_{a\in A}\Delta(S)\) is nonempty.
The marginal projection is \(\mathcal P_{s,a}=\{p_a:(p_b)_{b\in A}\in\mathcal P_s\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state-rectangular set is contained in its state-action rectangular hull, with equality exactly under within-state product closure.

notation.meaning: State-action rectangular hull formed from marginal projections
Worst-case expected total cost under policy pi

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison through the state-action rectangular hull of a state-rectangular ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\mathcal P^{s}=\prod_{s\in S}\mathcal P_s\) and its state-action rectangular hull by
\[
\widehat{\mathcal P}^{sa}=\prod_{s\in S}\prod_{a\in A}\mathcal P_{s,a}.
\]
Then \(\mathcal P^{s}\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal P}^{sa}\), and equality holds if and only if \(\mathcal P_s=\prod_{a\in A}\mathcal P_{s,a}\) for every \(s\in S\). Consequently, for every fixed policy \(\pi\) and cost criterion for which the expectations exist,
\[
J(\pi,\mathcal P^{s})\leq J(\pi,\widehat{\mathcal P}^{sa}),\qquad J(\pi,\mathcal P):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P^{\pi}[C].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The state-action rectangular hull removes within-state coupling, enlarges the ambiguity set, and cannot decrease worst-case cost. Equality holds precisely when every state set already factors by action.
knowledge_statements.title: Rectangularity Comparison Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hull inclusion and worst-case-cost monotonicity are coherent, but neither the comparison regime nor its equality characterization has cited support.

children.title: Policy-Conditioning Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where the chosen conditioning structure fails to support the intended dynamic model.

assumptions_latex: At a state \(s\), the controller uses a randomized action law \(\mu\in\Delta(A)\).
Nature's admissible transition vectors form \(\mathcal P_s\subseteq\prod_{a\in A}\Delta(S)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whether nature conditions on the realized action is determined by the order of randomization and ambiguity selection.

notation.meaning: Randomized action distribution at state s
Transition distribution selected for action a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier-order boundary between pre-action state conditioning and post-action state-action conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If nature observes \(s\) but must choose the entire vector \((p_a)_{a\in A}\in\mathcal P_s\) before the controller's random action is realized, the local worst-case continuation is
\[
\sup_{(p_a)_{a\in A}\in\mathcal P_s}\sum_{a\in A}\mu(a)\sum_{s'\in S}p_a(s')V(s').
\]
If nature may additionally condition its choice on the realized action, the value becomes
\[
\sum_{a\in A}\mu(a)\sup_{p\in\mathcal P_{s,a}}\sum_{s'\in S}p(s')V(s').
\]
The latter is at least the former and can be strictly larger when \(\mathcal P_s\) couples its action components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observing the realized action lets nature optimize separately by action; choosing before action randomization preserves within-state coupling and can yield a smaller worst-case continuation cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Conditioning Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantifier-order boundary fits the leaf, but the timing and information conventions governing nature's action-conditioned choice require an explicit source.

assumptions_latex: The horizon \(T<\infty\) and the canonical history spaces are measurable.
For each history \(h_t\), \(\mathfrak K_t(h_t)\) is a nonempty set of admissible one-step conditional kernels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ambiguity family contains every path law assembled by admissible history-dependent one-step kernel selections, and it is stable under admissible pasting.

notation.meaning: Admissible next-stage kernels after history h_t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon history-dependent kernel formulation of nested rectangularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An ambiguity family \(\mathfrak P\) is nested rectangular with respect to the history filtration if
\[
\mathfrak P=\left\{P_0\otimes K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{T-1}:K_t(\cdot\mid h_t)\in\mathfrak K_t(h_t)\ \text{for every }t<T\text{ and admissible }h_t\right\},
\]
subject to the required measurability of each kernel selection. Equivalently, whenever two measures in \(\mathfrak P\) agree up to a history \(h_t\), replacing the continuation kernels of one by admissible continuation kernels of the other after \(h_t\) produces another measure in \(\mathfrak P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested rectangularity means that admissible one-step conditional laws can be selected independently after each history and pasted into another admissible path law.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Rectangularity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits nested rectangularity, but the measurable-selection conditions and asserted equivalence with historywise pasting are not supported by a cited source.

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity family \(\mathfrak P\) consists of probability measures on a finite-horizon filtered path space.
Regular conditional continuation laws exist at every relevant history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonrectangularity occurs exactly when some admissible conditional continuation cannot be pasted onto an admissible prefix without leaving the ambiguity family.

notation.meaning: Measure obtained by pasting a prefix and continuation at h_t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure-of-pasting definition on a finite-horizon filtered path space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ambiguity family \(\mathfrak P\) is nonrectangular if it is not stable under conditional pasting: there exist \(P,Q\in\mathfrak P\), a time \(t<T\), and a history \(h_t\) having positive probability under the relevant prefix such that the measure \(P\otimes_{h_t}Q\), which follows \(P\) through \(h_t\) and thereafter uses an admissible conditional continuation law supplied by \(Q\), does not belong to \(\mathfrak P\). Thus the family imposes a cross-history or cross-time constraint that cannot be represented solely by independently selectable one-step conditional ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ambiguity family is nonrectangular when an admissible conditional continuation cannot always be combined with another admissible past, revealing a cross-time or cross-history coupling constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonrectangular Ambiguity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-of-pasting formulation is appropriate, but pasting at a particular history and the required positive-probability convention need authoritative specification.

assumptions_latex: The finite-horizon DRO problem admits optimal policies and regular conditional ambiguity sets \(\mathfrak P(h_t)\).
Continuation objectives are well defined at every history reached with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A policy is time consistent exactly when each of its prescribed continuations remains optimal for the corresponding conditional DRO problem.

notation.meaning: Continuation of pi after history h_t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong policy time consistency under conditional reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a continuation policy \(\rho\), define
\[
J_t(\rho,h_t)=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P(h_t)}\mathbb E_P^{\rho}\!\left[\sum_{k=t}^{T-1}c_k+c_T\,\middle|\,h_t\right].
\]
An optimal time-zero policy \(\pi^*\) is time consistent if, for every \(t\leq T\) and every history \(h_t\) reachable under \(\pi^*\),
\[
\pi^*_{t:}(h_t)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\rho}J_t(\rho,h_t).
\]
A DRO formulation is time consistent when it possesses such an optimal policy, or when every time-zero optimal policy has this property under the chosen convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DRO policy is time consistent when its planned continuation remains optimal after every reachable history under the ambiguity set conditioned at that history.
knowledge_statements.title: Time-Consistent DRO

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The policy-level condition fits the leaf, but the final sentence mixes existential and universal formulation-level conventions; a source must establish which convention is intended.

assumptions_latex: A time-zero optimal policy \(\pi^*\) and conditional continuation problems are well defined.
At least one reachable history permits a feasible continuation policy different from the planned continuation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Time inconsistency is witnessed by a reachable history at which reoptimization strictly improves the conditional worst-case objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure boundary defined by profitable conditional reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A time-zero optimal policy \(\pi^*\) is time inconsistent if there exist a time \(t<T\), a history \(h_t\) reachable under \(\pi^*\), and a feasible continuation policy \(\rho\) such that
\[
J_t(\rho,h_t)<J_t\bigl(\pi^*_{t:}(h_t),h_t\bigr),
\qquad
J_t(\eta,h_t):=\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P(h_t)}\mathbb E_P^{\eta}\!\left[\sum_{k=t}^{T-1}c_k+c_T\,\middle|\,h_t\right].
\]
Hence the action plan optimal under time-zero commitment is rejected by the same decision criterion after information \(h_t\) is observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DRO is time inconsistent when a policy optimal at time zero prescribes a continuation that is strictly suboptimal after some reachable history.
knowledge_statements.title: Time-Inconsistent DRO

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The profitable-reoptimization witness fits the failure-boundary container, but its reachable-history and strict-improvement convention lacks cited support.

assumptions_latex: The horizon and state-action spaces are finite.
Costs are bounded, and the transition ambiguity set is state-action rectangular with nonempty compact factors \(\mathcal P_{t,s,a}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust value satisfies a Bellman recursion, and stagewise minimizers form an optimal dynamically consistent Markov policy.

notation.meaning: Robust cost-to-go at time t and state s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon state-action rectangular robust-MDP version.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(V_T(s)=c_T(s)\). For \(t=T-1,\ldots,0\), define
\[
V_t(s)=\min_{a\in A(s)}\left\{c_t(s,a)+\sup_{p\in\mathcal P_{t,s,a}}\sum_{s'\in S}p(s')V_{t+1}(s')\right\}.
\]
Then \(V_t(s)\) equals the optimal worst-case expected cost from \((t,s)\). Any Markov policy selecting an action from the displayed minimizing set at every \((t,s)\) is optimal. Moreover, its continuation is optimal for every reached state-time pair, so the formulation is compatible with dynamic programming and is time consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under finite state-action rectangular ambiguity, backward robust Bellman recursion gives the exact value, and its minimizing selectors form an optimal time-consistent Markov policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Programming Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the leaf and the finite robust-MDP recursion is plausible, but the exact hypotheses, optimality conclusion, and time-consistency implication require an authoritative theorem citation.

children.title: Commitment Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dynamic DRO policies evaluated under ex ante commitment.

assumptions_latex: A policy \(\pi\) is selected at time zero from an admissible policy class \(\Pi\).
Nature selects a full path law from a fixed ambiguity family \(\mathfrak P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The commitment value evaluates one time-zero policy against one globally admissible worst-case path law without later resetting either choice.

notation.meaning: Time-zero ambiguity family of path laws

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precommitment formulation for a finite-horizon worst-case expected-cost problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For total cost \(C^\pi\), the commitment regime assigns the time-zero value
\[
V^{\mathrm{com}}=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}\mathbb E_P[C^\pi].
\]
The controller commits at time zero to the complete contingent policy \(\pi\), and nature's response is constrained to be a single path law \(P\) belonging to the original joint ambiguity family \(\mathfrak P\). At later histories, the prescribed continuation and the conditional law inherited from \(P\) are evaluated as parts of these time-zero choices rather than replaced by newly optimized objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a commitment regime, the controller fixes a complete contingent policy at time zero and evaluates it against a single worst-case joint law from the original ambiguity family.
knowledge_statements.title: Commitment Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits commitment regimes, but the single-path-law interpretation and timing of nature's response depend on an uncited game convention.

children.title: Reoptimization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dynamic DRO policies revised as information becomes available.

assumptions_latex: For every observed history \(h_t\), a conditional ambiguity family \(\mathfrak P_t(h_t)\) is specified.
Continuation policies belong to a feasible class \(\Pi_t(h_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At each history, the controller discards the previously planned continuation and solves the current conditional DRO problem.

notation.meaning: Conditional ambiguity family after history h_t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential conditional reoptimization under history-dependent ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At each time \(t\) and observed history \(h_t\), the reoptimization regime computes
\[
V_t^{\mathrm{re}}(h_t)=\inf_{\rho\in\Pi_t(h_t)}\sup_{Q\in\mathfrak P_t(h_t)}\mathbb E_Q^{\rho}\!\left[\sum_{k=t}^{T-1}c_k+c_T\,\middle|\,h_t\right].
\]
An action is implemented from a minimizing continuation policy, and the same conditional optimization is solved again after the next history is observed. The resulting strategy is therefore determined by the family of conditional problems, rather than by irrevocable adherence to a continuation policy selected at time zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reoptimization regime repeatedly solves the conditional DRO problem after each observed history and implements the current optimizer rather than an irrevocable time-zero continuation.
knowledge_statements.title: Reoptimization Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits reoptimization regimes, but the construction of the conditional ambiguity families and repeated-solution convention require a specific source.

children.title: Commitment–Reoptimization Gaps
children.top_down_role: Differences in value or policy induced by the two decision regimes.

assumptions_latex: The commitment and reoptimization problems use the same costs, feasible controls, and initial information.
Their conditional ambiguity-set convention is fixed and both values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The commitment-reoptimization gap vanishes under recursive stability and continuation optimality; without compatible conditioning, it may be nonzero and has no universal sign.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-gap statement separating the zero-gap rectangular case from convention-dependent nonrectangular cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the initial value gap by
\[
G=V^{\mathrm{re}}-V^{\mathrm{com}}.
\]
If the ambiguity family is stable under conditioning and pasting and a commitment-optimal policy has conditionally optimal continuations at every reachable history, sequential reoptimization implements that policy and \(G=0\). If either recursive stability or continuation optimality fails, a nonzero gap can occur. Without an explicit inclusion relation between the conditional ambiguity families used in reoptimization and the conditionals induced by the commitment family, neither \(G\geq0\) nor \(G\leq0\) follows universally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Commitment and reoptimization agree under rectangular conditioning and continuation optimality. Otherwise they may differ, and the gap's sign depends on how conditional ambiguity sets are constructed.
knowledge_statements.title: Commitment–Reoptimization Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the comparison leaf, but the zero-gap sufficiency conditions and assertion that no universal sign exists depend on conditioning conventions and need direct source support.

children.title: Time-Consistency Consequences
children.top_down_role: Dynamic-consistency implications of choosing commitment or sequential reoptimization.

assumptions_latex: Finite horizon and measurable stage costs.
Conditional ambiguity sets are rectangular with respect to the history filtration.
Stagewise infima and suprema are attained by measurable selectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t(h_t)=\inf_{a_t\in A_t(h_t)}\sup_{Q_t\in\mathcal Q_t(h_t,a_t)}\mathbb E_{Q_t}[c_t(h_t,a_t,\xi_{t+1})+V_{t+1}(h_{t+1})]\), and every Bellman-optimal continuation remains optimal after each reachable history.

notation.meaning: Conditional ambiguity set after a history-action pair

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rectangular conditional ambiguity permits recursive worst-case conditioning and dynamically consistent Bellman policies
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon rectangular version; nonrectangular ambiguity is outside scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_t\) be the history at stage \(t\), let \(A_t(h_t)\) be the feasible actions, and set \(V_T(h_T)=c_T(h_T)\). If the family of conditional ambiguity sets \(\mathcal Q_t(h_t,a_t)\) is rectangular, so that admissible joint laws are precisely compositions of independently selectable conditional kernels, then the committed minimax problem equals its backward recursion \[V_t(h_t)=\inf_{a_t\in A_t(h_t)}\sup_{Q_t\in\mathcal Q_t(h_t,a_t)}\mathbb E_{Q_t}\!\left[c_t(h_t,a_t,\xi_{t+1})+V_{t+1}(h_{t+1})\right].\] Consequently, a policy formed from measurable minimizing selectors is optimal both initially and after reoptimization at every reachable history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rectangular conditional ambiguity makes the committed minimax problem recursively decomposable, so Bellman-optimal policies remain optimal whenever the problem is re-solved after an observed history.
knowledge_statements.title: Time-Consistency Consequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the time-consistency leaf and states a plausible finite-horizon rectangularity result, but no source supports the precise equality, selector assumptions, or optimality after every reachable history.

assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite and rooted.
Each nonleaf node has a nonempty set of admissible child distributions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scenario-tree DRO value is \(V_r\), obtained by nodewise minimization followed by worst-case conditional expectation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree model with nodewise conditional ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scenario-tree distributionally robust optimization problem is specified by a finite rooted tree \(\mathcal T=(N,E)\), feasible node decisions \(x_n\in X_n(x_{\operatorname{pa}(n)})\), node costs \(c_n(x_n)\), and ambiguity sets \(\mathcal P_n\subseteq\Delta(C(n))\) at nonleaf nodes. Nonanticipativity is enforced by assigning one decision to each information node. With \(V_n=c_n\) at leaves, its value functions satisfy \[V_n(x_{\operatorname{pa}(n)})=\inf_{x_n\in X_n(x_{\operatorname{pa}(n)})}\left\{c_n(x_n)+\sup_{p\in\mathcal P_n}\sum_{m\in C(n)}p_mV_m(x_n)\right\}.\] The model value is the value at the root.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario-tree DRO assigns nonanticipative decisions to tree nodes and selects worst-case conditional branch probabilities from nodewise ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree DRO

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Scenario-Tree DRO, but the nodewise rectangular Bellman recursion is a substantive model restriction and has no cited source.

assumptions_latex: The state and action spaces are measurable.
The horizon is finite and all displayed expectations are well defined.
Every state-action pair has a nonempty ambiguity set of transition kernels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal robust value is \(\inf_\pi\sup_{P_t(\cdot\mid s,a)\in\mathcal P_t(s,a)}\mathbb E^{\pi,P}[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}c_t(S_t,A_t)+c_T(S_T)]\).

source_refs.locator: 3 Introduction to Markov Decision Processes p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite-horizon distributionally robust Markov decision process consists of measurable state spaces \(\mathsf S_t\), feasible actions \(A_t(s)\), costs \(c_t(s,a)\), terminal cost \(c_T(s)\), and nonempty ambiguity sets \(\mathcal P_t(s,a)\) of transition probability kernels on \(\mathsf S_{t+1}\). For an initial state \(s_0\), its minimax value is \[\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{P_t(\cdot\mid s,a)\in\mathcal P_t(s,a)}\mathbb E^{\pi,P}_{s_0}\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}c_t(S_t,A_t)+c_T(S_T)\right].\] State-action rectangularity means nature may select each conditional kernel independently within its corresponding ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributionally robust MDP minimizes expected cumulative cost against transition kernels selected adversarially from state-action-dependent ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributionally Robust Markov Decision Processes

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Introduction to Markov Decision Processes p. 57

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the DRMDP container, but the cited section concerns ordinary Markov decision processes and does not support transition-kernel ambiguity, state-action rectangularity, or the displayed minimax formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cooperative multi-agent sequential decision model with local partial observability and a shared objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP) is a partially observable Markov game in which every agent shares the same objective. Each agent \(i\in\mathcal I\) selects a local action \(a^i\in\mathcal A^i\) using its history of local observations in \(\mathcal O^i\); the agents share an underlying state \(s\in\mathcal S\), and the reward \(R(s,\mathbf a)\) depends on the state and joint action \(\mathbf a\). The agents jointly seek to maximize the shared expected reward over time subject to their local partial observability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Dec-POMDP is a partially observable Markov game with a common objective. Each agent chooses actions from its own observation history, while all agents share the underlying state and a reward determined by that state and their joint action. Their goal is to maximize the shared expected reward over time.
assumptions_latex: a^i\text{ is selected from agent }i\text{'s local observation history}
R:\mathcal S\times\mathcal A\to\mathbb R\text{ is shared by all agents}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{All agents optimize the same expected cumulative reward under local partial observability.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invariant and stationary measures of a transition operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures fixed by a Markov transition operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A probability measure $\pi$ is invariant, or stationary, for $\mathbf P$ if $\pi\mathbf P=\pi$. More generally, a measure $m$, not necessarily a probability measure, is invariant if $m\mathbf P=m$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary probability measure is unchanged by one application of the transition operator. The same fixed-point condition defines an invariant measure without requiring normalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(v\in\mathcal V\): (a) \(v\geq \mathcal Mv\) implies \(v\geq v^*\); (b) \(v\leq \mathcal Mv\) implies \(v\leq v^*\); and (c) \(v=\mathcal Mv\) implies that \(v\) is the unique solution of the Bellman equations and \(v=v^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider dynamics \(X_{t+1}=f_t(X_t,U_t,W_{t+1})\) for \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), where a causal policy \(\mu\in\mathcal M\) selects \(U_t=\mu_t(X_0,W_1,\ldots,X_t)\). Given stage costs \(\ell_t\), terminal cost \(\ell_T\), and a nonempty ambiguity set \(\mathcal Q\) of joint disturbance laws, distributionally robust control solves \[\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M}\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q}J(\mu,Q),\qquad J(\mu,Q)=\mathbb E_Q\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ell_t(X_t,U_t)+\ell_T(X_T)\right].\] Any structural restrictions on \(Q\), such as rectangular conditional ambiguity, are part of the model specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributionally robust control chooses a causal controller minimizing worst-case expected performance over an ambiguity set of disturbance laws.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the horizon \(T\), terminal cost \(c_T\), feasible actions \(A_t(s)\), stage costs \(c_t\), and rectangular transition ambiguity sets \(\mathcal P_t(s,a)\). Initialize \(V_T(s)=c_T(s)\). For \(t=T-1,\ldots,0\), compute \[V_t(s)=\inf_{a\in A_t(s)}\left\{c_t(s,a)+\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_t(s,a)}\int V_{t+1}(s')\,P(ds')\right\},\] and store a minimizing selector \(\pi_t^*(s)\). Stop after stage \(0\), and output \(\pi^*=(\pi_0^*,\ldots,\pi_{T-1}^*)\) together with \(V_0\); numerical implementations may stop inner solves when their prescribed tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust Bellman backward induction repeatedly minimizes immediate cost plus the worst-case expected next-stage value, storing a minimizing action at each state.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Batch LSTD estimator and temporal-difference moment equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear fixed-policy value approximation from a sample of \(n\) transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the LSTD sample matrix \(A^n\) and vector \(b^n\), if \(A^n\) is invertible, set \(\theta^n=(A^n)^{-1}b^n\). With \(\delta^i(\theta)=C(S^i,a^i,W^{i+1})+\gamma\phi(S^{i+1})^T\theta-\phi(S^i)^T\theta\), the sample residual satisfies \(A^n\theta-b^n=-\frac1n\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\phi(S^i)\delta^i(\theta)\). Hence the LSTD solution makes the empirical feature-weighted temporal-difference moment zero. Invertibility is not guaranteed, and generally one cannot make every sampled \(\delta^i(\theta)\) vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LSTD is a batch policy-evaluation algorithm. When its sample matrix is invertible, it solves a linear system for the value-function coefficients. The solution sets the empirical feature-weighted temporal-difference moment to zero, although individual temporal differences generally remain nonzero and the required inverse may not exist.
assumptions_latex: The value approximation is linear in \(\phi\).
\(A^n\) and \(b^n\) are the corresponding LSTD sample matrix and vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta^n=(A^n)^{-1}b^n\quad\text{and}\quad\frac1n\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\phi(S^i)\delta^i(\theta^n)=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LSPE update with empirical covariance scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive estimation of linear value-function parameters for a fixed policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: LSPE updates the parameter estimate by \(\theta^n=\theta^{n-1}-\frac{\alpha}{n}G^n\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\phi(S^i)\delta^i(n)\), where a natural scaling is \(G^n=\left(\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{i=0}^{n}\phi(S^i)\phi(S^i)^T\right)^{-1}\), whenever this empirical feature-covariance matrix is invertible. If there is one one-hot feature per state and empirical visitation frequencies converge under \(\pi\), then \(\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{i=0}^{n}\phi(S^i)\phi(S^i)^T\to D^\pi\), the diagonal matrix of state-visitation probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LSPE successively updates the linear value-function coefficients using accumulated feature-weighted temporal differences and an inverse empirical feature-covariance scaling matrix. With one-hot state features, that covariance converges to the diagonal state-visitation distribution when visitation frequencies converge.
assumptions_latex: A fixed policy \(\pi\) generates the sampled states.
The value approximation is linear in \(\phi\).
The empirical matrix \(\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{i=0}^{n}\phi(S^i)\phi(S^i)^T\) is invertible when its inverse is used.
For the limiting tabular statement, \(\phi(s)\) is the one-hot feature vector for state \(s\) and empirical visitation frequencies converge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta^n=\theta^{n-1}-\frac{\alpha}{n}G^n\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\phi(S^i)\delta^i(n),\qquad G^n=\left(\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{i=0}^{n}\phi(S^i)\phi(S^i)^T\right)^{-1},\quad G_n^{-1}\to D^\pi\text{ in the tabular case}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic cut-based nested decomposition for convex multistage DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize valid lower approximations \(\underline V_t^0\) of all continuation values and set \(k=0\). In a forward pass, solve each stage problem using \(\underline V_{t+1}^k\), generating a feasible nonanticipative policy and an upper estimate \(U_k\). In a backward pass, visit stages in reverse order, solve the conditional worst-case subproblem at sampled or enumerated predecessor states, and add a valid supporting cut \(\alpha_t^k+\langle\beta_t^k,x\rangle\) to obtain \[\underline V_t^{k+1}(x)=\max\{\underline V_t^k(x),\alpha_t^k+\langle\beta_t^k,x\rangle\}.\] Compute the root lower bound \(L_k\), increment \(k\), and stop with the incumbent policy when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested decomposition alternates forward policy construction with backward worst-case continuation-value cuts until certified lower and upper bounds meet the requested tolerance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive finite-tree approximation workflow; no universal convergence rate asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial finite tree \(\mathcal T_0\), a refinement rule, a validation sample, and tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tree}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{val}}>0\). At iteration \(k\), assign conditional ambiguity sets to the nodes of \(\mathcal T_k\), solve the resulting nonanticipative scenario-tree DRO problem, and obtain policy \(\pi_k\) and value \(v_k\). Evaluate \(\pi_k\) on independent scenarios to compute a validation estimate \(\widehat e_k\). If the tree-refinement indicator is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tree}}\) and \(\widehat e_k\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{val}}\), return \(\pi_k\). Otherwise refine or rebalance \(\mathcal T_k\), set \(k\leftarrow k+1\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method repeatedly builds a finite uncertainty tree, solves its DRO model, validates the resulting policy independently, and refines the tree until both criteria pass.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines efficiency for long-only, fully invested portfolios using expected return and standard deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x_i\ge 0\ (i=1,\ldots,n),\ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i=1\}\), and let \(\mu(x)\) and \(\sigma(x)\) denote a portfolio's expected return and standard deviation. A portfolio \(x^0\in X\), with \((\mu_0,\sigma_0)=(\mu(x^0),\sigma(x^0))\), is efficient if \(\mu\) cannot be increased without increasing \(\sigma\), and \(\sigma\) cannot be decreased without decreasing \(\mu\). Equivalently, \(\max\{\mu(x):x\in X,\ \sigma(x)\le\sigma_0\}=\mu_0\) and \(\min\{\sigma(x):x\in X,\ \mu(x)\ge\mu_0\}=\sigma_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A long-only, fully invested portfolio is mean–standard-deviation efficient when no feasible portfolio can improve expected return without increasing standard deviation and none can reduce standard deviation without decreasing expected return. Equivalently, its return is maximal at its risk bound and its risk is minimal at its return bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{x\in X,\,\sigma(x)\le\sigma_0}\mu(x)=\mu_0\quad\text{and}\quad\min_{x\in X,\,\mu(x)\ge\mu_0}\sigma(x)=\sigma_0

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty M, the worst-case loss at x is \sigma_M(-x)=\sup_{\mu\in M}(-x^\top\mu). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-only ambiguity for a single-period linear-return portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be the feasible portfolio set and let \(M\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a nonempty set of admissible mean returns. Define \(\mathcal P_M=\{P:\mathbb E_P[\lVert R\rVert]<\infty,\ \mathbb E_P[R]\in M\}\). The moment-based worst-case expected-loss portfolio problem is \[\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_M}\mathbb E_P[-x^\top R].\] Because the loss is linear, its inner problem has the exact reduction \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_M}\mathbb E_P[-x^\top R]=\sup_{\mu\in M}(-x^\top\mu),\] provided every \(\mu\in M\) is realizable by at least one integrable return law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With mean-only ambiguity and linear portfolio loss, worst-case expected loss equals the support function of the admissible mean set evaluated at the negative portfolio.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}x^\top\Sigma x=x^\top\bar\Sigma x\quad\forall x.

notation.meaning: Loewner-greatest covariance in the ambiguity set.

knowledge_statements.title: Loewner-Maximal Covariance Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-analytic representation of worst-case portfolio variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S_+^d, let \sigma_{\mathcal S}(Y)=\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}\langle\Sigma,Y\rangle with \langle A,B\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(AB). Then \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}x^\top\Sigma x=\sigma_{\mathcal S}(xx^\top). The robust variance is finite exactly when xx^\top lies in the effective domain of \sigma_{\mathcal S}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case portfolio variance is the matrix support function of the covariance set evaluated at the portfolio outer product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}x^\top\Sigma x=\sigma_{\mathcal S}(xx^\top).

notation.meaning: Matrix support function of the covariance set.

knowledge_statements.title: Covariance Support-Function Representation

assumptions_latex: The mean return is fixed at a finite vector.
Every candidate covariance matrix is symmetric positive semidefinite and realizable.
The portfolio objective penalizes variance with a nonnegative coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The worst-case variance penalty is \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}x^\top\Sigma x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: variance of a linear portfolio return is the covariance quadratic form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-period mean-variance model with covariance-set ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), fix \(\mu_0\in\mathbb R^d\), and let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S_+^d\) be a nonempty set of realizable covariance matrices. For \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}=\{P:\mathbb E_P[R]=\mu_0,\ \operatorname{Cov}_P(R)\in\mathcal S\}\), a covariance-robust mean-variance portfolio solves \[\inf_{x\in X}\left\{-x^\top\mu_0+\lambda\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}}\operatorname{Var}_P(x^\top R)\right\},\qquad \lambda\ge0.\] The inner variance term reduces exactly to \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}}\operatorname{Var}_P(x^\top R)=\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}x^\top\Sigma x,\] whenever each \(\Sigma\in\mathcal S\) is attainable with mean \(\mu_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covariance-robust mean-variance optimization replaces portfolio variance by the largest covariance quadratic form over the admissible covariance set.
knowledge_statements.title: Covariance-Based Portfolio DRO

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covariance-quadratic representation fits the leaf and includes the necessary joint attainability condition, but no source is cited.

children.title: Joint Moment–Covariance Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Portfolio ambiguity sets coupling return moments with covariance information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Realizability criterion for returns supported on all Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On support \mathbb R^d, every (\mu,\Sigma)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_+^d is realizable by a finite-second-moment law, for example the possibly degenerate Gaussian \mathcal N(\mu,\Sigma). Thus without support or shape restrictions, positive semidefiniteness is the only restriction on a prescribed mean-covariance pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With unrestricted Euclidean support, every mean and positive-semidefinite covariance pair is realizable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists P:\mathbb E_P[R]=\mu,\quad\operatorname{Cov}_P(R)=\Sigma.
review_flags: Additional support or shape restrictions can destroy realizability.
knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained-Support Realizability of Moment Pairs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of the worst case when the admissible moment-pair set is Cartesian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \mathcal U=M\times\mathcal S and every pair is jointly realizable, then for \lambda\ge0, \sup_{(\mu,\Sigma)\in\mathcal U}\{-x^\top\mu+\lambda x^\top\Sigma x\}=\sup_{\mu\in M}(-x^\top\mu)+\lambda\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}x^\top\Sigma x. For coupled \mathcal U\subseteq M\times\mathcal S, the separated expression is an upper bound and can be strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent mean and covariance ambiguity separates into two support problems; replacing a coupled set by its Cartesian projections may be conservative.
assumptions_latex: For equality, \mathcal U=M\times\mathcal S and all pairs are jointly realizable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{(\mu,\Sigma)\in M\times\mathcal S}[-x^\top\mu+\lambda x^\top\Sigma x]=\sigma_M(-x)+\lambda\sigma_{\mathcal S}(xx^\top).
knowledge_statements.title: Separable Product Moment–Covariance Ambiguity

assumptions_latex: The admissible mean-covariance pairs form a nonempty realizable set.
Return laws have finite second moments.
Portfolio weights lie in a specified feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For mean-variance loss, distributional ambiguity reduces to optimization over the realizable pair set \(\mathcal U\).

notation.meaning: Mean and covariance of returns under P

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a quadratic mean-variance criterion depends only on the first two moments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint first-and-second-moment ambiguity for single-period portfolios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_+^d\) be a nonempty set whose elements are realizable mean-covariance pairs, and define \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal U}=\{P:(\mathbb E_P[R],\operatorname{Cov}_P(R))\in\mathcal U\}\). For \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(\lambda\ge0\), the worst-case mean-variance criterion satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal U}}\left\{-x^\top\mathbb E_P[R]+\lambda\operatorname{Var}_P(x^\top R)\right\}=\sup_{(\mu,\Sigma)\in\mathcal U}\left\{-x^\top\mu+\lambda x^\top\Sigma x\right\}.\] Thus joint moment-covariance DRO is an optimization over feasible portfolios and realizable moment pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst-case mean-variance portfolio with joint ambiguity can be reduced from distributions to optimization over the admissible mean-covariance pairs.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Moment–Covariance Ambiguity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The first-two-moment representation fits the joint ambiguity leaf and is plausible for the displayed mean-variance criterion, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Covariance Misspecification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Portfolio regimes where covariance uncertainty dominates moment-based protection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular Covariance Is Not Itself Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample separating positive semidefiniteness from positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R=(Z,Z) with \operatorname{Var}(Z)=1. Then \operatorname{Cov}(R)=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\succeq0 is singular but valid. Thus covariance realizability requires positive semidefiniteness, not positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly collinear returns give a valid singular covariance matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Sigma\succeq0\text{ may be singular and still be a realizable covariance.}
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Covariance Is Not Itself Misspecification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covariance-Only Ambiguity Does Not Control Mean Return
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite expected-loss boundary when covariance is restricted but mean return is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix x\ne0 and \Sigma\succeq0. If the ambiguity set contains laws with covariance \Sigma and means \mu_t=-tx for every t>0, then \sup_P\mathbb E_P[-x^\top R]\ge\sup_{t>0}t\|x\|_2^2=+\infty. Hence covariance restrictions alone do not make expected-loss or mean-variance objectives finite unless the mean is fixed, bounded, or coupled to covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded covariance does not bound expected return; unrestricted adverse means make the robust objective infinite.
assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set permits arbitrarily adverse means while retaining an admissible covariance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_P\mathbb E_P[-x^\top R]=+\infty.

notation.meaning: Family of increasingly adverse mean-return vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Covariance-Only Ambiguity Does Not Control Mean Return

assumptions_latex: The portfolio contains a nonzero exposure.
The objective assigns a strictly positive weight to worst-case variance.
Covariance ambiguity is unbounded in the portfolio direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}x^\top\Sigma x=+\infty\), then the robust variance penalty and mean-variance objective are infinite at \(x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unbounded covariance in an exposed direction makes the worst-case quadratic variance infinite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-posedness from nonrealizable or directionally unbounded covariance sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A covariance ambiguity set must satisfy \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S_+^d\) and appropriate realizability conditions; otherwise it need not describe covariances of any probability laws. Moreover, let \(x\ne0\) and suppose \(\mathcal S\) contains \(\Sigma_k=kxx^\top\) for every integer \(k\ge1\). Then \[x^\top\Sigma_kx=k\lVert x\rVert_2^4\longrightarrow+\infty.\] Hence, for every \(\lambda>0\), \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal S}\lambda x^\top\Sigma x=+\infty\). A covariance-robust mean-variance model admitting such an exposure is therefore ill posed unless feasibility removes that exposure or the covariance set is bounded in all feasible portfolio directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-PSD matrices are not covariances, while covariance ambiguity unbounded along a feasible exposure makes its worst-case variance, and thus the robust objective, infinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Covariance Misspecification Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct knowledge kind, and the directional unboundedness calculation is internally consistent, but the realizability and ill-posedness claims have no cited source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Existence of Robust Mean–Risk Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-independent convexity and attainment conditions for the single-period formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F(x)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\{-\mathbb E_P[x^\top R]+\lambda\rho_P(-x^\top R)\}. If X is convex, \lambda\ge0, and x\mapsto\rho_P(-x^\top R) is convex for every P, then F is convex on X. If additionally X is nonempty and compact and F is proper and lower semicontinuous, then \arg\min_{x\in X}F(x)\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supremum of convex distribution-specific mean-risk criteria is convex; compactness and lower semicontinuity ensure attainment.
assumptions_latex: x\mapsto\rho_P(-x^\top R)\text{ is convex for every }P.
\text{For existence, }X\text{ is nonempty compact and }F\text{ is proper lower semicontinuous.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is convex, and under the additional assumptions it attains its minimum on }X.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Existence of Robust Mean–Risk Portfolios

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of robust mean-risk objectives under ambiguity-set inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \mathcal P_1\subseteq\mathcal P_2, define F_j(x)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_j}\{-\mathbb E_P[x^\top R]+\lambda\rho_P(-x^\top R)\} and v_j=\inf_{x\in X}F_j(x). Then F_1(x)\le F_2(x) for all x and v_1\le v_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging the ambiguity set cannot decrease the worst-case criterion or its minimum.
assumptions_latex: Both models use the same X, \lambda, and distribution-indexed risk functionals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_1\le F_2\text{ pointwise and }v_1\le v_2.

notation.meaning: Worst-case mean-risk objective for ambiguity set j.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguity-Set Monotonicity of Mean–Risk Value

assumptions_latex: The feasible portfolio set and distributional ambiguity set are nonempty.
Portfolio losses are measurable and the chosen risk functional is finite on admissible laws.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A distributionally robust mean-risk portfolio minimizes \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}[-\mathbb E_P[x^\top R]+\lambda\rho_P(-x^\top R)]\) over \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Risk functional evaluated under distribution P

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distributionally robust mean-risk models minimize the worst distribution-specific tradeoff between expected loss and risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic single-period formulation; the risk functional must be specified by the surrounding model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be the feasible portfolio set, let \(R\) be the random return vector, and let \(\mathcal P\) be a nonempty ambiguity set of its laws. Given distribution-indexed risk functionals \(\rho_P\) and \(\lambda\ge0\), a distributionally robust mean-risk portfolio is any solution of \[\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\left\{-\mathbb E_P[x^\top R]+\lambda\rho_P(-x^\top R)\right\}.\] The formulation is well defined only when both terms are finite for every relevant \((x,P)\); choices such as variance, semideviation, or conditional value-at-risk produce distinct model classes and must not be interchanged silently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributionally robust mean-risk portfolio minimizes the worst-case combination of expected portfolio loss and a specified distribution-dependent risk measure.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributionally Robust Mean–Risk Portfolios

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the mean-risk portfolio leaf and explicitly avoids conflating risk measures, but no source supports this particular distribution-indexed mean-risk convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nestedness of robust chance-feasible portfolio sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F(\mathcal P,\varepsilon)=\{x\in X:\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P(R^\top x<\tau)\le\varepsilon\}. If \mathcal P_1\subseteq\mathcal P_2, then F(\mathcal P_2,\varepsilon)\subseteq F(\mathcal P_1,\varepsilon). If 0<\varepsilon_1\le\varepsilon_2<1, then F(\mathcal P,\varepsilon_1)\subseteq F(\mathcal P,\varepsilon_2).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger ambiguity sets or stricter violation tolerances shrink the feasible portfolio set.
assumptions_latex: All compared models use the same target return and base portfolio set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(\mathcal P_2,\varepsilon)\subseteq F(\mathcal P_1,\varepsilon),\quad F(\mathcal P,\varepsilon_1)\subseteq F(\mathcal P,\varepsilon_2).
knowledge_statements.title: Reliability and Ambiguity Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Cantelli Reformulation under Known Moments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact return-floor chance test over all laws with specified mean and covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal P(\mu,\Sigma)=\{P:\mathbb E_P[R]=\mu,\operatorname{Cov}_P(R)=\Sigma\}, with \Sigma\succeq0 and a nonempty moment class. For 0<\varepsilon<1, \inf_{P\in\mathcal P(\mu,\Sigma)}P(R^\top x\ge\tau)\ge1-\varepsilon if and only if \mu^\top x-\tau\ge\sqrt{(1-\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}\sqrt{x^\top\Sigma x}. If x^\top\Sigma x=0, the condition is interpreted as \mu^\top x\ge\tau.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exact mean and covariance information, the worst-case return-floor chance constraint is an exact second-order-cone inequality.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P(\mu,\Sigma)\text{ contains all laws with the stated moments and is nonempty.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{P\in\mathcal P(\mu,\Sigma)}P(R^\top x\ge\tau)\ge1-\varepsilon\iff\mu^\top x-\tau\ge\sqrt{\frac{1-\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}}\|\Sigma^{1/2}x\|_2.
review_flags: Strict versus non-strict failure events must be retained consistently.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cantelli Reformulation under Known Moments
Distributionally Robust Portfolio Chance Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case return-floor chance constraint over a portfolio ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let portfolio weights be \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), uncertain asset returns be \(R\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\mathcal P\) be a nonempty ambiguity set of probability laws for \(R\). For a target return \(\tau\in\mathbb R\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), distributionally robust chance feasibility is the condition \[\inf_{Q\in\mathcal P}Q(R^\top x\ge \tau)\ge 1-\varepsilon.\] Equivalently, \[\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}Q(R^\top x<\tau)\le\varepsilon.\] A distributionally robust portfolio model restricts its decision to the set of \(x\in X\) satisfying this inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A portfolio is feasible when every return distribution in the ambiguity set assigns at most ε probability to missing the target return.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and encodes portfolio constraints.
\(\mathcal P\) is a nonempty set of probability laws on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ is feasible}\iff\inf_{Q\in\mathcal P}Q(R^\top x\ge\tau)\ge1-\varepsilon\).

source_refs.locator: 1.6 Properties of Probabilistic Constraints p. 46

source_witnesses.locator: 1.6 Properties of Probabilistic Constraints p. 46

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition and its complement formulation are mathematically correct and fit the leaf, but the cited section addresses probabilistic constraints without inspectable support for the worst-case ambiguity-set extension.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiperiod Portfolio DRO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon policy formulation with nonanticipativity and worst-case expected loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dates \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), let \(R_{t+1}\) be the next-period return vector and let \(\pi=(x_t)_{t=0}^{T-1}\) be a portfolio policy with each \(x_t\) measurable with respect to the information \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(R_1,\ldots,R_t)\). If \(\Pi\) denotes policies satisfying the prescribed self-financing and position constraints and \(L(\pi,R_{1:T})\) is terminal loss, a multiperiod distributionally robust portfolio problem has the representation \[\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_Q[L(\pi,R_{1:T})],\] where \(\mathcal P\) is an ambiguity set of joint path laws. Thus temporal dependence is governed by joint laws, while decisions cannot anticipate future returns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a nonanticipative, self-financing portfolio policy that minimizes terminal loss under the worst admissible joint distribution of returns.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a nonempty set of joint laws for \(R_{1:T}\).
\(L(\pi,\cdot)\) is measurable and integrable under every \(Q\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_Q[L(\pi,R_{1:T})]\).

source_refs.locator: 2.1.2 Robust optimization p. 35

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.2 Robust optimization p. 35

children.title: Newsvendor DRO
children.top_down_role: Distributionally robust single-period ordering models.

knowledge_statements.title: Newsvendor DRO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-period distributionally robust newsvendor with underage and overage losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\ge0\) be the order quantity and \(D\ge0\) random demand. With unit acquisition cost \(c\ge0\), underage penalty \(p\ge0\), overage penalty \(h\ge0\), and a nonempty ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) of demand laws, the distributionally robust newsvendor value is \[V=\inf_{q\ge0}\left\{cq+\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_Q\bigl[p(D-q)_+ + h(q-D)_+\bigr]\right\}.\] The supremum selects the admissible demand law producing the largest expected mismatch cost. If the infimum is attained, any element of the corresponding argmin set is a distributionally robust order quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one order quantity before demand is observed to minimize acquisition cost plus worst-case expected shortage and surplus cost; an optimal order quantity exists when the infimum is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a nonempty set of laws supported on \(\mathbb R_+\).
The displayed loss is integrable under every \(Q\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V=\inf_{q\ge0}\{cq+\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_Q[p(D-q)_++h(q-D)_+]\}\), and any \(q^\star\) in the argmin set is distributionally robust when that set is nonempty.

children.title: Inventory DRO
children.top_down_role: Distributionally robust inventory control across broader replenishment settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Inventory DRO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon inventory control under ambiguity about the joint demand law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Over periods \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(u_t\ge0\) be an order chosen from demand history, and let inventory satisfy \(I_t=I_{t-1}+u_t-D_t\). For ordering costs \(c_t\ge0\), holding costs \(h_t\ge0\), backlog costs \(b_t\ge0\), feasible nonanticipative policies \(\Pi\), and ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) of joint demand laws, inventory DRO is represented by \[\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_Q\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(c_tu_t+h_t(I_t)_+ + b_t(-I_t)_+\bigr)\right].\] Capacity, lead-time, and service restrictions may be included in \(\Pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select history-dependent replenishments that minimize worst-case expected ordering, holding, and backlog costs over admissible demand distributions.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb N\) is finite and \(I_0\in\mathbb R\) is given.
The total cost is integrable for every feasible policy and \(Q\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_Q[\sum_{t=1}^T(c_tu_t+h_t(I_t)_++b_t(-I_t)_+)]\).

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Stochastic optimization problems p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Stochastic optimization problems p. 3

children.title: Newsvendor-to-Inventory Extensions
children.top_down_role: Extensions from single-period ordering to repeated or networked inventory decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Newsvendor-to-Inventory Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding of newsvendor DRO into finite-horizon inventory DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The distributionally robust newsvendor is the one-period specialization of inventory DRO. Specifically, set \(T=1\), \(I_0=0\), \(u_1=q\), \(D_1=D\), \(c_1=c\), \(h_1=h\), and \(b_1=p\), and remove interperiod, capacity, and lead-time constraints. Then \(I_1=q-D\), and the inventory cost \(c_1u_1+h_1(I_1)_+ + b_1(-I_1)_+\) becomes \(cq+h(q-D)_+ + p(D-q)_+\). Consequently, with the same ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\), the finite-horizon inventory objective reduces exactly to the newsvendor objective. Multiperiod dynamics, lead times, capacities, and vector-valued inventories are extensions obtained by enlarging the state and policy sets while retaining the worst-case expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The newsvendor is the one-period inventory model when ordering, holding, and backlog costs are identified with acquisition, overage, and underage costs; additional dynamics and constraints yield inventory DRO extensions.
assumptions_latex: The inventory model permits \(T=1\), \(I_0=0\), and unrestricted nonnegative ordering.
The newsvendor and inventory formulations use the same demand ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\).
The one-period cost parameters satisfy \(c_1=c\), \(h_1=h\), and \(b_1=p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{\mathrm{inventory}}\big|_{T=1,I_0=0,u_1=q,c_1=c,b_1=p,h_1=h}=V_{\mathrm{newsvendor}}\).
